[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536
- canvas_ratio: {비율}

[1. PURPOSE]
Create a K-pop adjacent Gen Z kitsch collage poster for social media, using a photoreal base photo with playful hand-drawn overlays, sticker captions, and Instagram-card micro details.
Designed for Instagram self-promo, shop advertising, product showcases, lifestyle photo decoration, or a casual event/drop announcement.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- The original photo {원본 사진} stays photoreal and occupies the central 68–74% of the frame; let doodles, labels, and sticker tags overlap the photo corners like a handmade scrapbook page.
- Top header area takes about 16–20% of the canvas; place {메인 헤드라인} large, rounded, and immediately readable.
- Background should be {배경 톤}, with soft fabric grain, paper-cut edges, tiny tape pieces, sticker shadows, and a warm handmade zine atmosphere.
- Scatter {손그림 doodle 요소} around the subject and across the poster rhythmically, roughly 14–26 total elements, including a few elements touching the photo edge for a real collage feel.
- Add {말풍선·미니 라벨} as small callouts near objects, connected with thin arrows, squiggles, hearts, or short hand-drawn leader lines.
- Include an Instagram-style lower info strip: {인스타 핸들}, {짧은 캡션}, {해시태그}, small save/share/heart micro icons, and a tiny page-like indicator such as “01/03”.
- Add a date/location sticker using {날짜 라벨} and {위치 라벨}; make it look like a small removable label or receipt sticker.
- Add {CTA 문구} as a bright bubble button near the lower third, plus {스티커 가격표} if the image feels like a shop/product promo.
- Use {외곽선 프레임} as a thick comic-style border framing the full poster, with small corner doodles and imperfect hand-drawn wobble.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Header zone (top 18%): Place {메인 헤드라인} centered and large, with {헤드라인 폰트}; use outline, tiny drop shadow, and {그라디언트 컬러} fill.
2) Sub-header stickers: Add one or two small handwritten tags such as {날짜 라벨}, {위치 라벨}, or “NEW DROP” beside the headline, slightly tilted like pasted stickers.
3) Main photo zone (mid 55–60%): Keep {원본 사진} fully photoreal, with no illustration conversion; enhance it only with sticker-like overlays, tape corners, and hand-drawn accents on top.
4) Doodle layer: Distribute stars, clouds, lightning, pixel hearts, smiley faces, droplets, squiggles, cherries, bows, and colored dots from {손그림 doodle 요소}; do not hide key facial features, product labels, or important object details.
5) Label layer: Place {말풍선·미니 라벨} beside notable objects or mood points, using short pointer lines and a scrapbook note feel.
6) Social info layer: Along the bottom 12–15%, include {인스타 핸들}, {짧은 캡션}, {해시태그}, a tiny “♡  ↗  저장” row, and {CTA 문구}; align it like a playful Instagram promo card rather than a corporate ad.
7) Optional commerce sticker: If the base photo is a product, add {스티커 가격표} as a cute starburst or receipt-shaped label.
8) Frame treatment: Wrap the whole canvas with {외곽선 프레임} so it feels like a playful comic cutout, diary page, or zine poster.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use {헤드라인 폰트}; heavy weight, oversized header, slightly uneven handwritten curves, outer stroke, inner shine, and tiny sticker shadow for pop.
- Color palette: use the exact gradient from {그라디언트 컬러}, plus bright accent stickers in hot pink, mint, lilac, butter yellow, coral, sky blue, and cream.
- Border/shadow: thick comic outline with a slightly imperfect hand-drawn line, plus a subtle sticker shadow of 3px y-offset, 10px blur, about 18% opacity.
- Graphic texture: add believable paper grain, marker strokes, colored pencil edges, tape pieces, mini receipt stickers, gel-pen sparkles, and tiny registration misalignment for a handmade printed feel.
- Layout personality: keep elements lively and asymmetrical, with a few tilted labels, playful scale jumps, and overlapping stickers that feel manually placed.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: preserve the base image as if shot on a 50mm or 85mm lens at f/2.0 for crisp photoreal subject separation, while overlays remain flat graphic doodles.
- Lighting: keep the source photo’s existing lighting intact; if adding new overlay effects, match them to soft ambient daylight or studio softbox light without changing the original photo realism.
- Color grade: Y2K pop palette with candy pink, mint, lilac, and cream, slightly high-saturation and playful, like a modern Instagram scrapbook.
- Material realism: the photo should feel physically pasted into the design, with tiny tape corners, raised sticker shadows, marker-ink texture, and subtle paper/fabric background depth.

[6. MOOD]
Gen Z kitsch collage — a Y2K scrapbook-meets-Instagram promo aesthetic, like a playful magazine sticker spread, diary page, shop drop flyer, or handmade zine poster.

[7. CRITICAL]
- 반드시 정확한 한글로 렌더링할 수 있는 텍스트: “퍼퓸 파티”, “스위트 데이”, “베이비 무드”, “한정”, “오늘만”, “귀여움”, “맛있다”.
- 하단 정보 영역에는 {인스타 핸들}, {짧은 캡션}, {해시태그}, “♡  ↗  저장” 같은 마이크로 아이콘 텍스트가 보여야 한다.
- 날짜/위치 스티커에는 {날짜 라벨} 및 {위치 라벨}을 읽을 수 있게 넣고, 홍보형 이미지라면 {CTA 문구}와 {스티커 가격표}도 자연스럽게 포함한다.
- 원본 사진 {원본 사진}은 반드시 photoreal 상태를 유지하며 일러스트, 만화, 납작한 그림체로 변환하지 않는다.
- 손그림 doodle 요소는 사진 위에 얹힌 레이어처럼 보여야 하며, 얼굴·제품명·주요 오브젝트를 과하게 가리지 않는다.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites unless explicitly provided or requested

[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Create a vertical mobile-screen mockup of a Google Maps-style location and directions UI, designed to look like a real, information-rich map app screenshot for presentation, review, or concept mockup use.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main map view fills about 70% of the frame, with a detailed place info card anchored near the lower third and a route panel integrated into the map overlay.
- Center the scene on {장소·가게}, with the marker pin clearly visible and the surrounding streets, alleys, blocks, crosswalk hints, transit stops, parking icons, and road labels rendered like an authentic navigation interface.
- Background treatment: realistic digital map surface with layered roads, building footprints, pale terrain blocks, POI dots, subway/bus icons, small park and river/stream shapes if appropriate, and app-style interface panels.
- Keep the composition tight and smartphone-like, with readable labels, realistic screen density, status-bar details, and natural UI stacking.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top system area: include a smartphone status bar with time, signal, Wi‑Fi, and battery indicators, plus a search bar reading “{장소·가게}” with back arrow, voice/search icon, and profile dot.
2. Top map area: render a polished map interface in {지도 모드}, with streets, intersections, small blocks, route lines, neighborhood labels, transit-stop markers, parking/restaurant/cafe POI icons, and realistic traffic color accents arranged like a live navigation app.
3. Primary marker zone: place a prominent red location pin directly on {장소·가게}, with a tiny label bubble and nearby venue labels such as “카페”, “약국”, “버스정류장”, “공영주차장” placed naturally around the map.
4. Info card zone: show {추가 정보 카드} in a compact place card with clear hierarchy, app-like padding, rounded corners, rating row, review count, category, opening-hours snippet, address line, call/save/share micro icons, and a small thumbnail strip or photo preview area.
5. Directions overlay: if included, render {길찾기 경로 (선택)} as a blue route line with start and destination markers, turn arrows, ETA bubble, distance label, and a lower route summary such as “자동차 12분 · 4.8km” or “도보 9분 · 650m”, positioned naturally across the map.
6. Bottom app navigation: add a realistic bottom navigation row with small icons and Korean labels such as “탐색”, “저장됨”, “참여”, “업데이트”, plus a floating location button and map-layer button along the right edge.
7. UI fidelity pass: make {UI 톤} feel like an actual screen capture, with crisp edges, accurate map detail density, believable label hierarchy, and practical mobile interaction elements.
8. Aspect treatment: keep the composition fully vertical at {비율}, with the map and overlays scaled for smartphone readability.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for Korean UI text, medium to semibold weight, 18–28px for headers and 12–16px for metadata; tiny map labels may be 9–12px but still crisp.
- Color palette: Google Maps-style pale beige, soft gray, off-white cards, muted blue route line, red destination pin, green park blocks, yellow/orange traffic segments, warm neutral shadows; if the map mode leans Naver, introduce restrained green accents from {지도 모드}.
- Border/shadow: use subtle app-card shadows, about 0px x-offset, 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 12–16% opacity, with rounded 18–24px card corners.
- UI details: include believable microcopy like “영업 중”, “리뷰 128개”, “저장”, “공유”, “통화”, “길찾기”, “주변”, “혼잡도 보통”, while keeping the required placeholders as the dominant readable text.
- Map realism: vary road widths, include one or two major roads, several side streets, building blocks, pedestrian paths, transit icons, and POI labels at realistic density for a Korean urban neighborhood.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: front-facing screen mockup look, like a clean smartphone UI capture with flat orthographic framing rather than a photographic lens effect.
- Lighting: neutral studio-style screen presentation, even brightness across the UI, no dramatic highlights, no reflective glare.
- Color grade: crisp digital interface grade with beige-gray Google Maps tones or green Naver Maps tones, balanced contrast, clean whites, and controlled saturation.

[6. MOOD]
Practical app-demo mockup — credible everyday navigation UI with dense but readable map information, helpful place details, and real screenshot fidelity.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 다음 문구가 정확히 보여야 함: “{장소·가게}”, “{추가 정보 카드}”, “{길찾기 경로 (선택)}”.
- Add realistic Korean UI labels where appropriate, such as “길찾기”, “저장”, “공유”, “통화”, “영업 중”, “리뷰 128개”, “자동차 12분”, “도보 9분”, “공영주차장”, “버스정류장”.
- UI must read as a real map app screenshot, with legible road geometry, marker placement, POI density, route hierarchy, and authentic navigation-card structure.
- Keep all Korean characters crisp and correctly formed.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean wedding moodboard editorial, vertical collage poster for wedding planning inspiration.
Concept-driven visual board that combines style references, floral direction, table settings, props, schedule notes, venue cues, and color chips in a polished planner-meets-magazine layout.
The final image should feel like a real printed wedding planning board photographed or scanned from a premium studio sample sheet, with tactile paper, taped photo references, handwritten notes, and practical planning details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center composition: a 3-column collage grid with the main concept anchor occupying the upper 35% of the page, supporting reference tiles filling the middle 40%, and color swatches + planner memo cards grounding the lower 25%.
- Background treatment: warm ivory paper texture #F4F0E6 with faint recycled paper grain, subtle deckled-edge feel, soft vellum overlays, washi tape pieces, pencil guide marks, and tiny pinhole impressions.
- Framing direction: editorial wedding-planner sheet with slightly asymmetrical handmade collage feel; {레이아웃} guides the tile arrangement while keeping image tiles, labels, swatches, and notes clearly readable.
- Use {결혼 컨셉}, {컬러 팔레트}, {플로럴 디자인}, {소품}, {식기·테이블}, {무드 키워드}, {예식일}, {장소}, and {커플명} as semantic anchors for each visual block.
- Include small realistic printed details: planner file code, page indicator, venue/date label, florist memo, table checklist, budget note, and subtle decorative line drawings matching the wedding theme.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top hero band (upper 18%): large title area reading “결혼식 무드보드” with a smaller subtitle card showing “컨셉 · {결혼 컨셉}”. Add {커플명}, {예식일}, {장소}, and “담당 플래너 · {플래너명}” as compact planner metadata.
2. Main collage zone (middle 42%): arrange image tiles showing dress or venue cues, bouquet/floral close-ups, ceremony aisle texture, invitation paper, table styling, and prop styling in a balanced scrapbook grid with thin white photo edges and soft lifted shadows.
3. Floral focus tile: feature {플로럴 디자인} in a close-up botanical image with layered petals, greenery, ribbon tails, florist wire, and soft natural shadow, styled like an editorial flat-lay insert. Label it “플로럴” and add a tiny handwritten florist note.
4. Table styling tile: show {식기·테이블} with tactile detail — ceramic glaze, vintage glass reflections, linen folds, menu card edge, candle wax texture, natural centerpiece depth, and rustic wedding elegance. Label it “식기·테이블”.
5. Prop strip: place {소품} as small supporting visuals or cutout object photos, each framed like pasted reference snippets with tiny hand-drawn arrows, fabric tape, and Korean note tags such as “입구 장식”, “포토존”, “버진로드”. Label the strip “소품”.
6. Color palette area (lower 16%): display {컬러 팔레트} as 5–6 rectangular paint swatches with handwritten Korean labels, small HEX-style color chips, fabric/ribbon samples, and a label reading “컬러”.
7. Concept note area: include {결혼 컨셉} and {무드 키워드} as a handwritten callout card, making it the connecting thread across all collage pieces. Add “예산 메모 · {예산 메모}” as a practical planner note.
8. Footer planner band: include “레이아웃 · {레이아웃}”, “비율 · {비율}”, “페이지 · {페이지 표기}”, a tiny checklist row “꽃 / 테이블 / 소품 / 동선 / 촬영”, and a small studio-style contact placeholder “문의 · 플래닝 상담용 샘플”.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard SemiBold for main headings, Noto Sans KR Regular for labels, and a hand-drawn script style for annotations; title around 48–64px, labels around 18–24px, micro metadata around 12–16px.
- Color palette: use the provided {컬러 팔레트} as the primary scheme, with ivory paper #F4F0E6, muted taupe #B7A89A, soft charcoal #2E2A27, dusty rose #D9A7A0, sage #9EA98E, terracotta #B86F52, and gold accents #C8A96A.
- Border/shadow: thin white collage borders, soft drop shadows with 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity, subtle tape-like edges for pasted elements, and delicate gold pen lines around selected note cards.
- Decorative graphics: add tasteful botanical line art, tiny heart marks, numbered sticker dots, torn kraft labels, vellum tabs, and paperclip details that match a real wedding planning moodboard.
- Render the board as a finished premium planning poster, not a blank template; every visual tile should contain tangible wedding references, textures, and readable Korean labels.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial still-life look shot on a Canon EOS R5 with 50mm f/1.8 for detail crops and 35mm f/2.8 for the overall flat-lay composition.
- Lighting: soft overcast daylight from upper-left at 45°, gentle fill from the right, controlled specular highlights on glass, natural shadow falloff on paper, ribbon, linen, flowers, and ceramic surfaces.
- Color grade: muted cream, sage, blush, terracotta, and warm gold with slightly desaturated contrast, like a wedding editorial spread from Martha Stewart Weddings mixed with Kinfolk.
- Material realism: visible paper fibers, pressed flower veins, ribbon weave, linen wrinkles, translucent tape, pencil strokes, ink bleed on handwritten labels, and mild photo-print texture.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean wedding planner moodboard — a Kinfolk-meets-Martha Stewart Weddings editorial board with handcrafted scrapbook elegance, practical planning notes, romantic texture, and a warm personal studio feel.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 들어가야 하는 문구 — “결혼식 무드보드”, “컨셉”, “컬러”, “플로럴”, “소품”, “식기·테이블”, “레이아웃”, “비율”.
- Additional readable Korean text to include: “{커플명}”, “{예식일}”, “{장소}”, “담당 플래너 · {플래너명}”, “예산 메모 · {예산 메모}”, “페이지 · {페이지 표기}”.
- Layout invariant: collage must feel organized and readable, with clear separation between image tiles, swatches, planner metadata, checklist notes, and handwritten labels.
- All text should be cleanly legible Korean; no broken syllables, no random English fragments in labels unless part of a styled reference note.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or fake celebrity wedding references

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean vegan and healthy food magazine editorial photo, vertical cover-style composition for wellness, plant-based lifestyle, and recipe-feature use.
Premium real-food photography with natural ingredients, tactile surfaces, cover typography, issue metadata, feature blurbs, barcode area, and realistic print-magazine details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main dish cluster occupies the lower 62% of the frame, with {음식·식재료} arranged as the visual hero and secondary elements supporting a layered magazine cover layout.
- {구도} with deliberate asymmetry: the main plate or bowl sits slightly off-center while the upper third carries the magazine masthead, issue label, short feature lines, and small editorial credits.
- Background surface uses {배경·소품} on a matte, tactile setting such as pale oak, warm stone, washed linen, ceramic tile, parchment, cotton napkin, wooden spoon, glass cup, herb bundle, seed bowl, or recipe note with visible material texture.
- Include believable food-styling details: scattered sesame, quinoa, oat flakes, herb leaves, citrus wedges, olive oil sheen, sauce smear, crumbs, condensation on a glass, and handmade plate imperfections where suitable.
- Add a small barcode area near the lower-left or lower-right edge, a price/date line, a short spine-style vertical credit strip, and a compact cover-food credit that does not obscure the hero dish.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Hero food area: {음식·식재료} presented in a polished editorial arrangement, with crisp ingredient separation, visible freshness, natural irregularity, and a slightly elevated styling treatment.
2) Supporting surface styling: {배경·소품} placed naturally around the hero, including realistic crumbs, seeds, herb leaves, folded linen, a small bowl of dressing, handwritten recipe card, or cutlery to create a lived-in magazine shoot atmosphere.
3) Cover architecture: {구도} used to create a strong focal path from masthead to headline blurbs to the main dish; integrate magazine elements such as masthead, issue number, date label, price, barcode, feature callouts, photo credit, and small section markers.
4) Light behavior: {라이팅} should shape gentle highlights on glossy ingredients like avocado, tomato, citrus, olive oil, yogurt alternatives, or sauce while preserving soft shadow detail under the plate and props.
5) Capture look: {카메라·렌즈} with a high-end medium-format editorial clarity, shallow-to-moderate depth of field, and finely controlled texture rendering across grains, greens, linen weave, ceramic glaze, and matte paper.
6) Palette and finish: {컬러 톤} with a matte print-like finish, subtle contrast, and natural saturation so the image reads as premium wellness media.
7) Magazine copy system: {텍스트 (선택)} may appear as the main cover line near the top or upper-right, supported by short Korean feature blurbs, a date/issue label, and small credit text such as “푸드 스타일링: 김하루” and “사진: 이서윤”.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for Korean, medium to bold weight, masthead 72–96px equivalent, headline 34–46px equivalent, feature blurbs 20–28px equivalent, micro credits 10–14px equivalent; small English subcopy in Inter or Helvetica Neue at 16–22px equivalent.
- Color palette: use {컬러 톤} anchored by soft cream #F5F1E8, leaf green #7E9B6A, oat beige #D9CBB7, and coral accent #D98C76 where appropriate.
- Cover typography: add a realistic Korean magazine masthead such as “비건 라이프”, issue marker “VOL.247”, date label “2026년 5월호”, price “₩7,500”, and 2–3 short feature blurbs such as “제철 채소 한 접시”, “비건 소스 12가지”, “단백질 든든 샐러드”.
- Editorial details: include a small barcode box with black bars and tiny numbers, a compact credit line “커버 푸드: 그린볼 05”, a vertical spine-style line “PLANT-BASED WELLNESS MAGAZINE”, and a small page/section cue like “RECIPE SPECIAL”.
- Border/shadow: subtle soft drop shadow, 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 12–16% opacity; cover elements should feel printed on matte magazine stock, not floating like stickers.
- Paper/print feel: matte magazine stock texture, slightly muted ink density, gentle halftone-like print softness in typography, realistic crop edges.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: shot on Hasselblad X2D 100c or equivalent medium-format look, XCD 90mm f/2.5, ISO 100, f/4, precise food-detail rendering.
- Lighting: natural window light from upper-left at 45° with a soft fill from the opposite side, producing gentle shadow falloff and realistic ingredient texture.
- Color grade: natural editorial grade with green-beige-coral accents, slightly warm whites, controlled contrast, and a matte magazine finish.
- Surface realism: preserve pores in citrus, fibrous greens, grains, toasted seeds, sauce thickness, ceramic micro-scratches, linen weave, wood grain, and slight printing texture over the final cover.

[6. MOOD]
Kinfolk x Bon Appétit wellness spread feel — premium plant-based editorial with calm, modern, Scandinavian-influenced food styling, but with the full visual richness of a real Korean monthly magazine cover.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: “오늘의 건강한 한 끼” must appear exactly if {텍스트 (선택)} is included as the main cover line.
- Korean text accuracy: include intact Hangul for magazine details such as “비건 라이프”, “2026년 5월호”, “제철 채소 한 접시”, “비건 소스 12가지”, “단백질 든든 샐러드”, “푸드 스타일링: 김하루”, and “사진: 이서윤” when used.
- Korean text accuracy: any Korean food labels, headline text, date labels, or credits must render with intact Hangul, no broken syllables, no mojibake.
- Food anatomy/layout: ingredients must remain visually recognizable and appetizing without artificial deformation, excessive gloss, or CG-like smoothness.
- Composition invariant: keep the hero food as the dominant subject while integrating a believable magazine cover system with masthead, issue information, feature blurbs, barcode, and editorial credits.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean traditional market documentary photo, vertical editorial travel image.
Documentary street-market scene for travel magazine use, with realistic everyday activity, dense merchandise, handwritten signage, and tactile street-level visual texture.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main scene: a narrow Korean market alley photographed from a walking eye-level perspective, with {시장명} visible as the clear setting through an entrance sign, hanging banner, or shopfront signboard.
- Subject density: foreground shoppers, midground vendors, steam-filled food stalls, handwritten price tags, and background signboards layered to create a deep, crowded, believable market feel.
- Background treatment: weathered awnings, red and green vinyl canopies, hanging signs, exposed amber bulbs, plastic crates, stainless prep tables, tiled floors, drainage covers, old posters, tape marks, and worn surfaces with natural grime and patina.
- Framing direction: guide the eye forward along the alley so the viewer feels like they are walking through {시장명}; allow overlapping people, merchandise, and signage to fill the vertical frame naturally.
- Include everyday market micro-details: reusable shopping bags, black plastic produce bags, a vendor counting cash, paper cups, chopsticks, steam from pans, wet pavement reflections, delivery boxes, small price cards, and taped notices.
- Use {시장 모티프} as the dominant visual cue across stalls, carts, trays, menu boards, and storefront displays, while surrounding it with complementary items typically found in a Korean traditional market.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Foreground (bottom 20%): a few market-goers partially entering frame, such as an elderly shopper holding vegetables, a vendor’s gloved hands packing food, and a blurred shoulder or shopping bag near the lens; natural motion blur is acceptable when realistic.
- Left side stalls (35%): food vendors and displays related to {시장 모티프}, with steam, trays, metal bowls, cutting boards, tongs, oil sheen, handwritten menu boards, plastic-wrapped ingredients, and price tags visible in a documentary way.
- Right side stalls (35%): produce crates, snack counters, clothing racks, household goods, or dried-food bins depending on the market composition, with dense merchandising, taped labels, stacked baskets, and hanging scales.
- Center corridor (vertical path): a narrow walking lane leading deeper into {시장명}, with overlapping pedestrians, scooters or delivery carts parked at the edge if appropriate, hanging signs, and layered stall fronts creating strong perspective depth.
- Mid/background (upper 45%): older shop façades, signboards, awnings, electrical wires, ceiling beams, fluorescent tubes, pendant bulbs, ventilation ducts, and market arcade structure visible where appropriate, grounded in real Korean market architecture.
- Atmosphere layer: emphasize the active rhythm of {시간대·날씨}, including the sense of crowd movement, vendor chatter, food steam, damp air, and lived-in neighborhood street energy.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: visible signage should look like real Korean market lettering: printed vinyl banners, laminated menus, handwritten marker price tags, faded shop signs, and taped notices; keep Hangul legible, natural, and slightly worn.
- In-scene text examples to include naturally where relevant: “{시장명}”, “오늘만 세일”, “국산 배추 한 단 ₩3,000”, “따끈한 어묵 3개 ₩2,000”, “순대·튀김”, “카드 가능”, “현금 환영”, “직접 담근 반찬”.
- Color palette: use {컬러 톤} with faded amber, charcoal, red canopy accents, dull stainless steel, green produce tones, warm bulb highlights, and muted skin tones; keep saturation controlled and photographic.
- Edge treatment: let the frame crop naturally through people, bags, awnings, and stall edges, as in a candid street photograph; use natural shadowing from awnings and overhead bulbs with subtle contrast separation between stalls and people.
- Surface detail: preserve realistic paper-thin wrappers, oil sheen on pans, steam haze, reflective metal, condensation on plastic covers, damp tile reflections, rough awning fabric, worn cardboard boxes, and scuffed floor texture.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: shot on Fujifilm X-T5, 23mm f/2, ISO 400, f/4, documentary street photography framing with moderate depth of field.
- Lighting: natural daylight mixed with warm pendant shop lights and fluorescent tubes, lightly diffused by {시간대·날씨}, with gentle contrast, believable shadows under awnings, and realistic mixed color temperatures.
- Color grade: Portra-style film tonality with faded amber, charcoal, soft reds, muted greens, and restrained highlights; preserve authentic market color imbalance instead of overly clean correction.

[6. MOOD]
Candid documentary travel editorial — like a National Geographic street-market feature with a subtle Portra 400 film look, full of everyday human presence, food aroma, weathered surfaces, and neighborhood market warmth.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: all visible Korean signage must remain fully legible and natural; render Hangul cleanly in signs such as “{시장명}”, “오늘만 세일”, “국산 배추 한 단 ₩3,000”, “따끈한 어묵 3개 ₩2,000”, and “카드 가능”.
- The image must feel like a real Korean traditional market scene, with no staged commercial polish and no artificially arranged symmetry.
- Maintain realistic crowd scale, stall proportions, food handling details, and market clutter consistent with an operating neighborhood market.
- Keep {시장 모티프}, {시간대·날씨}, {구도·앵글}, {라이팅}, {컬러 톤}, and {카메라·렌즈} visually reflected in the final scene while preserving the Fujifilm X-T5 documentary feel.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean camping and car-camping lifestyle editorial photo, travel/outdoor magazine spread feel.
Wide horizontal scene designed for lifestyle social posts and outdoor editorial use, with realistic documentary framing, lived-in campsite details, and cinematic dusk ambience.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main scene: {장면} placed in a wide landscape frame, with the tent, campfire, and seating area forming the main visual cluster across the central-left and middle of the image, while the right side continues into natural mountain air, parked car-camping setup, and atmospheric landscape depth.
- Human figures: {인물} integrated naturally near the seating area, relaxed posture, not posing directly to camera, with casual interaction such as pouring coffee, turning skewers, checking a map, or wrapping a blanket around shoulders.
- Vehicle element: {차량} partially visible near the tent or behind the seating area, tailgate open or side door ajar, with blankets, storage boxes, and soft practical lights suggesting real Korean car-camping use.
- Background treatment: layered mountain silhouette, dim forest edge, small campsite path, distant ridge lights or faint valley glow, and a subtle sky gradient that supports {시간대} without overpowering the campsite.
- Props layout: {장비·소품} arranged in a believable lived-in rhythm, including cooking tools, cups, folded jackets, storage crates, a small cooler, lanterns, and firewood pieces around the fire zone.
- Korean local detail: {한국적 디테일} appears naturally as small signage, a campsite notice board, convenience-store drink packaging, a road map, or a handwritten memo, never as a graphic overlay.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Foreground (lower 20%): textured campsite ground with pine needles, small gravel, dry grass, boot marks, firewood chips, tent pegs, and a few naturally cropped gear edges to anchor the composition.
- Main focus zone (center-left to center): {장면} rendered with the tent as the dominant silhouette, campfire glow as the secondary focal point, and seated figures slightly offset for a candid lifestyle look.
- Car-camping zone (mid-right): {차량} and open tailgate or roof-box detail create a realistic travel narrative, with soft reflections from lanterns and dusk sky on the car body.
- Food and drink detail: {음식·음료} placed around the low table or chair arms, with light steam, enamel cups, foil packets, tongs, cutting board marks, and casual crumbs for natural realism.
- Atmosphere layer (upper 35%): {시간대} sky with subtle haze, faint stars or sunlit gradient depending on time, and soft separation between mountains, treeline, and sky.
- Accent details: {장비·소품} should include warm practical light sources, wood grain on chairs, fabric texture on the tent, realistic ember glow around the fire, and slight soot or heat shimmer near the flames.
- Color integration: apply {컬러 톤} across shadows and midtones while preserving natural flame warmth, believable skin tones, and outdoor contrast.
- Camera rendering: {카메라·렌즈} look should feel like a high-resolution documentary frame, with gentle depth separation, natural lens falloff, and tactile detail in fabric, wood, gravel, and smoke.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: no editorial title overlay; only incidental real-world Korean text may appear on campsite signs, small labels, packaging, maps, or handwritten notes.
- Color palette: {컬러 톤} with faded amber, sage green, charcoal gray, weathered beige, and a slight cyan lift in the deep shadows.
- Composition density: allow authentic camping clutter and functional outdoor objects so the image feels inhabited, spontaneous, and grounded rather than showroom-staged.
- Materials: emphasize canvas tent weave, scuffed plastic storage boxes, brushed metal mugs, matte car paint, worn chair fabric, rough firewood bark, smoke haze, and uneven natural ground.
- Environmental realism: include season-appropriate traces such as condensation on cups, cool evening breath, dew on grass, wind-softened tent fabric, or smoke drifting according to the scene.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Sony A7R V, 35mm f/1.4 GM, ISO 800, f/2, documentary-style wide environmental portrait framing.
- Lighting: {라이팅} with realistic firelight spill on faces, hands, tent fabric, cups, and props, plus balanced ambient fill from dusk sky or moonlight.
- Color grade: Portra 800-inspired warm amber highlights, muted sage mids, charcoal shadows, and restrained cyan in the sky.
- Texture rendering: detailed but natural grain, realistic smoke translucency, soft highlight bloom only from practical light sources, and believable low-light shadow detail.

[6. MOOD]
Outdoor travel editorial — feels like a Kinfolk x National Geographic Traveler crossover, calm and grounded with cinematic dusk realism, quiet conversation, cool mountain air, and the intimacy of a real Korean weekend camping trip.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: incidental Korean text, if visible, should be clean and readable, such as “강원 숲길 캠프”, “오늘의 자리”, “따뜻한 밤”, “분리수거”, “매점 200m”, or a small handwritten date label “2026.05.17”.
- Composition must feel like a real camping or car-camping trip in Korea, with believable scale, safe fire placement, natural smoke direction, practical gear use, and anatomically correct human figures.
- Include authentic lived-in details: half-used firewood bundle, thermos lid, local snack packaging, damp jacket over a chair, map corner under a cup, and lantern cords or hooks placed logically.
- The image should remain photographic and documentary, not a product advertisement, showroom camping setup, or fantasy campsite.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or recognizable public figures
- Distorted hands, unreadable faces, or impossible campsite physics

[1. PURPOSE]
Game streamer live-screen mockup for Twitch / CHZZK / SOOP, styled like a real 16:9 PC livestream capture with authentic streaming UI layers, active chat, live game HUD details, donation alerts, stream schedule micro-text, and platform-native broadcast chrome.
Designed as an i2i livestream interface composition using the attached person as the camera-captured streamer, preserving the original face and overall identity through {원본 보존}.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main webcam frame: the attached person {원본 보존} occupies the left or center-left 42–45% of the screen, framed like a live facecam crop with natural shoulders visible, a slightly cropped bottom edge, mild webcam compression, and monitor reflections on the face to mimic a real streaming layout.
- Game content area: the remaining 55–58% is a gameplay-like broadcast panel based on {게임 장르}, with believable in-game HUD elements such as a minimap block, team list, cooldown/status bars, score panel, inventory strip, health bar, objective marker, or match timer depending on the genre.
- Top and bottom overlays: streamer nickname, platform branding, live badge, viewer metrics, follower/sub goal, chat, pinned notice, donation alert, recent subscriber line, and tiny stream status labels are arranged as separate HUD layers with realistic nesting and alignment.
- Right-side chat stack: include a vertical translucent chat panel with multiple short Korean messages, colored username chips, emotes, timestamps, and one highlighted donation or subscription message connected to {채팅·알림}.
- Lower-third details: include a compact ticker such as “오늘의 미션: 치킨 3회 / 랭크 올리기”, “방송 시작 02:18:44”, “다음 게임 투표 진행 중”, plus a small audio/mic/status icon row like real streaming software.
- Background treatment: dark neutral broadcast UI canvas with subtle gradients, glass-like semi-transparent panels, thin separators, soft shadows, compression artifacts, tiny pixel UI noise, and layered OBS-style depth.
- Use {플랫폼}, {스트리머 닉네임}, {게임 장르}, {시청자·구독자}, {채팅·알림}, {UI 톤}, {비율} placeholders throughout the layout.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Facecam zone: place {원본 보존} as the streamer camera feed, cut cleanly within a rounded-rectangle or rectangular broadcast window, with realistic in-game lighting spill, slight webcam grain, mild H.264 compression blocks in shadows, and a small corner label reading “CAM 01 · LIVE”.
- Facecam overlay details: add a slim nameplate below or above the camera window with {스트리머 닉네임}, a red “LIVE” pill, platform marker for {플랫폼}, tiny mic/camera icons, and a current queue/status text such as “듀오 대기중” or “솔로 랭크”.
- Game HUD zone: build a large gameplay panel with a streamer overlay shell, including genre-appropriate HUD fragments for {게임 장르}: scoreboard-like team rows, minimap-style blocks, mission markers, weapon/item slots, kill feed snippets, party list, match timer, or resource counters. It should read as an actual live broadcast screenshot rather than a generic placeholder.
- Header area: set {스트리머 닉네임} prominently in the top bar or lower-third header, using compact streamer branding treatment with icon-sized platform markers, a small “ON AIR” indicator, a bitrate/FHD label such as “1080p60”, and tight baseline alignment.
- Metric cluster: display {시청자·구독자} in a small stat block near the top-right or under the nickname, using tabular spacing, subtle separators, and micro labels like “동시 시청자”, “구독자”, “즐겨찾기”, “팔로우 목표 78%”.
- Chat / alert layer: render {채팅·알림} as a translucent right-side or bottom overlay, with colored message chips, small emote squares, Korean usernames, timestamps, and a donation banner that feels native to stream software. Include a yellow alert banner reading “☆팬님이 1만원 후원!” and a few chat lines such as “ㅋㅋㅋㅋ”, “와 방금 샷 미쳤다”, “오늘 감도 몇이에요?”, “나이스 치킨각”.
- Platform identity: adapt accent colors and chrome to {UI 톤}, keeping the interface instantly recognizable for Twitch / CHZZK / SOOP while allowing real platform-style badges, icons, and logo-like UI markers.
- Broadcast software realism: include tiny OBS-like edge details such as scene labels “GAME”, “CAM”, “CHAT”, an audio level meter with green/yellow bars, recent event list “최근 구독: 별빛님”, and a small status line “Dropped frames 0.2% · 60fps” tucked into the lower UI.
- Aspect treatment: maintain {비율} with safe zones for all text, icons, facecam, game HUD, and chat so the final frame reads like a genuine streaming OBS-style screen capture.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard SemiBold for primary labels, Noto Sans KR Medium for metrics, and Pretendard Regular for chat; title size ~26–34 px, metrics ~18–22 px, chat ~14–16 px, micro UI text ~10–12 px, with crisp vector-like rendering.
- Korean UI copy should feel like actual streamer interface text: short, conversational, and compact, including labels such as “실시간 채팅”, “후원 알림”, “오늘의 미션”, “최근 구독”, “방송 시작”, “시청자 참여”, “랭크전”, and “다음 판 대기”.
- Color palette: use the platform-specific palette from {UI 톤}, anchored by deep black #0B0B0F, off-black #121218, neutral gray #2A2F3A, soft white #EDEFF5, and one vivid accent color (purple / green / red) depending on platform.
- Border/shadow: use thin 1px separators, 8–12 px panel radius, and soft drop shadows with 0px x-offset, 6px y-offset, 18px blur, 18% opacity for layered broadcast depth.
- UI finish: keep glyph edges sharp, spacing consistent, overlay opacity between 75% and 90%, and small interface artifacts such as slight aliasing, compression, notification badges, hover-like highlights, and chat scroll softness so the interface feels screen-captured rather than poster-designed.
- Visual density: the screen should contain enough real livestream information to feel active and lived-in: game panel, facecam, chat, alerts, metrics, ticker, small icons, and micro labels, while keeping the streamer and main gameplay panel readable.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: realistic front-facing webcam look, equivalent to a 35mm lens at f/2.8 for the facecam region, with slight perspective compression and natural framing.
- Lighting: monitor glow from lower front, soft room ambient from upper-left, and subtle fill from the right to preserve skin detail and create believable streamer-room contrast.
- Facecam realism: skin texture, hair edges, clothing folds, and webcam noise should look like a real live camera feed; include slight color temperature mismatch between the facecam and the game capture as often seen in actual streams.
- Game capture realism: simulate a real-time PC game feed with crisp HUD text, motion-safe sharpness, faint compression in dark areas, and subtle UI glow matched to {게임 장르}.
- Color grade: cool desktop broadcast grade with black-neutral base, slight magenta/green platform tint depending on {UI 톤}, modest saturation, and realistic digital contrast so the screenshot feels live and current.

[6. MOOD]
Authentic esports livestream capture — a polished but lived-in OBS-style late-night Twitch / CHZZK / SOOP stream with active viewers, chat energy, real broadcast overlays, and a believable gamer-room camera feed.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문자열: “혜민의 게임방”, “동시 시청자 2,847 / 구독자 12K / 즐겨찾기 8.4K”, “실시간 채팅 빠르게 / 후원 알림 \"☆팬님이 1만원 후원!\" 노란 배너”, “치지직 (CHZZK 네이버) / 또는 Twitch / SOOP — 자유”, “배틀그라운드 / 리그오브레전드 / 발로란트 / 마인크래프트 / 이세계아이돌”, “16:9 PC 라이브 화면”.
- Additional Korean livestream microcopy may include: “오늘의 미션: 치킨 3회”, “최근 구독: 별빛님”, “방송 시작 02:18:44”, “나이스 샷!”, “감도 설정 공유해주세요”, “다음 판 같이 해요?”, “팔로우 목표 78%”, “1080p60 LIVE”.
- The streamer face must look like a real camera feed from a live broadcast, with preserved identity from {원본 보존}, realistic webcam texture, natural skin detail, and no exaggerated retouching.
- All UI text should remain clean, legible, correctly layered, and separated into streaming panels as if captured from OBS, Twitch Studio, CHZZK live software, SOOP Studio, or similar broadcast software.

[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Photoreal concert ticket and VIP pass mockup for a fan-made event presentation, suitable for social sharing, portfolio display, or premium merchandise preview.
Vintage-luxury printed paper product mockup showing a realistic horizontal admission ticket and vertical VIP pass in one rich flat-lay composition, with believable production details such as barcode, QR code, perforations, serial numbering, venue information, fine print, and lanyard hardware.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: the ticket and VIP pass occupy about 70% of the frame, arranged diagonally with slight overlap so the horizontal ticket reads first and the vertical VIP pass supports it as a secondary collectible layer.
- Background: warm neutral tabletop in textured off-white handmade paper or matte stone surface, with visible paper grain, faint scuffs, soft shadows, and a few natural concert-stationery context elements such as a folded envelope edge, small paper confetti pieces, a satin lanyard strip, or a partial wristband tucked near the corners.
- Framing: use an editorial product-photo composition with readable printed zones; allow believable margins, layered shadows, and cropped peripheral accessories that make the scene feel physically staged.
- Printed information hierarchy: include primary event title, date, venue, seat class, admission gate, ticket price, barcode area, QR code block, serial number, order code, small sponsor/production credit line, fine-print rules, and a detachable stub section.
- Use {아티스트·이벤트}, {날짜·장소}, {좌석·등급}, {티켓 디자인}, {컬러 톤}, {레이아웃}, {추가 디테일} as the customizable content blocks in the printed layout.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Ticket body (primary layer): design a horizontal 3:1 ticket with perforation edges, rounded corners, subtle punch marks, tactile paper thickness, and a detachable right-side stub; place {아티스트·이벤트} as the main header, {날짜·장소} beneath it in smaller type, and {좌석·등급} in a highlighted label box near the right side.
- Ticket detail layout: add short Korean microcopy such as "ADMISSION TICKET", "LIVE IN SEOUL", "GATE 03", "입장권", "예매번호 0626-0615-HM", "가격 ₩132,000", "DOOR OPEN 18:00", and "본 티켓은 당일 1회 입장만 가능합니다" in tiny but crisp print; include a barcode strip on the detachable stub and a QR code in a separate lower zone.
- VIP pass body (secondary layer): render a vertical 1:2 pass with a lanyard-hole impression at the top, metal eyelet shadow, and a soft fabric lanyard partially visible; repeat the same event identity in a tighter stacked layout with {아티스트·이벤트} near the top, {날짜·장소} centered, and {좌석·등급} near the bottom.
- VIP pass detail layout: include realistic access labels such as "VIP PASS", "BACKSTAGE LOUNGE", "PHOTO ZONE", "STAFF CHECK", "입장 확인", "NO. VIP-0615-012", plus a small vertical barcode, access-level badge, and tiny terms printed at the bottom.
- Signature illustration zone: integrate a small hand-drawn signature-style emblem, minimal concert stage line drawing, or abstract waveform linked to {티켓 디자인}, placed near one corner with ink-like irregularity and authentic print bleed.
- Security/detail zone: add a QR code, barcode, serial number, tiny fine print, row/seat metadata, and {추가 디테일}; make the QR code sharply printed but physically believable, with slight paper texture interrupting perfect edges.
- Sponsor/credit area: include a small lower-band credit line such as "Presented by H Studio · Production Support: Seoul Live Crew · Design Credit: fan archive" and a tiny contact-style line like "문의 02-0000-0615" without implying any official certification.
- Color application: apply {컬러 톤} across paper, borders, labels, section tabs, stamps, access badges, and accent rules, ensuring the red accents are restrained and used for hierarchy cues such as stamps, separators, barcode labels, or small markers.
- Layout treatment: follow {레이아웃} while keeping a realistic product-photo composition; if both formats appear together, make the ticket dominate the lower-left or center area and the pass sit upper-right or behind it for depth, with overlapping paper shadows and slight rotation differences.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard SemiBold or Noto Sans KR Bold for the main title, Noto Sans KR Regular for metadata, and a condensed numeric style for serial numbers and barcode labels; main title around 28–40 px equivalent, supporting text 14–18 px equivalent, fine print around 6–9 px equivalent but still structurally visible.
- Korean printed text: combine bold event branding with small practical ticket details; set short labels in Korean such as "입장권", "좌석", "공연일시", "공연장", "유의사항", "입장 시 신분증 지참", and "분실 시 재발급 불가".
- Color palette: craft beige, deep charcoal, muted paper white, and restrained red accents from {컬러 톤}; use hex references such as #D8C3A5, #2E2A27, #F4EBDD, and #B23A3A as a realistic print palette.
- Border/shadow: add a soft natural shadow with 4px y-offset, 14px blur, and 18% opacity; use thin printed rules, decorative micro borders, perforation dots, slight edge wear, stamp-like marks, and subtle emboss-like separation rather than heavy digital outlines.
- Material realism: show lightly uneven ink density, paper fibers, tiny registration imperfections, rounded die-cut corners, faint crease lines, and very slight edge fraying to make the ticket and pass look physically printed.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: full-frame product photo look, shot on a Sony A7R IV or Canon EOS R5 with an 85mm f/1.8 lens, styled like a premium flat-lay print mockup.
- Lighting: soft window light from upper-left at about 45°, with a faint fill from lower-right; keep highlights gentle and paper fibers visible, avoiding harsh specular reflections.
- Depth and focus: realistic shallow product depth with the main ticket face crisp, the overlapped pass and surrounding props slightly softer but still identifiable; maintain legibility for all critical Korean text.
- Color grade: warm beige paper tones with charcoal contrast and muted red detail, similar to a Kinfolk-style editorial product photograph with slightly desaturated vintage print character.

[6. MOOD]
Premium fan merchandise editorial — a high-end stationery and concert memorabilia mockup feel, mixing Kinfolk magazine layout discipline, Aesop-inspired material restraint, and the excitement of a carefully saved first solo concert ticket.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문자열이 이미지에 정확히 보여야 함:
  - "HYEMIN"
  - "첫 단독 콘서트 \"Slow Days\""
  - "2026.06.15 (토) 19:00"
  - "잠실종합운동장 보조경기장"
  - "VIP A구역 1열 12번"
  - "입장 시 신분증 지참"
- Additional Korean ticket details should look natural and short, for example "입장권", "DOOR OPEN 18:00", "GATE 03", "가격 ₩132,000", "분실 시 재발급 불가", "예매번호 0626-0615-HM".
- Ticket authenticity cues: serial number, barcode, QR code, perforation marks, detachable stub, punch marks, fine print, and lanyard eyelet must look physically printed and aligned; text must remain crisp and legible, with no mirrored or distorted Korean characters.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness
- Misaligned or unreadable critical ticket information

[INPUT]

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean one-room interior before/after 4-cut grid, social-media-ready square post. Show a realistic lived-in 자취방 transformation with clear comparison across stages, like an Instagram interior makeover card that includes practical room details, small captions, and believable everyday objects.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Compose a 1024x1024 square post using {레이아웃}: a slim Instagram-style header at the top, a central 2x2 photo grid, and a compact footer caption bar.
- Center the 2x2 grid so each panel reads equally, with thin gutters between cells and a consistent camera angle across all four cuts.
- Keep the room layout stable across panels; only props, tidiness, lighting touches, textiles, and styling evolve from messy to complete according to {4컷 흐름}.
- Use {원본 보존} as the base room source, preserving the original room structure, window position, walls, floor, and major furniture placement.
- Background treatment: small Korean one-room studio, 5-pyeong feel, wood floor, off-white walls, real wall texture, cable traces, small storage solutions, delivery boxes, bedding wrinkles, fabric grain, and natural lived-in details matching {공간 컨셉}.
- Each panel must have a small label sticker at the top-left of each cell: BEFORE / 정리 / 꾸밈 / AFTER, styled like matte paper tape or a clean rounded tag.
- Add social-post context: top header text "@my_room_log · 자취방 비포애프터", small date/location label "2026.05.01 · 서울 원룸", bottom caption "5평 방, 오늘부터 집답게" plus tiny save/share/comment micro icons and hashtags "#자취인테리어 #비포애프터 #원룸꾸미기".
- Include small handwritten-style Korean micro notes inside or near panels, such as "입주 첫날", "바닥 확보", "조명 추가", "완성샷", placed like subtle annotation stickers without hiding the room.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Panel 1 — BEFORE: show the room immediately after moving in, with 택배 boxes, shopping bags, scattered clothes, tangled charging cables, uneven bedding, plastic storage bins, a half-open suitcase, and a slightly chaotic floor.
2) Panel 2 — 정리: clear most of the floor, align furniture edges, stack boxes neatly, fold textiles, group books and toiletries, add a laundry basket, and make the same room angle visibly easier to read.
3) Panel 3 — 꾸밈: add a small plant, warm table lamp, fabric curtain or sheer panel, small mirror or wall poster, tray with mug and notebook, cushion, rug edge, and a few curated daily-life props that introduce personality.
4) Panel 4 — AFTER: present the finished room as the hero frame, with cohesive bedding, tidy desk or side table, warm lamp glow, neatly managed cables, styled shelf, small plant, framed print, rug, and calm editorial interior-photo feel.
5) Across all panels, keep the same structural anchors in place so the before/after progression is immediately comparable: same window, bed orientation, wall corner, floor line, and main furniture footprint.
6) Make the transformation readable at a glance: clutter density decreases from left/top to right/bottom progression, while warmth, texture, organization, and styling increase.
7) Add realistic interior details: fabric weave on bedding, cardboard box seams, wood floor scratches, wall outlet, cable clips, small price-tag-like sticky note "예산 ₩73,000", and a tiny checklist sticker "수납 / 조명 / 러그".

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR, bold for labels at 18–24px equivalent, clean sans for header/footer captions, with tiny UI text kept plausible and legible.
- Color palette: faded beige, wood brown, sage green accents, warm white, muted gray; use the palette implied by {컬러 톤}.
- Border/shadow: thin light-gray separators, subtle soft shadow under each panel, soft matte sticker labels, realistic paper/card texture in the header and footer areas, no heavy outlines or glossy UI framing.
- Keep the image realistic and slightly editorial, with natural room textures, readable object edges, believable household clutter, and photo-based lighting.
- The post should feel like an actual Korean interior account upload, not a showroom render: include modest furniture, affordable storage, practical styling, and small signs of daily use.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: full-frame 35mm lens, eye-level interior snapshot, f/4 look for moderate depth of field and clear room detail.
- Lighting: all four panels under {시간대·라이팅}, natural side light from a window with soft diffused daylight direction kept consistent for comparison; Panel 3 and Panel 4 may include a warm lamp accent while retaining the same daylight base.
- Color grade: Portra-like faded beige and muted sage, gentle contrast, slightly lifted shadows, warm wood neutrality.
- Texture rendering: real cardboard, cotton bedding, woven rug, matte painted wall, plastic storage, ceramic mug, glass mirror reflection, and soft dust/floor wear should look photographic.

[1. PURPOSE]
Lo-fi BGM video cover for study and work, illustrated editorial YouTube thumbnail with a calm rainy-city atmosphere.
Designed as a familiar study-with-me / ambient beats cover that still feels like a real uploaded video thumbnail: readable title, channel identity, cozy desk narrative, and small clickable details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main scene: {장면 컨셉} as the central narrative, with the desk area occupying about 55% of the frame and the window/city area filling the remaining 45%.
- Subject placement: desk and listening zone slightly lower-left, with the laptop glow, coffee steam, and cat forming a warm focal triangle near the center.
- Background treatment: layered room interior with bookshelf edges, pinned notes, charging cable, rain-dotted window glass, neon reflections, and small signage outside for a lived-in rainy Tokyo night mood.
- YouTube thumbnail layout: integrate a bold title block for {메인 타이틀} in the upper-left to top-center area, supported by {서브타이틀}, a compact channel tag {채널 핸들}, and a view-bait pill reading {시청 유도 문구}.
- Add one soft accent graphic such as a rounded cyan-lilac speech bubble, small coffee emoji-style icon, or vinyl-disc sticker behind the title so the thumbnail feels clickable while staying cozy.
- Keep the desk, laptop, headphones, coffee, notebook, rain window, and cat readable at thumbnail scale, with natural small objects enhancing the scene rather than flattening it.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Foreground desk zone (bottom 35%): laptop, headphones, coffee cup, small cat, open notebook, pencil, sticky notes, book stack, and a loosely coiled cable arranged as a gentle diagonal from left to right; the laptop screen is the brightest practical object.
- Midground work zone (center 30%): matte wooden desk surface, warm desk lamp spill, playlist card on the laptop screen, subtle waveform graphic, tiny calendar note, and a paper tag showing {업로드 정보}.
- Window zone (upper-right 40%): rainy Tokyo night view with reflected neon signage, soft apartment lights, wet street color streaks, and a few legible tiny shop-sign shapes softened by glass and rain.
- Character/mascot treatment: if a seated figure is implied by {장면 컨셉}, keep it small and secondary to the room atmosphere, wearing headphones or a hoodie silhouette, matched to the classic lo-fi cover language.
- Text system: {메인 타이틀} appears largest, {서브타이틀} below it, {배지 문구} inside a small rounded badge, {채널 핸들} near the lower-left or beside a tiny avatar circle, and {시청 유도 문구} as a warm callout near the laptop glow.
- Style translation: {화풍} should appear as polished 2D illustration with soft cell-shaded edges, subtle gradient shadows, hand-drawn line clarity, and tactile paper grain.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard SemiBold for Korean and a clean sans serif for numerals, 42–64 px range for the main title, 22–30 px for the subtitle, and 16–20 px for channel/date microcopy, with slightly expanded letter spacing.
- Color palette: draw from {컬러 톤} plus deep navy #1B2333, soft cream #F4EBDD, muted teal #6C98A8, dim neon pink #D97A9A, and warm lamp amber #E0A85A as small accents.
- Border/shadow: soft drop shadow 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 18% opacity for text, stickers, laptop, and desk objects; edge highlights should feel hand-painted rather than glossy.
- Surface texture: lightly paper-like illustration grain, faint brush texture in the sky, raindrop trails on glass, matte tabletop reflections, soft fabric texture on the chair or hoodie, and gentle steam from the coffee.
- Thumbnail readability: emphasize large Korean title hierarchy, strong light-dark grouping around the desk, and recognizable silhouette shapes for cat, headphones, laptop, cup, and window.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 35mm equivalent, slightly elevated indoor perspective with a gentle wide-angle feel, as if framed for a YouTube thumbnail rather than a full illustration plate.
- Lighting: {시간대} ambient room light from the left window side, cool neon spill from the rainy city outside, and a small warm desk lamp fill from lower-left.
- Color grade: faded amber, cyan, and lilac with restrained contrast, soft blacks, slightly hazy highlights, and a calm editorial thumbnail finish.
- Aspect treatment: compose for {비율}, with important title and face/desk details visible even when cropped by platform previews.

[6. MOOD]
Classic lofi study stream cover — quiet-focus atmosphere, rainy Tokyo night, warm desk routine, coffee steam, gentle cat presence, and a clickable but soothing YouTube music thumbnail mood.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Exact rendered main title: {메인 타이틀}
- Exact rendered subtitle: {서브타이틀}
- Exact rendered channel handle: {채널 핸들}
- Exact rendered badge text: {배지 문구}
- Exact rendered view-bait text: {시청 유도 문구}

- Korean text must be sharp, correctly spelled, and readable at thumbnail size.
- Laptop, headphones, coffee, cat, rain window, and title block must all be immediately identifiable.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

- Hyper-real CGI sheen, plastic AI-smooth surfaces, or distorted anatomy

[INPUT]

[1. PURPOSE]
Create a realistic Korean newspaper front-page article mockup in a horizontal A3-like newspaper format, with the interview subject as the main feature and a classic Korean daily + New York Times editorial feel. The page should look like an actual printed A1 front page photographed or scanned on warm newsprint, with credible editorial details, dense Korean typography, captions, section markers, and production text.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Overall canvas: wide newspaper front page layout, top masthead and date/edition bar across the full width, large headline below, then a dominant main photo with multiple article columns surrounding it in a believable front-page hierarchy.
- Main subject placement: {인터뷰 사진} positioned as the primary visual anchor, occupying about 35–45% of the page area, aligned slightly left-of-center for a real front-page editorial composition.
- Background treatment: warm white newsprint surface with subtle paper grain, faint off-white undertone, natural ink absorption, fine gray rule lines, column guides, fold marks, and light print registration imperfections.
- Spacing and framing: realistic newspaper gutters, crop marks, thin dividers, column rhythm, crisp vertical alignment, and a dense but readable front-page information structure.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Masthead zone (top 12–15%): place {신문명·날짜} in a strong newspaper masthead style, black ink, centered or slightly left-aligned, with thin divider rules, compact date spacing, edition text such as "제1판", "종합 A1", "서울·수도권", and a small price label like "₩1,500".
- Utility details near masthead: add a small barcode box, issue number such as "VOL.247", weather snippet "오늘의 날씨 맑음 18°", and tiny publisher/credit text in Korean to make the page feel printed and authentic.
- Headline zone (next 14–18%): set {메인 헤드라인} in oversized bold serif or newspaper headline type, spanning multiple columns, with strong visual weight and tight editorial line breaks.
- Subhead zone: place {부제} directly under the headline in smaller serif or clean sans-serif text, with a short kicker label above or beside it such as "단독 인터뷰" or "사람과 시대".
- Main photo zone (mid-left or mid-center, 35–45%): place {인터뷰 사진} as the featured 1면 portrait, treated like a newspaper print photo with subtle halftone-like softness, realistic grayscale contrast, and clean rectangular cropping.
- Photo caption: under the main portrait, include a compact Korean caption such as "변화를 말하는 오늘의 인터뷰 주인공. 사진=편집부" plus a small photographer credit line.
- Body copy zone (lower half and/or right-side columns): fill {본문 컬럼} into 3–5 dense newspaper columns with justified Korean text, short paragraphs, drop cap or first-line emphasis, and at least one pull-quote block like "나다운 선택이 가장 좋은 답" if space allows.
- Additional front-page realism: add a secondary small article teaser box, a continuation note such as "관련 기사 A4면", page number "A1", fold/section marker, and small footer text with newspaper address/contact line.
- Layout coherence: {레이아웃} should read as a believable front-page editorial arrangement, with clear hierarchy from masthead to headline to photo to columns, while preserving the classic newspaper structure.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use a classic newspaper serif for headline such as Noto Serif KR or Nanum Myeongjo Bold, headline size very large, body in Pretendard or Noto Sans KR Regular at small newsprint size, with compact leading, narrow column width, and justified Korean spacing.
- Color palette: black #111111, paper white #F4F1EA, cool gray #B9BCC2, faint charcoal #4A4A4A; keep {컬러 톤} faithful to a restrained newspaper print palette with warm paper and matte ink.
- Ink and print detail: include subtle halftone dots in photos, slight ink spread on small characters, thin rules, understated gray boxes for metadata, and realistic newspaper edge shadow like a printed sheet laid flat.
- Editorial embellishments: use small section labels, caption lines, page indicators, barcode area, issue/date details, and column dividers as authentic newspaper elements rather than decorative poster graphics.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial portrait photographed on a full-frame camera with an 85mm f/1.8 lens for the main interview image, or a 70–200mm at around 135mm for a serious press-photo look.
- Lighting: soft diffused window light from upper-left at roughly 45°, with gentle shadow falloff and restrained contrast, similar to an NYT-style portrait shoot.
- Color grade: monochrome or near-monochrome newsprint grade, slightly warm paper tone, neutral blacks, low saturation, print-friendly contrast, and realistic matte paper texture.
- Rendering approach: make the page feel physically printed, with tangible paper fibers, faint center fold, slight edge curl, and authentic offset-print softness without losing legibility.

[6. MOOD]
Serious, authoritative, and content-rich newspaper editorial — The New York Times front-page feature meets a polished Korean daily press mockup, credible enough to feel like a real published interview issue.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문자열: {신문명·날짜}, {메인 헤드라인}, {부제}.
- Add believable Korean newspaper microcopy such as "단독 인터뷰", "종합 A1", "제1판", "관련 기사 A4면", "사진=편집부", "VOL.247", and "₩1,500" with clean typography.
- The main interview subject in {인터뷰 사진} must look like a real person portrait, not a stylized illustration, and the page must feel like a plausible front-page newspaper mockup.
- All body text in {본문 컬럼} must remain legible Korean with proper spacing and no broken characters.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[1. PURPOSE]
Turn the attached person into a game character select screen portrait and full UI mockup, with a polished but authentic in-game interface look. The final image should feel like a real character selection screen from a commercial fantasy RPG / fighting game / sci-fi / cyberpunk title, complete with playable-character UI layers, ranked-mode details, loadout panels, selectable slots, ability icons, and readable Korean interface text.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center the converted character portrait as the hero element, occupying about 55% of the frame height, framed by a high-end game UI character bay with layered metallic / glass panels.
- Keep {원본 보존} visible in face identity and overall likeness, while swapping clothing, props, armor, weapon styling, and scene into the selected {게임 장르} style.
- Add a top navigation/header bar with Korean game UI text such as "캐릭터 선택", "랭크전", "시즌 07", a small server/date label like "KR-01 · 2026.05.01", and a subtle build/version tag like "v3.8.12".
- Place the character info card on the lower-left or lower-center area, with the right side and upper-right area filled by stat bars, ability icons, rarity badges, and loadout buttons.
- Background treatment should match {배경 무대}: medieval castle / dragon cave, cyberpunk city, or fighting stage, with layered stage architecture, lighting sources, banners/screens, particles, and arena atmosphere that still supports UI readability.
- Use {캐릭터명·클래스·스탯}, {무기·장비}, {UI 디자인}, and {컬러 톤} as editable content anchors, integrated naturally into the interface.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Portrait area (main 55%): {원본 보존} preserved in facial structure, converted into a game character render with matching costume, weapon, class-specific stance, hair/detail styling, gloves/armor trims, and believable fabric/metal textures.
- Weapon / equipment layer: {무기·장비} placed in hand, across the back, or strapped on the body, sized to read clearly as a selectable character loadout item; include small item tags such as "주무기", "보조장비", "강화 +7".
- Top UI header: include a bold title area reading "캐릭터 선택" and secondary menu tabs such as "영웅", "스킨", "장비", "스킬", plus a small timer or matchmaking label like "선택 시간 28초".
- Info panel: {캐릭터명·클래스·스탯} displayed inside a crisp premium game card with visible hierarchy, including name, class, level badge, rarity frame, short lore line, and tiny ID text such as "ID: KR-HYM-0427".
- Stat section: horizontal bars for HP, attack, and defense, aligned cleanly and spaced evenly, with numeric labels, small icons, and secondary attributes like "속도 82", "치명 18%", "난이도 ★★★".
- Ability section: add 4–5 square skill icons with cooldown labels and Korean captions such as "강타", "돌진", "수호", "궁극기", using genre-matched icon art and hover-card style tooltips.
- Background stage: {배경 무대} rendered as a recognizable game arena backdrop with layered environment detail, interactive lighting, atmospheric depth, banners, monitors, stone arches, neon signs, or arena floor markings depending on the genre.
- Character carousel: add side thumbnails of other selectable heroes as dimmed cards with Korean placeholder names like "민준", "서아", "태오", lock icons on a few slots, and one highlighted slot for the main character.
- Selection controls: {UI 디자인} including a bold SELECT button, controller/key prompts like "A 선택", "B 뒤로", "Y 상세보기", character slots, party indicator "파티 1/4", and premium HUD accents placed as a believable playable menu.
- Bottom information strip: include ticket/currency/resource indicators such as "골드 12,450", "젬 380", "전투력 8,720", plus a small notice line like "오늘의 보너스 활성화".

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard Bold for the main name, Noto Sans KR Medium for class and stats, and a compact arcade-style sans for button labels; title size large, stat labels small and readable.
- Color palette: use {컬러 톤} with genre-specific accents such as gold and brown for fantasy, neon cyan and magenta for cyberpunk, or red and black for fighting-game energy; pair with dark neutral UI panels and luminous selection states.
- Border/shadow: sharp beveled UI frames with subtle outer glow, 2px inner stroke, and soft drop shadow at 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity.
- Interface texture: add light scanline / glass / metallic panel treatment depending on genre, with readable Korean labels, semi-transparent overlays, brushed metal edges, holographic highlights, and small micro-text details.
- UI density: the screen should feel like an actual playable game menu with layered panels, tabs, badges, stats, notifications, selection outlines, and controller prompts, not a single character poster.
- Korean text styling: render short Korean labels cleanly with proper spacing and punctuation; mix English only where typical for game UI such as "SELECT", "READY", "LOCKED", "Lv.".

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 85mm f/1.8 portrait look for the character face and upper body, combined with a game key art presentation rather than a real-world photograph.
- Lighting: studio-style key light from upper-left at 45°, controlled rim light from upper-right, balanced fill so the face remains clear inside the UI frame, and genre-matched environmental glow from the stage.
- Color grade: genre-matched game art grading — fantasy amber and steel, cyberpunk neon teal and violet, or fighting-game red and charcoal.
- Rendering quality: premium AAA game menu render with sharp facial identity, realistic armor/material response, readable UI panels, detailed background stage elements, and subtle animated-menu cues implied through glow streaks and particle accents.

[6. MOOD]
Premium AAA game character select screen — a polished Capcom / Square Enix / Blizzard-style interface with strong esports-menu clarity, cinematic character presence, believable menu functionality, and enough UI information to feel like a screenshot from a finished commercial game.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구가 정확히 보여야 함: "SELECT", "이름: HYEMIN", "클래스: 워리어", "HP 1200", "공격 95", "방어 70".
- Additional Korean UI text should be short and legible, such as "캐릭터 선택", "랭크전", "시즌 07", "선택 시간 28초", "강타", "돌진", "수호", "궁극기", "파티 1/4".
- Maintain the original face identity from the reference image.
- Character anatomy must remain natural and game-poster believable, with correct proportions and no extra limbs or distorted hands.
- UI layout must read as a real character select screen with clear hierarchy, not a poster or social media edit.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized celebrity likeness

- Title zone: magazine masthead at the top 12–15% of the page; set {잡지 종류} as the primary cover title with strong hierarchy, partially interacting with hair or shoulders if compositionally natural.
- Editorial cover text system: place {이슈·날짜} as a clear issue/date line near the masthead; place {부제·크레딧} as a refined subtitle/credit stack; add 2–3 short Korean feature blurbs around the left and right sides without covering the face.
- Real cover details: include a small issue number such as “VOL.247”, a date label such as “2026년 5월호”, a barcode/pricing block near the lower-left or lower-right, a small model-name credit line like “MODEL  오늘의 얼굴”, and tiny spine/credit text along one vertical edge.
- Background treatment: {배경 톤} with realistic editorial separation, subtle paper grain, studio backdrop depth, and print-ready tonal control.
- Spacing and framing: design the page like an actual newsstand fashion magazine, balancing masthead, face, shoulders, blurbs, barcode, and credits while keeping the portrait visually dominant.
- Use {원본 보존}, {잡지 종류}, {이슈·날짜}, {부제·크레딧}, {모델 톤}, {배경 톤}, {컬러 톤} as editable variables.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Hero portrait area (center 60–65%): transform the attached person into a magazine-cover model while preserving facial identity, bone structure, age appearance, and natural expression; elevate styling to editorial fashion level with polished posture, composed gaze, and refined body language.
2. Wardrobe and grooming layer: apply {모델 톤} with believable fabric detail, premium tailoring, layered accessories if appropriate, clean hair styling, and refined makeup that matches the selected magazine identity.
3. Masthead and top band: place {잡지 종류} as a large, authentic cover title across the top with strong magazine hierarchy; use classic high-fashion masthead scale and let it feel printed into the page rather than pasted on.
4. Issue and subtitle stack: render {이슈·날짜} clearly near the top area and set {부제·크레딧} in a smaller editorial credit style with thin spacing, crisp alignment, and a real cover-credit rhythm.
5. Feature headline blurbs: add 2–3 short Korean cover lines in supporting positions, for example “나다운 선택이 가장 좋은 답”, “지금 입고 싶은 실루엣”, “새로운 계절의 얼굴”; vary size and weight like real magazine teasers.
6. Cover metadata: include small realistic details such as “VOL.247”, “SPECIAL ISSUE”, “₩7,500”, “www.magazine.kr”, a compact barcode area, tiny photographer/stylist credits, and vertical spine text reading “FASHION · BEAUTY · CULTURE”.
7. Background and color system: build the cover around {배경 톤} and tint it using {컬러 톤}, ensuring the subject remains visually separated from the background through contrast, edge light, realistic shadows, and print-like tonal control.
8. Final cover polish: add subtle print realism such as faint paper texture, ink density variation, controlled contrast, page-edge toning, and premium magazine-cover finishing so the image feels like a real fashion editorial cover.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use high-fashion magazine typography such as Didot, Bodoni, or modern serif masthead styling for the title; use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for Korean supporting text; masthead large and bold, subtitle smaller with tight tracking, credits in 9–14 px equivalent.
- Korean cover text: render short, clean Korean lines accurately and naturally, such as “나다운 선택이 가장 좋은 답”, “지금 입고 싶은 실루엣”, “새로운 계절의 얼굴”, “서울에서 만난 오후”, and “스타일의 기준”.
- Color palette: follow {컬러 톤}; for Vogue-style use black #111111, ivory #F4F0E8, cool white #FFFFFF, and sharp contrast accents; for GQ-style use charcoal #1A1A1A, deep gold #B08D57, and warm neutral highlights; for Marie Claire-style use blush #E8C9D3, soft cream #FAF4EF, and muted rose accents.
- Cover furniture: include a believable barcode block, price/date text, issue number, model credit, small production credits, and a few editorial blurbs arranged with professional hierarchy.
- Border/shadow: subtle magazine print realism, slight edge vignette, soft subject shadow 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 12% opacity; avoid heavy drop shadows or sticker-like outlines.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial fashion photography look, shot on a Hasselblad X2D 100C with 80mm f/1.9 lens or Phase One IQ4 with 80–110mm prime, shallow depth separation but realistic facial detail.
- Lighting: studio softbox key light from upper-left at 45°, gentle fill from front-right, faint rim light separating hair and shoulders, clean specular control on skin and fabric.
- Color grade: print editorial grade with magazine-specific toning; Vogue-like high contrast monochrome-neutral polish, GQ-like deep black and gold warmth, Marie Claire-like pastel soft contrast.
- Print finish: realistic paper grain, slight ink texture, subtle halftone softness in large color fields, crisp typography edges, and believable magazine-cover density.

[6. MOOD]
Premium fashion editorial cover — Condé Nast print cover aesthetic with a refined runway-to-magazine transformation feel, like a top-tier seasonal issue photographed for Vogue or Harper's Bazaar and prepared for a real newsstand release.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following values must appear correctly if shown in the cover design: {잡지 종류}, {이슈·날짜}, {부제·크레딧}.
- Include realistic magazine-cover additions: issue number/date label, barcode/pricing area, 2–3 short Korean feature headline blurbs, tiny spine or credit text, and a model-name credit line.
- Identity preservation: keep the attached person recognizably the same person; do not change face identity, age appearance, or core facial proportions.
- Hair, hands, and clothing must remain anatomically and visually believable; avoid distorted fingers, warped jawlines, or unnatural facial smoothing.
- Cover layout must feel like a real magazine front page, with clear masthead, issue line, subtitle, feature blurbs, barcode, credits, and editorial hierarchy.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized celebrity likeness
- Overwritten face identity

[INPUT]
