- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
K-pop dance 4-panel sequence image for social sharing, capturing a single performer across four action beats with MV-style energy.
Square 2x2 choreography sequence card that feels like a polished K-pop music video still, ready for Instagram feed sharing with Korean captions, handle, hashtags, and small social UI details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Keep the attached photo subject as the same person throughout, preserving face identity, body proportions, hairstyle silhouette, and overall presence.
- Arrange the performer across a 2x2 grid, with each cell showing one distinct choreography beat from {안무 컨셉}; the movement should read like consecutive frames from one performance take.
- Use {원본 보존} as the identity constraint for all four frames, keeping facial recognition consistent even during jump, turn, and finish poses.
- Dress the performer in {의상}, styled with layered stage accessories such as headset mic, metallic belt detail, fingerless gloves, chain accents, or reflective fabric trim.
- Build the background from {배경}, with each panel sharing one cohesive MV set while adding realistic variations: LED wall glow, light haze, floor reflections, lens flare streaks, and color wash shifts.
- Add a social-post overlay system: top header with {계정명}, small location/date label {촬영 정보}, bottom caption band with {메인 타이틀}, {서브 캡션}, and {해시태그}.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Panel 1 (top-left): Intro stance — the performer is upright and centered, feet grounded, shoulders squared, preparing the move with a clean silhouette; add a small Korean label “01 INTRO”.
- Panel 2 (top-right): Highlight beat — a dynamic jump or turn lands with higher energy, stronger motion blur only in clothing edges, not the face; add a small Korean label “02 JUMP TURN”.
- Panel 3 (bottom-left): Hook move — the most recognizable point choreography is shown clearly, with sharp arm lines and a readable torso angle; add a small Korean label “03 HOOK”.
- Panel 4 (bottom-right): Finish pose — the performer freezes in a strong final pose, slightly angled toward camera for a confident ending frame; add a small Korean label “04 FINISH”.
- Maintain consistent framing scale across all four cells so the sequence feels editorial and intentionally timed.
- Follow {레이아웃}, using bold panel separation lines, numbered corner tabs, small arrow marks between beats, and a glossy dance-practice storyboard rhythm.
- Include realistic social details: tiny save/share/heart/comment micro icons, a page marker “1/4”, a small sticker tag {스티커 문구}, and a subtle timestamp line {업로드 시간}.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard SemiBold and Pretendard Black; main title 42–54px equivalent, captions 22–30px equivalent, panel labels 16–20px equivalent; all Korean text must be legible and properly spaced.
- Text placement: top header bar contains {계정명} and {촬영 정보}; bottom caption band contains {메인 타이틀}, {서브 캡션}, {해시태그}; micro UI icons sit along the lower right edge without covering the performer’s face or hands.
- Color palette: vivid K-pop stage colors from {컬러 톤}, with hot pink, cyan, gold, violet, and deep black accents; keep skin tones natural and not over-filtered.
- Border/shadow: thin glossy panel borders, 2–3px separation lines, soft drop shadow 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity for each cell; add reflective highlights and stage-floor shine for realism.
- Graphic accents: add diagonal neon slashes, small beat markers, waveform-like rhythm lines, sparkle particles, and translucent sticker shapes that enhance the dance-sequence energy.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 35mm full-frame look, f/2.8, fast shutter feel, crisp performance capture with slight concert-photo energy.
- Lighting: strong backlight plus colored stage lights from left and right, including hot pink, cyan, and gold washes; add controlled rim light to separate the performer from the background.
- Color grade: vivid neon performance grade with deep contrast, electric highlights, polished MV still treatment, glossy black levels, and realistic skin texture.
- Rendering detail: sharp eyes, stable facial identity, fabric movement, shoe contact shadows, subtle haze beams, LED reflections on the floor, and believable motion freeze in each choreography beat.

[6. MOOD]
High-energy K-pop music video storyboard — glossy concert still aesthetic with the punch of a major-label stage rehearsal photo, fan-post excitement, and shareable comeback-teaser energy.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: render the following Korean text exactly where used — “{메인 타이틀}”, “{서브 캡션}”, “{해시태그}”, “{촬영 정보}”, “{스티커 문구}”, “좋아요”, “댓글”, “공유”, “저장”.
- Preserve the same subject identity from the reference image in all four panels, including face shape, hairstyle silhouette, and body proportions.
- Keep all four panels as a true choreography sequence with clear progression from intro to highlight to hook to finish.
- Hands and limbs must remain anatomically correct, with natural finger counts, believable joints, stable feet, and clean dance poses.
- Korean captions, labels, handle, and micro UI text must be readable at 1024x1024 square output.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or implying the subject is a real idol unless provided as the reference
- Extra limbs, duplicated hands, warped fingers, or face identity drift

studio:prompts3:ours-351.content:
[INPUT]
- reference_image: {참고 이미지}
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536
- aspect_ratio: {비율}

[1. PURPOSE]
3D animated feature-film style portrait transformation from the reference photo, designed as a cinematic character-cut frame for social sharing.
Make the subject look like the protagonist of a modern animated movie still, while preserving identity and facial structure, with rich scene details that feel like a believable moment captured from a full-length animation film.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Subject placement: {포즈·자세} as the main focus, occupying about 55–65% of the frame, with the face slightly above center and the body angled for cinematic depth.
- Identity retention: {원본 보존} with clearly recognizable facial landmarks, natural proportions, and stable expression.
- Animation style direction: {애니 스타일 결}, applying expressive shape language, readable facial planes, and premium animated-feature rendering.
- Background treatment: {배경} rendered as a polished cinematic environment with layered architecture, atmospheric depth, practical lights, surface textures, and small lived-in details.
- Scene enrichment: include {장면 디테일} and {소품} around the subject so the frame feels like an actual movie scene rather than a plain portrait setup.
- Framing: portrait-oriented composition with strong hero emphasis, cinematic depth around the head and shoulders, and background details arranged to guide the eye back to the face.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Character conversion layer — Turn the reference photo into a modern 3D animated-film look while keeping the person’s likeness, expression, hairstyle silhouette, and core facial proportions intact.
2. Face and skin rendering — Apply smooth stylized skin shading, gentle gradient transitions, subtle subsurface scattering feel, clean facial planes, expressive eyes, and animated-film highlight design without photoreal pores.
3. Costume and material styling — Preserve the original outfit shape where possible, but reinterpret fabrics with {의상 디테일}, crisp folds, stitching, buttons, woven textures, leather or fabric sheen, and slightly exaggerated form readability.
4. Background build — Expand {배경} into a cinematic set with layered depth, controlled perspective, window glows, signs, foliage, pavement, props, posters, rails, curtains, lamps, or other scene-appropriate details that support the story moment.
5. Color and atmosphere — Push {컬러 톤} across the whole frame through subject shading, background glow, atmospheric particles, reflective surfaces, and accent highlights so the image feels like a unified film frame.
6. Pose energy — Use {포즈·자세} to create a lively movie-still attitude, with body language that feels intentional, expressive, and scene-ready.
7. Lighting pass — Apply {라이팅} with clear separation between key light, rim light, and fill, keeping the face readable and the edges sculpted.
8. Film-cut overlay option — Add subtle cinematic frame information such as a small scene label, tiny production-style corner mark, or subtitle-like caption using {영화컷 라벨} and {자막 문구}, integrated as part of the social-share movie-still design.
9. Final animation polish — Add stylized contour definition, controlled contrast, soft cinematic bloom, specular edge highlights, screen-space glow, and tidy render finishing so the result reads as a premium animated-feature screenshot.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: if text is included, use Pretendard Bold or Noto Sans KR Bold with cinematic title-card spacing; keep the Korean text crisp, correctly spelled, and naturally placed as a small film-cut overlay or subtitle plaque.
- Color palette: follow {컬러 톤}; additionally support with deep navy #0F172A, electric cyan #22D3EE, magenta #D946EF, warm gold #F5C542, and neutral shadow gray #2B2F36 as needed.
- Edge and shadow treatment: clean edge separation with soft contact shadow under the subject, 8px y-offset, 18px blur, 20% opacity; use stylized contours, rim glow, or painterly edge accents when they match {애니 스타일 결}.
- Environmental detail: allow scene-specific props, textures, reflections, fabric patterns, signage, foliage, dust motes, light streaks, and background characters or silhouettes only when they strengthen the cinematic story and do not steal focus from the subject.
- Character finish: slightly enlarged animated eyes only if identity remains recognizable; keep nose, mouth, jawline, hairline, and face shape faithful to the reference.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: full-frame cinematic portrait look, 85mm f/1.8 equivalent with shallow-to-moderate depth of field, character-focused framing, and gentle perspective compression.
- Lighting: strong rim light + colored accent light, with a key light from upper-left at about 45°, soft fill from front-right, and background glow separated from the subject.
- Color grade: vivid magenta-cyan-gold cinematic grade with controlled darks, bright highlight edges, and animated-feature contrast shaping.
- Render texture: high-end 3D animation still with soft skin gradients, painterly shader transitions, stylized material response, light bloom, ambient occlusion, and expressive halftone or cel-shaded accents where appropriate.

[6. MOOD]
Premium modern animated-feature film still — a polished Pixar / DreamWorks-style character frame with cinematic energy, blockbuster polish, and a believable story-world atmosphere.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: if on-image text appears, render exactly “{영화컷 라벨}” and “{자막 문구}” in complete, legible Korean with no broken Hangul.
- Preserve identity: the subject must still read as the same person from the reference image, with natural facial recognition and no character redesign that breaks likeness.
- Anatomy/layout invariants: eyes, nose, mouth, ears, hands, and body proportions must remain anatomically correct; no extra fingers or distorted limbs.
- Visual priority: 셀쉐이딩, 림라이트, 하프톤 텍스처, cinematic depth, expressive 3D character lighting, and rich scene-world detail must be the main visible cues of the transformation.
- Social-share readiness: the final image should feel like a vertical animated movie cut suitable for profile posts, reels covers, and character-introduction cards.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals, government marks, certification badges, or fabricated institutional emblems
- Broken Korean characters or unreadable Hangul in any on-image text
- Celebrity composites or replacing the subject with another real person’s face

[INPUT]
- reference_image: {참고 이미지}
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Create an i2i family multi-generation cut layout, showing the same family identity across 4 eras in a polished magazine-album presentation.
Square 2x2 grid format for a shareable family timeline card with editorial polish, realistic family-photo details, archival labels, captions, and a premium printed-album feel.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- The composition is a 2x2 or 4-panel series, with each cell occupying an equal square quadrant and a thin gutter between panels, following {레이아웃} and {비율}.
- Keep the family identity from {원본 보존} consistent across all panels, while clearly shifting age, styling, and era cues according to {4세대 흐름}.
- Use era-specific wardrobes and settings from {시대 의상·배경}, including believable household objects, street details, furniture, wall textures, framed photos, seasonal cues, and lived-in background elements that match each time period.
- Apply subtle era-to-era variation in {라이팅·컬러} so each panel feels distinct yet unified.
- Add editorial panel labels, small date/location captions, and archive-style micro text so the layout feels like a family magazine spread or carefully curated photo album.
- Include a slim top masthead strip or small cover-note area reading in Korean: “우리 가족 4세대 기록”, “VOL.004”, “2026.05 ARCHIVE”, and a tiny page indicator “PAGE 01/04”.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top-left panel: Show the youthful/earliest era from {4세대 흐름} with {시대 의상·배경} rendered as a nostalgic, period-accurate scene; keep the family’s identity recognizable and cohesive. Add a small label such as “1세대의 시작”, a date tag like “1980년대 봄”, and a short caption like “처음 함께한 집 앞에서”.
2. Top-right panel: Move to the next era in {4세대 흐름}, updating clothing, hair, and background details while maintaining the same family lineage and composition logic. Add era props such as family snapshots on a shelf, school bags, analog objects, apartment hallway details, or street signage when appropriate. Add label text such as “2세대의 시간” and a caption like “서로를 닮아가던 날”.
3. Bottom-left panel: Present the adult/current era from {4세대 흐름} with a photoreal family portrait feel, contemporary styling, realistic skin texture, natural clothing folds, and a familiar modern home, cafe, studio, park, or city background. Add label text such as “오늘의 우리” and a small location/date line like “서울 · 2026”.
4. Bottom-right panel: Depict the future/elder era from {4세대 흐름} with a refined, modernized setting and tasteful aging details, avoiding sci-fi exaggeration. Use gentle wrinkles, mature posture, refined wardrobe, warm family closeness, and a setting that feels realistically advanced yet personal. Add label text such as “이어지는 기억” and caption “함께 남긴 다음 장”.
5. Across all panels: Ensure the visual progression reads as one continuous family archive, with consistent framing, similar crop logic, clear age progression, and matching family resemblance in eyes, facial proportions, smile shape, posture, and relationship dynamics.
6. Layout finish: Use {레이아웃} as the structural template, with neat labels, small decorative archive stickers, thin tape-like corner markers, tiny handwritten-style Korean notes, and a small credit line such as “사진 기록 · 가족 아카이브” so the series feels like a premium family magazine feature.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Use Pretendard SemiBold or Noto Sans KR Bold for main labels, around 22–30 px depending on panel density, with clean Korean character rendering. Use smaller Noto Sans KR Regular micro text for captions, around 10–14 px.
- Korean text elements to render: “우리 가족 4세대 기록”, “VOL.004”, “2026.05 ARCHIVE”, “PAGE 01/04”, “1세대의 시작”, “2세대의 시간”, “오늘의 우리”, “이어지는 기억”, “사진 기록 · 가족 아카이브”.
- Color palette: Match {라이팅·컬러} using era-aware tones such as vintage beige, muted sepia, warm gray, modern neutral white, soft silver accents, faded paper cream, and gentle family-photo warmth; avoid oversaturated colors.
- Border/shadow: Thin off-white dividers with subtle soft drop shadow, 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity, to separate panels without heavy framing.
- Add realistic printed-paper details: faint paper grain, slight album-card texture, subtle edge wear, small caption boxes, and delicate divider marks while keeping the family portraits dominant.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Photoreal family portrait look using an 85mm f/1.8 for the modern panels and a 50mm f/2.0 documentary portrait feel for the era panels, with natural perspective and gentle compression.
- Lighting: Soft diffused key light from upper-left, slight fill from front-right, with era-specific adjustments—more textured and slightly flatter in older panels, cleaner and brighter in current/future panels.
- Color grade: Subtle family-archive grade with 90s vintage warmth, 2000s neutral film tones, current-day realistic color, and future-era cool modern refinement.
- Realism details: Preserve natural skin pores, hair strands, fabric texture, jewelry or watch details, eyeglass reflections when present, slight photo-print imperfections, and believable background depth for each era.

[6. MOOD]
Editorial family archive — like a premium Kinfolk family spread mixed with a refined photo-album timeline, warm domestic memory, realistic generational continuity, and intimate documentary portrait storytelling.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: panel labels and micro captions must render correctly in Korean without broken characters.
- Preserve the family’s identity from {원본 보존} across all 4 panels.
- Keep the same family members conceptually consistent across eras; only age, clothing, hairstyle, posture, environment, and setting should evolve.
- The image must clearly read as a 4-generation progression, not four unrelated families.
- Render short Korean text clearly: “우리 가족 4세대 기록”, “VOL.004”, “2026.05 ARCHIVE”, “1세대의 시작”, “2세대의 시간”, “오늘의 우리”, “이어지는 기억”.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized celebrity likeness

[1. PURPOSE]
운세 카드 편집 디자인, 세로형 소셜 카드, 첨부 인물 기반 개인화 결과물.
Korean astrology/zodiac/four pillars fortune card with premium mystic editorial styling for annual or monthly sharing, optimized as a 1024x1536 vertical Instagram/card-news style image.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- 전체 프레임: 세로 2:3 비율의 카드형 구성, 상단 18%는 타이틀·카테고리·발행 정보, 중앙 50%는 인물 및 운세 상징, 하단 32%는 운세 요약·행운 정보·소셜 카드 요소로 구성.
- 인물 배치: {원본 보존} 인물은 {레이아웃}에 맞춰 좌측 또는 중앙에 배치하고, 얼굴과 실루엣은 선명하게 유지하며 별자리 원·띠 동물·사주 오행 그래픽이 자연스럽게 감싸도록 한다.
- 배경 처리: {컬러 톤} 기반의 짙은 배경 위에 은은한 별무리, 점성술 원형선, 얇은 금박 링, 한지 결감, 미세한 구름 텍스처, 단청 패턴 조각을 레이어링한다.
- 텍스트 영역: 상단에는 {운세 유형}과 {운세 대상}을 명확히 보이게 두고, 그 아래에 {기간 라벨}, {발행일}, {카드 번호}를 작은 라벨처럼 배치한다. 하단에는 {운세 제목}, {한줄 요약}, {상세 코멘트}, {핵심 키워드}, {행운 정보}를 읽기 쉬운 카드뉴스 정보 블록으로 정렬한다.
- 소셜 카드 요소: 좌하단 또는 우하단에 {계정명}, {해시태그}, 저장/공유/댓글 형태의 작은 마이크로 아이콘, 페이지 인디케이터 “01/04”, 그리고 {CTA 문구}를 넣어 실제 공유용 운세 카드처럼 보이게 한다.
- 프레이밍: 얇은 금색 외곽 라인과 안쪽 장식 프레임, 모서리의 작은 별·구름·원형 문양, 하단 정보 박스의 반투명 패널을 사용해 프리미엄 점술 카드 느낌을 완성한다.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Header zone: 상단 중앙에 {운세 유형}을 굵은 제목으로 배치하고, 바로 아래에 {운세 대상}과 {기간 라벨}을 보조 문구로 넣는다. 우측 상단에는 {발행일}, 좌측 상단에는 {카드 번호}를 작은 캡슐 라벨로 표기한다.
2) Hero zone: 중앙의 {원본 보존} 인물은 깨끗하게 정돈된 사진 기반 컷아웃 또는 자연스러운 반신 포트레이트로 배치하고, 주변에 별자리 원, 띠 동물 아이콘, 사주 오행 기호를 얇은 금선과 반투명 광채로 둘러싼다.
3) Symbol zone: {시각 모티프}는 인물 뒤편 또는 우측 패널에 배치해 시선 흐름을 만들고, 민화풍 동물·점성술 차트·천간지지 기호·달의 위상 그래픽이 장식과 정보의 역할을 동시에 하도록 구성한다.
4) Result zone: 하단의 반투명 정보 패널에 {운세 제목}을 소제목으로 넣고, {한줄 요약}을 1줄 강조 문장으로 배치한다. 그 아래에 {상세 코멘트}를 2~3줄 설명문으로, {핵심 키워드}를 작은 골드 태그 3~4개로 정리한다.
5) Lucky info zone: 하단 끝에는 {행운 정보}를 “행운 컬러 / 행운 숫자 / 좋은 방향 / 주의할 날”처럼 작은 표 형식으로 넣고, {계정명}, {해시태그}, 저장·공유 마이크로 아이콘, {CTA 문구}를 함께 배치한다.
6) Frame details: 카드 가장자리에 1.5px 금색 라인, 안쪽에는 얇은 원형 점성술 눈금, 모서리에는 작은 별/구름/단청 꽃문양을 넣어 럭셔리한 운세 리포트 카드 느낌을 완성한다.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard SemiBold for titles, Pretendard Regular for body, Noto Sans KR for small labels; title 42–54px, subtitle 22–28px, body 18–24px, micro labels 13–16px. Korean text must be crisp, evenly kerned, and actually readable.
- Color palette: {컬러 톤}을 기준으로 딥 네이비 #0B1020, 골드 #C8A24A, 미스틱 퍼플 #5B3A86, 보조로 아이보리 #F5EEDB 또는 단청 적 #C93F2D, 청 #2E5B9A, 황 #D9A441을 사용한다.
- Border/shadow: 1.5px gold border, soft shadow 0 10px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.22), faint inner glow around symbols, subtle foil shimmer on gold lines, no heavy blur.
- Information design: 운세 본문은 실제 카드뉴스처럼 제목, 요약, 키워드, 행운 정보, 페이지 인디케이터가 구분되어야 하며, 장식 그래픽은 텍스트 가독성을 방해하지 않도록 투명도와 크기를 조절한다.
- Decorative realism: 금박 라인, 한지 질감, 별자리 눈금, 단청 패턴, 얇은 구름 무늬, 작은 아이콘을 자연스럽게 포함해 완성된 상업용 소셜 카드처럼 보이게 한다.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial portrait look with 85mm f/1.8 for the person, combined with a flat graphic overlay for symbols; if illustrated, use a clean high-resolution composite rather than painterly distortion.
- Lighting: soft window light from upper-left at 45° with a subtle rim from the right, controlled contrast, slight specular highlights on gold elements.
- Color grade: deep navy + antique gold + muted purple mystic grade, or dancheong red/blue/yellow with restrained saturation and elegant shadows.
- Texture: refined paper grain, subtle foil-stamped gold edges, translucent celestial overlays, faint ink-wash cloud texture, clean editorial finish suitable for mobile viewing.

[6. MOOD]
Premium fortune editorial — Vogue Korea x Korean temple ornament aesthetic, with a refined New Year fortune-card atmosphere. 신비롭지만 과장되지 않고, 실제 SNS에서 저장하고 공유할 만한 개인 맞춤 운세 리포트 카드 분위기.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문구: “{운세 유형}”, “{운세 대상}”, “{기간 라벨}”, “{발행일}”, “{카드 번호}”, “{운세 제목}”, “{한줄 요약}”, “{상세 코멘트}”, “{핵심 키워드}”, “{행운 정보}”, “{계정명}”, “{해시태그}”, “{CTA 문구}”.
- {원본 보존} 인물의 정체성과 얼굴 특징은 유지해야 하며, 인물 비율이 과도하게 변형되지 않도록 한다.
- 운세 카드 구성은 카드형 편집물로 읽혀야 하며, 타이틀·인물·심볼·요약·행운 정보·소셜 카드 요소의 계층이 분명해야 한다.
- 실제로 렌더링될 예시 문구는 “2026 신년 운세”, “양자리”, “VOL.247”, “2026.01.01”, “올해는 시작의 기운이 강합니다”, “행운 컬러: 골드”, “01/04”, “저장하고 다시 보기”처럼 자연스러운 한국어로 또렷하게 보이게 한다.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites unless explicitly requested
- Misleading legal, medical, or financial fortune claims

[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1536x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Photoreal device mockup for a personal brand, creator portfolio, online class page, or profile banner, showing a laptop or tablet with a custom screen insert that feels photographed in a real workspace.
Use for social profile headers, landing-page hero images, portfolio presentations, creator media kits, and personal branding visuals.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main device occupies 55–65% of the frame, angled slightly toward camera for clear screen visibility while keeping realistic perspective.
- Build a lived-in editorial desk scene around the device: oak or walnut desk surface, ceramic coffee cup, notebook with handwritten marks, slim pen, small plant, charging cable, phone, glasses, paper clips, and a few layered paper cards that support the personal-brand workspace mood.
- Background treatment: warm indoor workspace with tactile surfaces, soft shelves or wall art in shallow depth, realistic household details, and natural depth separation behind the screen.
- Keep the screen area as the visual focal point; place {디바이스} so the display is fully readable and not clipped.
- The screen content must be inserted with crisp perspective matching the device tilt, using {화면 컨텐츠}; if it contains a portrait, personal photo, portfolio page, or social profile design, make it look like it is actually displayed on glass.
- Add small real-world desk details that enhance scale and realism: a sticky note reading “오늘 업로드”, a notebook date label “2026.05.01”, a tiny tab sticker “PORTFOLIO”, and a small caption card near the device reading “작업 기록”.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Foreground hero area: {디바이스} on a desk, shown as a realistic product mockup with matte metal finish, accurate bezels, thin glass layer, hinge or tablet edge detail, keyboard/trackpad or stand structure when applicable.
- Screen insert layer: {화면 컨텐츠} centered within the device display, with correct edge alignment, slight perspective warp, native screen brightness, soft glass reflection, and readable UI or photo details.
- Screen context details: include believable browser/app chrome if appropriate, such as a slim top bar, small icons, thumbnail strip, profile badge, Korean UI labels like “프로필”, “작업물”, “문의하기”, and tiny metadata text such as “Last updated 2026.05”.
- Environment layer: {환경} arranged to frame the device naturally, with plant leaves, stationery, cable curves, fabric coaster, paper texture, and desk objects placed lower and to the sides so the screen remains visible.
- Lighting layer: {라이팅} rendered as believable indoor daylight, producing gentle contact shadow under the device, subtle edge highlights, screen-glass reflection, and soft dimensional shadows from nearby props.
- Color layer: apply {컬러 톤} across props, desk, background, stationery, and screen-adjacent details so the mockup feels cohesive and editorial, like a real photoshoot rather than a flat template.
- Format layer: {비율·구도} preserved for a 1536x1024 horizontal composition suitable for hero banners and social headers, with the device, props, and background distributed in a polished lifestyle layout.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: visible Korean text may appear on small desk notes, UI labels, portfolio tabs, and stickers; keep it modern, readable, and naturally integrated, using contemporary sans-serif styling on screen and casual handwritten styling on paper notes.
- Color palette: use warm beige, natural oak brown, soft cream, charcoal gray, muted sage accents, and any palette direction from {컬러 톤}; allow small accent colors from stationery, thumbnails, or the screen design.
- Border/shadow: soft realistic contact shadows and ambient occlusion; device shadow should feel physically grounded on the desk, with gentle edge falloff and plausible glass highlights.
- Surface finish: matte desk texture with visible paper grain or wood pores; device body should read as anodized aluminum with subtle bevels, fingerprints, and micro-scratches where light catches.
- Prop realism: coffee surface, ceramic glaze, notebook paper fibers, cable rubber, plant leaf veins, keyboard legends, trackpad edge, and tablet/laptop ports should have authentic material detail.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: full-frame 50mm lens at f/2.8 for a natural product-lifestyle perspective, or 35mm lens if a slightly wider desk scene is needed.
- Lighting: soft window light from upper-left at about 45°, with mild fill from right and a faint shadow falloff across the desk; realistic reflections on the device glass and metal edges.
- Color grade: warm cream + oak brown + charcoal device, with slightly lowered saturation, natural skin/photo tones if present in {화면 컨텐츠}, and clean editorial contrast.
- Rendering quality: photoreal commercial still life, accurate perspective, tactile materials, realistic exposure balance between screen brightness and ambient room light.

[6. MOOD]
Premium lifestyle tech mockup — editorial studio still with a Kinfolk x Aesop workspace aesthetic, personal creator desk atmosphere, calm productivity, and refined portfolio-brand presentation.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: preserve all Korean text inside {화면 컨텐츠} exactly; additional small Korean labels must be legible, for example “오늘 업로드”, “작업 기록”, “프로필”, “작업물”, “문의하기”, “PORTFOLIO”.
- Screen content must remain legible, proportionally scaled, and aligned to the device perspective with believable screen luminance and glass reflection.
- If {화면 컨텐츠} includes a personal photo or portrait, keep facial features natural, realistic, and undistorted; avoid waxy skin or mismatched reflections.
- Hands are optional; if any human element appears in the scene, screen content, or reflection, keep it anatomically correct and realistically lit.
- Device details must match {디바이스}; if it is a laptop, show believable keyboard/trackpad/hinge; if it is an iPad or tablet, show believable bezel, stand, pencil or case detail when appropriate.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness

studio:prompts3:ours-347.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536
- aspect_ratio: vertical {비율}

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean year-end recap and reflection card, editorial diary-style multi-category summary for books, movies, travel, food, and people.
Designed as a shareable vertical social post with a magazine-meets-personal-journal feel, like a photographed printed recap page from a personal archive.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center or slightly left-align the main title block in the upper 18% of the frame, with {결산 분야} as the headline and a compact subtitle beneath.
- Use a polished {레이아웃} structure that keeps each category clearly separated, with equal visual weight, editorial rhythm, and realistic printed-card density.
- Background should be a paper-like cream surface with subtle grain, faint warm shadows, tactile diary texture, and small real-world stationery details such as washi tape corners, page tabs, tiny sticker labels, pencil tick marks, and light paper overlap.
- Place {Top 5} as the primary content inside the grid cells, with category icons, ranking numbers, short handwritten-feel memo tags, small thumbnail-like photo blocks, and coral highlight strokes supporting each category.
- Add card-news details: slide number label “01/05”, page indicator dots, a small series tag “YEAR-END RECAP”, a date stamp “2026.12.31”, and a final CTA strip near the footer reading “저장해두고 내년에도 다시 보기”.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header area (top 18%): Set {결산 분야} in a bold Korean sans-serif title using {타이포}, centered or slightly left-aligned depending on the grid balance, with supporting lines such as “2026 연말 결산·회고 카드”, “나의 취향과 순간을 기록한 5가지 리스트”, and a tiny credit “recorded by @myyear.note”.
- Main grid area (middle 72%): Build {레이아웃} as either a 2x3 card grid or a 5-panel vertical stack, with one cell per category: 책, 영화, 여행, 음식, 사람.
- Each cell: Show a small category icon, the Top 1 item from {Top 5}, a one-line personal comment in compact legible type, a small ranking chip such as “TOP 1”, and a tiny metadata line such as “기억 점수 9.4”, “다시 보고 싶음”, or “올해의 장면”.
- Category visual cues: 책 includes a tiny book spine thumbnail and bookmark ribbon; 영화 includes a ticket stub or film frame; 여행 includes a mini map pin and route dash; 음식 includes a receipt-like price tag or plate doodle; 사람 includes a small profile badge or conversation quote bubble.
- Content logic: Keep the five categories visually parallel so the design reads as a full-year summary rather than a random collage, while allowing realistic notes, stamps, highlights, and clipped-paper layers to create a lived-in diary spread.
- Accent system: Use coral highlights to mark important words, dates, emotional cues, ranking numbers, underline strokes, sticker tabs, and page indicator dots without overpowering the calm editorial structure.
- Footer area (bottom 10%): Include a diary signature or year-end memo such as “올해도 잘 살아냈다”, a small page number “p.12”, the page indicator “● ○ ○ ○ ○”, and a CTA line “공유하기 · 저장하기 · 내년의 나에게 보내기”.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for the main title in bold 700–800 weight, with body text in 400–500 weight; allow a hand-drawn accent script only for tiny emphasis, not for core readability. Apply {타이포} consistently across headings, captions, ranking chips, and footer notes.
- Color palette: Use {컬러 톤} while preserving the core palette: cream beige #F4EBDD, charcoal #2E2A27, coral accent #E97B6A, muted warm gray #8C837A, optional soft paper white #FAF7F2.
- Border/shadow: Add thin 1px charcoal rules, rounded paper card borders, subtle divider lines, stamped labels, soft torn-paper edges, and gentle shadows with 4px y-offset, 10px blur, 12% opacity for lifted paper cards.
- Realistic print details: Include tiny registration-like dots, slight ink absorption, faint paper fiber, lightly imperfect sticker placement, realistic pen underline texture, and small clipped note pieces that feel photographed rather than vector-flat.
- Text hierarchy: Large title, medium category headers, readable Top 5 item text, then small captions and metadata. Keep the visible Korean text crisp enough to read at social-post scale.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Flat-lay editorial look, as if shot on a 50mm lens at f/5.6 with a slightly top-down perspective, crisp but not sterile.
- Lighting: Soft diffused window light from upper-left at 45°, with a faint bounce fill from lower-right and natural warm paper shadows around layered cards, tape, and stickers.
- Color grade: Warm cream + charcoal + coral, with restrained saturation and a lightly muted print-like finish.
- Material feel: Matte paper stock, tactile ink, gentle paper curl at corners, tiny tape translucency, and subtle desk-surface texture around the card edges.

[6. MOOD]
Feels like a Kinfolk-style year-end diary spread mixed with a modern Notion recap template and a Korean social card-news carousel, calm, thoughtful, personal, and content-rich.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문자열: “연말 결산·회고 카드”, “책”, “영화”, “여행”, “음식”, “사람”.
- All five categories must appear exactly once as category headers and remain clearly readable.
- If {Top 5} is rendered as visible text, preserve Korean punctuation, spacing, and quoted title formatting cleanly.
- Include realistic visible Korean microcopy such as “2026.12.31”, “01/05”, “YEAR-END RECAP”, “저장해두고 내년에도 다시 보기”, “올해의 장면”, and “올해도 잘 살아냈다”.
- The final card must read as a finished vertical social post in 1024x1536, not as an empty template.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean neighborhood alley documentary photo, vertical travel-editorial frame for social media or poster use.
Realistic street-level scene that feels like an understated magazine travel spread, grounded in everyday local life rather than a staged ad image.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main scene: {동네·시그니처} should define the alley identity, with the street lines naturally pulling the eye inward.
- Framing: {구도} with the camera placed at pedestrian height, keeping the alley width tight and the perspective slightly compressed.
- Subject balance: if {인물} is present, keep them small and secondary so the alley architecture remains the hero.
- Everyday layer: include {생활 소품} as believable neighborhood evidence, placed casually along storefront edges, steps, walls, and curb lines.
- Environmental text: integrate {간판·문구} as real shop signs, small menu boards, faded stickers, delivery labels, and wall notices within the scene.
- Background treatment: aged walls, shopfronts, signboards, utility lines, potted plants, window grilles, awnings, air-conditioner units, pavement patches, and small repairs should all feel real and slightly weathered.
- Seasonal detail: reflect {계절감} through light, plants, clothing silhouettes, and small street objects without making it feel like a tourist postcard.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Foreground (bottom 20%): textured pavement, curb edges, drainage cover, cracked stone or asphalt patches, a small fallen leaf cluster, and subtle street grime to anchor the frame.
- Midground (center 55%): {동네·시그니처} alley corridor with layered storefronts, house fronts, signs, rooflines, utility meters, doorbells, and narrow side entrances on both sides.
- Human scale layer: {인물} placed naturally along the path, small enough to support the sense of neighborhood scale rather than dominate the scene.
- Local commerce layer: show a few readable Korean details such as a café standing sign, handwritten opening hours, delivery box label, or small menu strip using {간판·문구}.
- Depth layer (upper third): distant alley continuation and softly receding buildings, overhead wires, roof edges, warm window reflections, and hazy late-day atmosphere.
- Light behavior: {시간대·날씨} should create long, soft shadows and gentle contrast across walls, pavement, plants, and shop glass.
- Color treatment: apply {컬러 톤} across concrete, wood, brick, fabric, signage, metal shutters, and plastic crates so the palette feels cohesive and film-like.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: all visible typography must be environmental Korean text physically printed or painted on signs, menus, stickers, posters, door labels, or shop windows; it should look photographed in perspective.
- Local realism: add small imperfect details such as taped notices, faded paint, scuffed steps, mismatched planters, worn door handles, scooter mirrors, folded umbrellas, and utility cables where they naturally belong.
- Color palette: use the tones implied by {컬러 톤}, supported by muted stone gray, worn wood brown, dusty cream, soft black, faded green plants, and sun-warmed metal.
- Texture rendering: preserve tactile surfaces — rough plaster, brick seams, tiled thresholds, translucent café curtains, scratched glass, paper notices, and uneven pavement.
- Shadow behavior: keep natural shadow falloff with subtle 8–12% contrast in recesses, especially under awnings, roof eaves, plant pots, and step edges.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Fujifilm X-T5, 35mm f/2 look, ISO 200, f/4, street-documentary framing with moderate depth of field.
- Lighting: late-afternoon golden hour from one side, slightly low sun angle, long shadows stretching across the alley with soft ambient fill from surrounding buildings.
- Color grade: faded warm amber with beige and charcoal, Portra 400-inspired film rendering, restrained saturation and gentle highlight rolloff.
- Image character: realistic handheld travel-editorial still, fine film grain, natural micro-contrast, sharp enough to read nearby Korean signs while letting distant details recede naturally.

[6. MOOD]
Understated Korean neighborhood travel editorial — quiet, lived-in, warm, and observational, like a real city-guide photo taken while walking through a familiar alley just before evening.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: visible signs and notices must render cleanly, using plausible text such as “골목다방”, “오늘의 커피 ₩4,500”, “연중무휴”, “택배 보관함”, “조용히 닫아주세요”, “익선길 12”.
- Keep the scene photorealistic: natural lens behavior, believable street scale, real material texture, and everyday Korean neighborhood clutter should be present.
- If {인물} is included, face detail must stay minimal and incidental, preserving the alley as the subject.
- Maintain the 1024x1536 vertical composition with a documentary street-photo feeling suitable for a Korean local travel editorial.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or recognizable public figures

[1. PURPOSE]
A realistic future baby simulation portrait-card for social-media sharing, showing a believable child derived from the parents’ facial features.
Create a premium Korean family-studio keepsake image that feels like an actual printed announcement card photographed in a studio: warm, emotional, tactile, and content-rich while keeping the child as the clear hero.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: the future child takes 55–65% of the frame, centered or slightly off-center depending on {레이아웃}, with clear facial visibility, natural eye contact, and an age-appropriate infant/toddler pose matching {자녀 나이}.
- Parent relation cue: show subtle parental resemblance through facial structure, eye shape, nose bridge, cheeks, smile lines, and hair texture; keep the result photorealistic rather than stylized.
- Background treatment: {배경} as a realistic Korean portrait-studio setting with soft seamless paper, light linen texture, a warm floor mat, or gentle nursery-style depth depending on the chosen background.
- Portrait-card details: include a tasteful lower caption area and small decorative tags/stickers around the photo, such as a tiny heart sticker, date label, location label, and soft baby milestone tag, integrated as real printed or overlay elements.
- Spacing and framing: maintain a balanced portrait layout with comfortable breathing room for the face, visible shoulders or seated baby posture, and realistic studio styling elements that support the keepsake-card feel.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Hero area (mid 60%): composite the future child as a high-end studio portrait, with natural skin texture, soft baby hair detail, believable eyelashes, gentle expression, and age-accurate facial fullness matching {자녀 나이}.
- Face synthesis area: blend facial cues from {부모 사진} into the child’s face in a believable way, preserving recognizable family resemblance without exaggeration or caricature.
- Outfit and age rendering: dress the child in simple but realistic baby/studio clothing appropriate to {성별}, such as a soft knit romper, cotton cardigan, muslin bib, tiny socks, or neutral-toned studio outfit with visible fabric weave and seams.
- Physical setting layer: add natural studio details like a textured linen blanket, round cushion, wooden milestone block, small plush toy partly out of focus, or folded muslin cloth, all secondary to the child and consistent with {배경}.
- Caption/card layer: add small Korean on-image elements: title text “우리의 미래 아기”, a date label “2026.05”, a location label “서울 스튜디오”, and a short caption “엄마 아빠를 닮은 작은 미소”. Use these as refined keepsake-card typography, not loud advertising.
- Decorative metadata layer: include subtle printed-card details such as “BABY PREVIEW CARD”, “No. 001”, “DREAM FAMILY SESSION”, a tiny page-like corner mark, and a small handwritten-style tag near the bottom edge.
- Lighting layer: apply {라이팅} with soft shadow definition under the chin, cheeks, and tiny hands, plus natural catchlights in the eyes and gentle falloff across the background.
- Color treatment: apply {컬러 톤} across skin, clothing, typography, props, and background so the image feels cohesive, premium, and studio-finished.
- Layout finish: follow {레이아웃} while maintaining a realistic portrait-card composition with the child as the emotional focal point and all text/props acting as supporting details.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use refined Korean editorial typography; main small title in Pretendard SemiBold 30–38px, supporting labels in Pretendard Medium 18–24px, handwritten accent tag in a soft script style. Keep all text sharp, correctly spelled, and naturally printed on the card/photo layout.
- Color palette: warm cream #F5EFE6, ivory #FFF9F1, blush pink #F3D3D6, soft baby blue #D7E6F7, light beige #D8C9B8.
- Card finish: soft drop shadow with 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 12% opacity; add realistic paper grain, gentle rounded-card edge, subtle sticker sheen, and soft photographic depth.
- Styling details: allow realistic studio textures such as muslin, knit cotton, matte paper, wood grain, and softly blurred nursery elements, all coordinated with {컬러 톤}.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: full-frame portrait look, 85mm f/1.4 equivalent at f/2.0, shallow but realistic depth separation.
- Lighting: soft studio key light from upper-left at 45°, subtle fill from front-right, very gentle shadow roll-off, natural catchlights, and controlled highlights on skin and fabric.
- Color grade: warm cream and ivory base with muted pink and baby-blue accents, mild pastel studio grading, natural skin tones preserved.
- Realism: preserve fine photographic details including baby skin pores, faint cheek redness, soft hair flyaways, fabric texture, tiny wrinkles in clothing, and believable lens softness in the background.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean family portrait-card — warm, affectionate, and realistic, like a boutique Seoul baby studio announcement photo with a refined magazine-family keepsake feel.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: render the following Korean strings cleanly and legibly when included: “우리의 미래 아기”, “2026.05”, “서울 스튜디오”, “엄마 아빠를 닮은 작은 미소”. Avoid misspellings, distorted Hangul, or random pseudo-text.
- Visual invariants: the generated child must look like a plausible future offspring of the parents in {부모 사진}, with natural facial feature blending; preserve realistic human anatomy, correct proportions, and age-appropriate infant/toddler details for {자녀 나이} and {성별}.
- Photographic finish: the image must feel like a real studio photograph and printed portrait card, not an illustration, not a cartoon, and not an obvious AI composite.
- Layout fidelity: respect {레이아웃}, {배경}, {라이팅}, and {컬러 톤} while keeping the child’s face clear, emotionally engaging, and central to the composition.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Broken Korean characters
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized likeness

[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean autobiographical essay book cover, single-volume literary jacket, designed for intimate personal storytelling, bookstore shelf presence, and e-book thumbnail readability.
Editorial literary cover with a quiet human portrait, still-life detail, window-side scene, or abstract painterly symbol, presented as a believable printed trade paperback front cover.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Compose a vertical 1024x1536 front cover for a Korean essay/memoir paperback, with the main visual occupying the upper 55–60% and a structured title/publishing zone in the lower portion.
- Use {비주얼 컨셉} as the core image direction; enrich the scene with tactile paper grain, soft shadows, faint ink absorption, and small book-design details that would naturally appear on a contemporary Korean literary cover.
- Arrange {제목}, {부제}, {작가}, {장르라벨}, {판정보}, {추천문}, {표지문장}, and {출판사·로고} on a calm editorial grid, allowing the image and typography to feel intentionally designed as one finished jacket.
- Apply {컬러 톤} across background, image treatment, type color, small accent marks, and publication details; let the accent colors appear through subtle typographic highlights, a small line motif, or a restrained publisher-style graphic device.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Main visual block: build a single focal image using {비주얼 컨셉}, positioned like a refined book-jacket hero image, with realistic print texture, soft paper grain, and believable halftone or ink-on-stock detail.
2) Genre / series label: place {장르라벨} as a small editorial label near the top or upper-left, similar to a Korean bookstore category mark or independent press series note.
3) Title zone: place {제목} prominently in the upper-middle or mid-lower area depending on image balance, with strong hierarchy, clear legibility, and a literary Korean serif presence.
4) Subtitle zone: place {부제} directly under the title in a lighter, smaller style, using measured spacing and delicate alignment rather than a heavy divider.
5) Author line: place {작가} near the subtitle or lower title area in a modest size, maintaining a personal, trustworthy memoir tone.
6) Cover quote and micro text: integrate {추천문} and {표지문장} as small but readable Korean jacket copy, positioned like a real essay cover blurb or reflective excerpt line.
7) Publication details: include {판정보} and {출판사·로고} near the lower edge or corner as discreet imprint-style elements; add a tiny simulated spine-credit hint along one vertical edge if it fits the front-cover mockup.
8) Finish: make it feel like a Korean trade paperback jacket photographed or rendered front-on, with subtle stock texture, precise print alignment, fine ink edges, and a believable matte cover surface.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use {타이포}; title in a high-contrast Korean serif such as 본명조 Medium or Noto Serif KR SemiBold, about 62–88 pt equivalent; subtitle in Light or italic-inspired styling, about 24–34 pt; author, genre label, edition, quote, and imprint in small clean sans text like Pretendard Regular, about 14–22 pt.
- Color palette: use {컬러 톤} as the primary palette; background can carry cream, beige, taupe, warm gray, or off-white paper tones; main text should remain deep charcoal or near-black; coral and sage accents may appear in small lines, dots, publisher marks, or cover-note highlights.
- Print treatment: include matte paper texture, gentle ink spread, subtle paper-edge shadow, faint emboss-like pressure on the title, and realistic cover stock reflectance under soft light.
- Decorative structure: allow refined literary elements such as a thin vertical rule, small page-number-like mark, quiet floral/sky/window motif, handwritten-style note fragment, or abstract brush trace when it supports the autobiographical mood.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: if photographic, render like an 85mm portrait lens at f/2.0 or a 50mm normal lens at f/2.8 for gentle subject separation; if abstract, emulate a gallery print photographed with a 70mm equivalent front-on.
- Lighting: soft window light from upper-left at roughly 45°, with very mild fill from the right; if using a portrait, keep shadows natural and low-contrast; if using an abstract image, simulate diffused daylight across paper.
- Color grade: muted cream + taupe + charcoal with small coral and sage notes, lightly filmic and low saturation, similar to a quiet literary magazine cover.

[6. MOOD]
A restrained Korean literary memoir cover with the intimate calm of a New Yorker-style essay jacket and the tactile seriousness of a well-designed independent press book, enriched with real publication details and quiet emotional evidence of a lived life.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문자열: "{제목}", "{부제}", "{작가}", "{장르라벨}", "{판정보}", "{추천문}", "{표지문장}", "{출판사·로고}"
- Cover realism: one cohesive Korean essay book front cover only; all visible Korean typography must look typeset, printed, aligned, and publication-ready.
- Text hierarchy: "{제목}" must be the dominant readable element; "{부제}" and "{작가}" must remain clearly readable; micro copy may be smaller but should not become broken glyphs.
- If a portrait is used, facial anatomy must be natural and realistic; if a figure appears, hands must be anatomically correct with exactly 5 fingers per hand.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Dating-app profile card mockup for a vertical phone screen, designed to look like a realistic Bumble/Tinder-style app profile screenshot.
Make it usable as a believable fake app screen preview with a main photo, profile details, interest tags, location/activity microcopy, photo navigation indicators, and action buttons.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- 9:16 phone portrait layout with the main profile image occupying the top 62% of the frame, and the card info panel stacked in the lower 38%.
- The main photo area should feel like an in-app profile hero image, with realistic UI framing, rounded corners, subtle safe-area status bar, and no visible device bezel.
- Place {배경 사진} as the main profile photo, cropped to fill the hero area naturally, with authentic social-profile framing and realistic depth.
- Overlay small app UI elements on the hero image: top status bar time/battery/wifi glyphs, photo carousel dots or segmented bars, a back chevron, a three-dot menu, and a small label such as “오늘의 추천”.
- Add a translucent lower gradient over the bottom of the photo only where needed so the UI remains legible while the image still looks natural.
- Profile name block should sit immediately below the photo, aligned left with comfortable mobile padding, including {이름·나이} plus a small verified-style check badge, “최근 활동” dot, or distance/location line.
- Interest tags should appear as pill-shaped chips in a one- to two-row cluster under the bio, mixed with one or two app-generated chips such as “주말 산책” or “카페 투어” only if space allows.
- The action area should reserve space at the bottom for X / super-like or star / like buttons, with realistic thumb-sized spacing, circular controls, shadows, and small icon labels.
- Include tiny mobile details such as a bottom gesture bar, section divider, “신고” or share micro icon, page indicator “1/4”, and a faint bottom navigation hint if it fits {레이아웃}.
- Keep the overall layout modern, screenshot-like, and content-rich, with realistic mobile app spacing and card hierarchy.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Hero photo area (top 62%): {배경 사진} displayed as a polished dating-app profile image, full-bleed within a rounded card, with subtle top-safe-area spacing, natural lens depth, realistic exposure, and authentic in-app photo cropping.
- Photo UI overlay: add segmented photo progress bars near the top, a small “1/4” indicator, top-left navigation chevron, top-right overflow menu, and a small translucent badge reading “오늘의 추천” or “NEW”.
- Header block (below photo): show {이름·나이} in a bold app-style profile header, positioned left-aligned with strong hierarchy. Add a tiny check mark badge, a green active dot with “최근 활동”, and a location/distance line such as “서울 성수동 · 2km 거리”.
- Bio section: place {자기소개} beneath the name in smaller, readable UI text, wrapped across 1–3 lines with realistic app line spacing. Add a subtle prompt label above or beside it such as “내 소개” or “한 줄 소개”.
- Interest chip row: render {관심사 태그} as rounded tags with consistent padding, subtle border, soft shadow, and equal spacing like a real dating app interface. Chips may include tiny icons or emoji accents such as “☕”, “🎧”, “🏃” when visually appropriate.
- Detail snippets: include 2–3 small profile info rows or chips below the bio/tags, such as “키 172cm”, “반려견 좋아함”, “답장 빠른 편”, “주말엔 전시회”, styled as realistic app metadata without overpowering the main text.
- UI theme treatment: apply {UI 모드} consistently to accent color, button style, icon tint, progress bars, highlight labels, active dots, and selected chips.
- Layout framing: follow {레이아웃} precisely, keeping the screen vertical, profile-first, and visually close to an authentic mobile dating-app screenshot.
- Bottom controls: add circular X, star/spark, and heart buttons with realistic icon weight, touch-target sizing, soft drop shadows, and a small bottom gesture bar.
- Final realism pass: ensure the full composition reads like a genuine dating-app card preview, with natural UI density, varied microcopy, crisp alignment, and credible app-screen details.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for UI text, with bold 700–800 weight for the name and medium 500–600 weight for body text; size hierarchy should feel like a modern mobile app screenshot.
- Color palette: if {UI 모드} leans Bumble, use warm yellow #FFC629 with white, charcoal, honey beige, and soft gray surfaces; if Tinder, use pink #FD5068, orange #FF8A3D, white, blush highlights, and soft gray #F3F4F6.
- Borders/shadow: rounded card corners with a soft shadow 0px 10px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.12), thin divider lines in #E7E7EA, translucent photo badges, and subtle button depth without glossy effects.
- UI surfaces should use clean off-white or light neutral panels, with crisp app-like contrast, layered cards, chip borders, small icons, and believable touch-interface spacing.
- Add realistic mobile interface details: status bar glyphs, segmented photo bars, micro labels, distance/activity metadata, bottom gesture bar, and tiny icon buttons sized like an actual phone screenshot.
- Keep all UI copy short and functional; avoid long marketing slogans. Korean microcopy should look like real dating-app labels rather than an ad.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 35mm full-frame smartphone-style portrait capture look, equivalent to an 85mm f/1.8 shallow-depth profile shot for the main image area.
- Lighting: soft window light from upper-left at 45°, gentle fill from the front-right, realistic indoor social-photo exposure with natural skin tones.
- Color grade: clean mobile app realism with slightly warm neutral skin tones, balanced whites, and mild saturation; if Tinder-style, shift highlights toward pink-orange accents; if Bumble-style, keep yellow accents crisp and bright.
- UI rendering: high-resolution app screenshot clarity, sharp vector-like icons, crisp Korean typography, subtle translucency on overlays, and realistic antialiasing.
- Photo treatment: natural skin texture, believable social-profile composition, authentic background context from {배경 사진}, and depth that looks captured rather than artificially generated.

[6. MOOD]
Realistic modern dating-app UI mockup — feels like a polished app store preview or a high-fidelity product concept for Bumble/Tinder, with enough small interface details to resemble a real profile someone could swipe on.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: "{이름·나이}", "{자기소개}", and "{관심사 태그}" must render clearly in Korean if present in the design.
- Include short Korean UI labels where appropriate, such as “오늘의 추천”, “최근 활동”, “서울 성수동 · 2km 거리”, “내 소개”, “관심사”, “1/4”, and “신고”, all crisp and legible.
- The profile card must read like a real mobile dating app interface, not a poster or advertisement.
- Keep the photo, name, bio, tags, metadata, photo indicators, and action controls in the correct mobile-app hierarchy.
- Text must remain crisp and fully legible; avoid broken Korean characters, distorted letters, or unreadable microcopy.
- The composition should preserve a believable app screenshot structure with clean alignment, realistic spacing, and content-rich UI details.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness

[INPUT]
- language: Korean

[1. PURPOSE]
K-pop comeback teaser full set for a girl group, designed as a 4-panel editorial campaign package for album jacket, teaser poster, MV still, and concert stage.
Magazine-style K-pop rollout visual with cohesive branding, realistic printed/social campaign details, and enough small metadata to feel like an actual comeback promotion post.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- 2x2 grid fills the square canvas evenly, with each panel separated by thin off-white gutters and a consistent editorial magazine margin.
- {그룹 이름} should feel like the central brand across all four panels, with the same logo treatment, color identity, date labels, and campaign typography carrying through every frame.
- Backgrounds shift by panel but stay inside the same palette, using soft floral surfaces, stage-light ambience, satin fabric, printed paper grain, lens flare, confetti specks, and lightly textured poster overlays.
- Keep {컴백 컨셉} present through styling, set dressing, props, motion cues, lighting motifs, and repeated graphic symbols rather than literal repetition.
- Use {레이아웃} as the structural guide, while maintaining readable panel hierarchy, authentic comeback-poster density, and clear editorial framing between the four cuts.
- Add small real-world campaign elements: issue/date label, barcode block, track-release note, short feature blurbs, panel captions, model/member credit, tiny production credit, and social-handle style microtext.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Panel 1 — Album jacket: a clustered group close-up with layered flower backdrop, faces and shoulders overlapping slightly, soft frontal composition, polished cover-art framing. Add a compact album-cover masthead, {그룹 이름} logo, small sticker-like label "앨범 재킷", tiny credit line "PHOTO BY STUDIO 247", and a slim side-spine text strip reading "COMEBACK ISSUE / VOL.247".
2. Panel 2 — Teaser poster: one main member as the hero, centered at 60% frame height, surrounded by dramatic floral shadows, glossy hair highlights, fabric texture, and a bold poster title zone. Include short Korean cover blurbs such as "오늘 밤 6시 공개", "스페셜 포토북", and "멤버 인터뷰", plus a small barcode area and release-date label "2026년 5월호".
3. Panel 3 — MV still: dynamic dance moment captured mid-motion, diagonal body lines, one or two members partially motion-blurred for energy, realistic studio floor reflections, haze, backlight streaks, and visible choreography spacing. Add film-still metadata like "MV 스틸", "SCENE 03", "TAKE 07", a tiny timecode strip, and a caption bar reading "컴백 티저 풀세트".
4. Panel 4 — Concert stage: wide live performance shot with visible stage lights, LED screen glow, microphone stands or handheld mics, audience light-stick bokeh dots, confetti particles, stage smoke, and the group arranged in a strong horizontal stage line. Add concert-poster details: "콘서트 무대", "첫 무대 D-7", venue-style microtext "SEOUL LIVE HALL", and a small ticket-info block "OPEN 20:00".
5. Across all four panels, preserve one shared graphic language: floral texture, soft editorial contrast, consistent color treatment, small magazine annotations, and repeated comeback-campaign icon marks so the set reads as one professionally art-directed rollout.
6. Integrate {4컷 시리즈} as clearly distinct visual beats, each panel immediately understandable at a glance: cover art, teaser portrait, music-video performance, and live concert reveal.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: bold English sans-serif for {그룹 이름}, paired with compact Korean supporting text in Pretendard or Noto Sans KR, heavy weight for headers and medium weight for subtext, roughly 42–64 px for main titles and 18–24 px for secondary labels, with tiny 8–12 px production credits and barcode captions.
- Color palette: {컬러 톤} with controlled accents of charcoal, plus paper white #F5F1EA and deep near-black #1E1C1F for contrast; allow realistic lipstick tones, skin tones, metallic jewelry glints, stage LEDs, and printed-paper ink variation.
- Border/shadow: thin editorial gutters, subtle soft drop shadow 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity under each panel, refined magazine-cutout separation, no hard outlines.
- Use {타이포} for title treatment, keeping letter spacing slightly expanded and the hierarchy clean like a K-pop magazine spread, while adding authentic small cover lines, captions, issue labels, and social-post metadata.
- Graphic details may include small flower icons, translucent stickers, corner crop marks, vertical spine text, tiny page codes, and a barcode rectangle, all integrated into the campaign design without overpowering the idols.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial fashion photography look, 85mm f/1.4 for the hero and group close-ups, 35mm f/1.8 for the stage wide, crisp but not hyperreal.
- Lighting: soft diffused studio key from upper-left at 45°, gentle fill from right, plus subtle rim light on hair and shoulders; stage panel uses concert spotlights with controlled bloom, LED backlight, atmospheric haze, and realistic reflections on skin, sequins, microphones, and glossy floor.
- Color grade: faded pink, coral, and ivory with deep charcoal anchoring shadows, slightly filmic contrast, clean print-like separation.
- Surface realism: visible magazine paper grain, soft halftone-like ink texture in poster areas, realistic fabric folds, flower petal depth, hair detail, makeup sheen, jewelry highlights, concert smoke, and shallow depth-of-field bokeh where appropriate.

[6. MOOD]
K-pop comeback campaign editorial — feels like a high-end music magazine spread and fandom teaser package, polished like a Vogue Korea x DAZED-style rollout, with the excitement of a real album comeback, teaser drop, MV reveal, and first concert stage announcement.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the rendered image must correctly show these Korean strings when text is included in the design: "K-pop 그룹", "컴백 티저 풀세트", "앨범 재킷", "티저 포스터", "MV 스틸", "콘서트 무대", "오늘 밤 6시 공개", "스페셜 포토북", "멤버 인터뷰", "첫 무대 D-7", "2026년 5월호".
- Keep {그룹 이름}, {컴백 컨셉}, {4컷 시리즈}, {컬러 톤}, {레이아웃}, {타이포}, and {비율} visually respected exactly as the user-provided creative direction.
- All 4 panels must clearly read as distinct scenes while sharing one cohesive brand identity for {그룹 이름}.
- Keep faces anatomically correct, hands correct with exactly 5 fingers per hand if visible, and stage choreography believable.
- Text should look printed or professionally composited into the campaign design, with clean Korean character rendering and plausible magazine/poster alignment.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized real-person likeness

[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Instagram Story Q&A box mockup that looks like a realistic fake screenshot, designed for social media storytelling and casual Q&A content.
Vertical story-style phone screenshot composition using {비율}, with {배경 사진} as the full-screen background and an overlaid Instagram-style question-and-answer card enriched with believable story UI details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- The background photo fills the full frame edge-to-edge, behaving like a captured Instagram Story rather than a studio mockup.
- Place the Q&A card in the upper-middle to center area, occupying about 34–42% of the frame width and 24–32% of the height, with believable mobile UI spacing.
- Use {배경 사진} as the full-screen backdrop; let natural details from the photo remain visible so the screenshot feels lived-in and personal.
- Render {Q&A 박스 질문} as the main focal text inside the question sticker, and {답변} as a casual reply-style block beneath it with clear hierarchy.
- Add authentic Instagram Story screenshot cues: top progress bar, small profile handle area, timestamp, close/menu icon hints, bottom reply field, tiny heart/share icons, and a subtle “답장 보내기” input bar.
- Include small social-card details such as “@daily_hongdae”, “오늘의 Q&A”, “홍대 점심 기록”, and short hashtag-like micro text such as “#오늘점심 #홍대맛집” without competing with the main Q&A.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Background layer: {배경 사진} should fill the entire canvas like a real smartphone story screenshot, with natural crop, real texture, and contextual visual detail from the photo.
2. Story chrome layer: Add a thin Instagram-like progress bar at the very top, a tiny circular profile thumbnail placeholder, handle text “@daily_hongdae”, a small timestamp “방금 전”, and subtle top-right story icons consistent with {UI}.
3. Q&A UI layer: Add a white rounded question box with Instagram-like story styling, using a pink-to-light-yellow gradient accent around the UI, matching native story interface proportions.
4. Sticker header: At the top of the Q&A card, include a small gradient pill label reading “무엇이든 물어보세요” or “오늘의 Q&A”, with a tiny sparkle or question-mark icon accent.
5. Question area: Place {Q&A 박스 질문} near the top of the card in crisp Korean text, centered or slightly left-aligned depending on the UI layout, with strong readability and mobile-app scale.
6. Answer area: Place {답변} beneath the question region as a reply-style text block, visually separated with a soft divider, pale chat bubble, or light gray answer panel while staying integrated into the same story screenshot aesthetic.
7. Interface detail: Include a subtle “답장 보내기” button/input field at the bottom, a tiny paper-plane/share icon, a heart icon, and a small “친한 친구” or “공유” micro label if it fits the UI naturally.
8. Decorative story details: Add 1–2 small sticker-like accents such as a tiny “맛집 저장” tag, location pin label “홍대입구”, or a small doodle arrow pointing toward the answer, using the same blush pink, pale yellow, and soft coral palette.
9. Photo-treatment: Preserve the natural look of the background photo while applying a very slight translucent dark or light gradient behind the UI only where needed for text readability; keep the Q&A card sharply legible.
10. Screenshot realism: The final image should read like a genuine Instagram Story capture, with believable spacing, rounded corners, native app proportions, subtle compression feel, and layered mobile interface details.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for Korean UI text, medium to semibold weight for the question, regular to medium weight for the answer, with sizes that match mobile story readability.
- Color palette: white #FFFFFF for the card, blush pink #F8B8C8, pale yellow #FFF3B0, soft coral #FF8FA3, light gray #E9E9E9, and the natural tones from {컬러 톤}.
- Border/shadow: use a soft drop shadow with 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 16% opacity, and rounded corners around 22px to mimic a mobile overlay.
- UI styling: keep the Q&A element compact, native-looking, and touch-friendly, with a subtle gradient ring or highlight typical of story UI.
- Microcopy styling: set secondary details like “@daily_hongdae”, “방금 전”, “답장 보내기”, “홍대입구”, and hashtags in smaller Korean UI text with realistic opacity and spacing.
- Visual hierarchy: the largest readable text is {Q&A 박스 질문}, the second strongest text is {답변}, and all handle, timestamp, hashtag, sticker, and icon details remain secondary.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: smartphone front-camera story capture look, equivalent to a 26–28mm full-frame smartphone wide lens, vertical crop, slight perspective distortion typical of handheld story screenshots.
- Lighting: preserve the lighting already present in {배경 사진}; if the scene looks indoor, keep soft ambient light from the side, and if outdoor, retain natural daylight without artificial studio treatment.
- Color grade: natural story-screenshot grade with the background photo kept mostly intact, while the Q&A card uses pink and light pastel accents for contrast.
- Texture realism: allow subtle phone screenshot artifacts, slight app-layer translucency, natural background grain, and realistic compression softness while keeping all Korean text crisp.

[6. MOOD]
Casual Instagram Story screenshot — like a real everyday Q&A post captured from a personal social feed, with the authenticity of a mobile app interface, friendly lunch-chat energy, and spontaneous social storytelling.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구가 정확히 보여야 함
  - {Q&A 박스 질문}  예시 기본값: "오늘 점심 뭐 드셨어요?"
  - {답변}  예시 기본값: "홍대 어쩌면식당 제육 정식! 진짜 맛집임 강추"
- Additional small Korean UI text may appear naturally, such as "무엇이든 물어보세요", "오늘의 Q&A", "답장 보내기", "방금 전", "홍대입구", "홍대 점심 기록", "#오늘점심 #홍대맛집".
- The UI must feel like a real Instagram Story Q&A screenshot, with believable spacing, rounded white card, top story chrome, bottom reply field, and native app-like placement.
- Keep all Korean characters clean and fully legible, with no broken glyphs or scrambled text.
- The answer should read as a fake screenshot reply from a casual story interaction, not as a polished ad headline.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

Create a realistic 4-cut makeup comparison portrait card for social sharing, showing one person transformed across clearly different beauty styles while preserving identity.
Fashion/beauty editorial layout with side-by-side comparison, suitable for a Korean salon portfolio, Instagram carousel cover, or beauty magazine feature page.
Use {4컷 모드}, {레이아웃}, {라이팅}, {배경}, and {비율} to guide the final arrangement and visual balance.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Single model is repeated across 4 equal panels, with identical face angle and framing in every cut so makeup changes are the main difference.
- Keep {원본 보존} as the invariant across all panels; only makeup, hair, and styling may change.
- Use a 2x2 grid as the primary layout following {레이아웃}; if horizontal 4-cut is chosen, maintain equal panel widths and consistent face crop.
- Background should be {배경} with a realistic Korean beauty studio feel: softly lit paper backdrop or seamless wall, subtle blush-beige texture, faint studio depth, and refined salon/editorial atmosphere.
- Keep all faces centered at chest-up or shoulder-up crop, with consistent eye line and similar head size across the 4 panels.
- Add a polished social-card frame around the grid: top header bar, small issue/date label, beauty studio handle, and tiny save/share-style micro icons.
- Include small realistic comparison details around the panels: makeup shade swatches, tiny sparkle stickers, delicate divider dots, and short Korean caption notes that do not cover facial features.
- Add a small bottom footer line with salon-style credit text such as “MAKEUP COMPARISON | Seoul Beauty Studio | 2026.05”.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Panel 1 — Daily look: soft natural base, light blush, neutral lips, understated eyeliner, and simple natural hair styling; overall effect should read fresh and everyday.
2. Panel 2 — Wedding look: brighter complexion, fuller eye makeup, romantic blush, glossy or satin lips, and polished bridal hair with elegant volume or soft waves.
3. Panel 3 — Post-procedure glow look: luminous skin finish, hydrated cheeks, subtle pink warmth, refined brows, and healthy rested impression without over-contouring.
4. Panel 4 — K-pop idol look: stronger eyeliner, defined lashes, bolder lip color, sharper facial contrast, and more styled hair with performance-ready polish.
5. Bottom labels — Place short readable Korean labels beneath each panel, aligned consistently, with enough padding so the text does not touch the face crop or frame edge.
6. Header content — Add a realistic beauty editorial title area: “메이크업 4컷 비교”, “VOL.042”, “2026.05 BEAUTY NOTE”, and handle “@seoul.makeup.room”.
7. Micro captions — Add very short Korean notes near each label: “출근 메이크업”, “본식 촬영”, “맑은 피부결”, “무대 조명”.
8. Footer CTA — Add small Korean CTA text: “저장하고 내 스타일 찾기 · 상담 예약 DM”.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR, medium to semibold weight, 26–34px equivalent for main labels, clean sans-serif with tight vertical alignment; use smaller 11–16px equivalent text for date, handle, micro captions, and footer credits.
- Color palette: white #FFFFFF, soft blush pink #F7E7EC, warm beige #F3EBDD, light gray #E6E6E6, charcoal #2B2B2B for text, with small rose gold or muted mauve accents for stickers and swatches.
- Border/shadow: use thin 1px to 2px separators or subtle panel borders, with a very soft drop shadow 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 12–15% opacity only if needed.
- Layout should feel like a finished Korean beauty comparison card: editorial header, balanced grid, readable panel labels, realistic printed/social UI details, and refined salon portfolio polish.
- Decorative elements may include tiny sparkle icons, lipstick-tone swatches, blush circles, and thin annotation lines, kept secondary to the face and makeup comparison.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: full-frame portrait look, 85mm f/1.4 or 70–200mm at 135mm, medium close-up framing for beauty comparison, sharp facial detail without distortion.
- Lighting: all four panels use the same soft studio setup guided by {라이팅}, key light from upper-left at 45°, gentle fill from front-right, soft catchlights in the eyes, flattering skin texture, and controlled shadow contrast.
- Color grade: clean editorial neutral grade with slightly warm skin tones, soft pink-beige whites, controlled highlights, and moderate contrast.
- Rendering: realistic skin texture, natural pores, believable hair strands, accurate makeup finish differences, and high-resolution beauty-retouch quality without making the face look synthetic.
- Overall ratio and crop should respect {비율}, producing a square 1024x1024 social-ready comparison card.

[6. MOOD]
Korean beauty magazine comparison spread — Vogue Korea / Allure Korea editorial polish with a Seoul salon portfolio feel, lively enough for Instagram but refined enough for professional makeup consultation.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구가 정확히 보여야 함
  - 메이크업 4컷 비교
  - 데일리
  - 웨딩
  - 시술 후 광채
  - K-POP 아이돌
  - 저장하고 내 스타일 찾기
- Preserve identity across all 4 panels: same person, same facial structure, same camera angle, same crop, same background family, only makeup/hair/style changes.
- All four panels must feel like a deliberate comparison set with equal visual weight and consistent framing.
- The makeup differences must be immediately readable: natural daily, romantic bridal, luminous glow, and bold idol styling.
- Small header, handle, date, captions, swatches, and footer details should enhance realism while keeping the face and makeup as the main focus.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

- Broken Korean characters

- Background should stay visually unified through {배경}: warm ivory studio / softly lit window-side interior, with subtle lived-in details such as a curtain edge, small plant blur, desk corner, film-photo texture, or age-appropriate personal cue that does not steal focus.
- Keep framing, crop height, and head angle nearly identical from panel to panel so the age progression is easy to compare.

- Add a subtle top header strip reading {카드 제목}, a small handle {핸들}, and a timestamp/location label using {날짜} · {장소}.

- Panel 1: 10대 — show youthful facial softness, bright eyes, smoother skin, and the clothing cues from {4컷 흐름}; expression should feel relaxed and natural, like a school-year portrait captured near daylight.
- Panel 2: 20대 — keep the same face shape and pose, with slightly more defined features, casual university-age styling, and a clean modern portrait finish; include a faint campus-life cue such as a tote strap, knit cardigan, or blurred notebook edge.
- Panel 3: 30대 — introduce subtle maturity in the face, more structured styling, and a polished working-adult look while preserving identity; add refined details like a neat shirt collar, watch glint, or soft office-window tone.

- Place small age labels beneath each panel exactly as specified in {레이아웃}; include the caption band text in accurate Korean: 15세, 25세, 35세, 45세.
- Add a footer area with {캡션}, {해시태그}, small save/share micro icons, and a tiny page indicator {페이지 표시} to make the result feel like a polished social portrait card.
- Maintain the same overall visual language across all four frames so the result reads as one coherent timeline.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for labels, medium weight, small size around 18–22 px equivalent for age labels; header and caption can use 24–34 px equivalent with clean editorial spacing.
- Color palette: use the faded warm tones from {컬러 톤}, with soft ivory, muted beige, gentle peach, warm gray, and low-saturation skin tones; keep contrast elegant and film-like.
- Border/shadow: thin white gutters between panels, subtle 2–4 px soft shadow, light paper-card separation, and a delicate rounded-corner social-card frame suitable for a 1024x1024 square.
- Include small decorative tags from {장식 태그}: tiny timeline dots, archive number, date stamp, or film-frame marks, styled like a Korean lifestyle magazine insert.
- Keep all Korean text legible, aligned, and intentionally placed; the portrait remains dominant while the card details add realism.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: full-frame portrait look, 85mm f/1.8 equivalent, centered head-and-shoulders framing, shallow but realistic depth of field, editorial studio portrait clarity.
- Lighting: use gentle window light from upper-left at about 45° with soft fill from the front-right; make the 10대 panel slightly brighter and the 40대 panel slightly more diffused and calm.
- Color grade: faded warm Portra 400-inspired grade, soft cream highlights, muted skin tones, low-contrast film-like rolloff, slightly desaturated shadows.

[6. MOOD]
Korean magazine portrait editorial — warm personal archive, Dazed Korea / Kinfolk-style time progression, realistic aging, soft daylight, and restrained film-photography emotion.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: "15세", "25세", "35세", "45세"
- Rendered header text: "{카드 제목}" / "{핸들}" / "{날짜} · {장소}"
- Rendered footer text: "{캡션}" / "{해시태그}" / "{페이지 표시}"
- Facial identity must stay consistent across all four panels; only age, styling, and subtle skin texture should change.
- All four panels must keep the same grid structure and comparable crop so the timeline reads clearly.
- Natural aging only: avoid exaggerated wrinkles, extreme transformation, or uncanny face drift.
- Keep the image photoreal with believable skin, hair, clothing, and lighting.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

- Broken Korean characters

- Using a different identity between panels
