[1. PURPOSE]
Indie LP / EP album cover design, square 1:1 release artwork for streaming platforms and physical jacket use.
Cinematic indie-ballad sleeve with restrained emotional depth, designed to feel like a real small-label record cover with authentic printed-jacket details, catalog markings, release metadata, and tactile production texture.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Square LP format fills the full frame, with the main visual occupying about 65% of the canvas and integrated typography, label marks, and jacket metadata arranged as part of a real release cover.
- Primary title block is placed in the upper-left or upper-center area according to {레이아웃}, while the artist name, label mark, catalog number, and release-date microtext sit near the bottom edge like a finished indie record sleeve.
- Background treatment should feel like a tactile printed surface: faded paper grain, slightly desaturated color wash, subtle ink density variation, faint sleeve scuffs, soft corner wear, and offset-print texture.
- Include believable album-cover production details: small catalog number such as “CAT. NO. 326-EP”, release date “2026.05.01”, format note “SINGLE / EP”, tiny copyright line “ⓒ 2026 {브랜드·라벨}”, and a compact barcode block on the back-cover-inspired lower corner or side strip.
- Use {아티스트·제목}, {장르·무드}, {비주얼 컨셉}, {타이포}, {컬러 톤}, {레이아웃}, {브랜드·라벨} as editable placeholders.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Main visual zone (center 60–70%): build one clear focal subject based on {비주얼 컨셉}, such as a beach at dusk, a sunset road, a back-view figure near water, a bedroom window scene, a faded flower still life, or one expressive abstract painting treatment; enrich it with natural scene details like windblown hair, rippled water, curtain texture, handwritten tape marks, film dust, paper fibers, or soft environmental traces that support the mood.
- Title zone: place {아티스트·제목} as the dominant typographic anchor, with strong hierarchy, readable Hangul, and elegant spacing aligned to {레이아웃}; add one short Korean cover line nearby, for example “천천히 사라지는 밤” or “다시 돌아오는 계절”, small enough to feel like sleeve poetry rather than advertising.
- Supporting mood text zone: integrate {장르·무드} as a small secondary line beneath or beside the title, paired with compact English microtype such as “indie ballad / analog session / side A”.
- Release metadata zone: include short realistic sleeve details: “VOL.326”, “2026년 5월 발매”, “SIDE A 03:42”, “STEREO”, “33⅓ RPM”, and a tiny track hint such as “01. 낮은 파도” or “02. 오래된 편지” in Korean, arranged like genuine LP jacket typography.
- Typography treatment: apply {타이포} with a refined editorial balance, ensuring Hangul remains crisp and English microtype stays compact, realistic, and print-accurate.
- Palette application: render {컬러 톤} across the whole cover through muted print-like layering, allowing natural tonal variation, ink overlap, gentle stains, and analog grain while avoiding neon saturation or glossy digital gradients.
- Bottom margin / label zone: place {브랜드·라벨} small and restrained as if printed by an indie label on a real LP jacket, accompanied by a tiny label emblem, catalog code, copyright line, and barcode area.
- Layout structure: respect {레이아웃} by keeping the cover cohesive and grid-aware, with the visual, title, microtext, label information, and barcode arranged as a finished retail-ready album sleeve.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: combine a bold Korean serif for the main title, such as Noto Serif KR or Nanum Myeongjo Bold at large size, with a small sans-serif like Pretendard Medium or Inter for secondary English details, catalog numbers, release date, and track metadata.
- Color palette: use specific muted tones derived from {컬러 톤}, such as faded cyan #8FB7C6, coral #E7A08A, ivory #F4EFE6, charcoal #2C2C2C, dusty beige #D8C9B6, and warm gray #8A8178.
- Printed jacket realism: add subtle CMYK misregistration, faint halftone edge texture, sleeve rub marks, paper tooth, tiny dust specks, light ink trapping, and mild corner softening so the design feels physically printed.
- Border/shadow: no heavy frames; instead use a soft printed shadow or gentle tonal separation, around 3–5px offset and 10–15% opacity, to mimic offset-print jacket artwork.
- Album-cover details: include a compact barcode block, catalog number, release-date label, tiny track or side information, and small credits such as “photo / design / mix note” in Korean or English microtype, without overpowering the main title.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: if figurative, shoot like a 50mm f/1.8 full-frame editorial portrait with a slightly compressed, intimate perspective; if abstract, present it like a high-resolution scanned artwork sheet with flat, even framing.
- Lighting: use soft overcast daylight or late golden-hour side light from the right, with low-contrast shadow rolloff, gentle texture visibility, and a faint rim on the subject edge.
- Color grade: apply faded analog print tones, slightly lifted blacks, muted cyan-coral balance, ivory paper warmth, light film grain, and realistic scanned-sleeve texture.
- Physical finish: make the cover feel like matte uncoated paper or lightly worn record-jacket stock, with believable ink absorption and small imperfections visible at close inspection.

[6. MOOD]
Indie record sleeve editorial — like a quiet A24 film poster meets a 1990s small-label LP cover, upgraded with authentic release metadata, tactile sleeve production marks, and emotionally specific scene details.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 다음 문자열이 정확히 보여야 함: "{아티스트·제목}", "{장르·무드}", "{브랜드·라벨}".
- Additional Korean sleeve text may include short realistic lines such as “2026년 5월 발매”, “천천히 사라지는 밤”, “낮은 파도”, “오래된 편지”, and “서울 녹음실 기록”, but all Hangul must remain legible.
- Typography must be fully legible, with no broken Hangul characters, no distorted spacing inside Korean syllables, and no accidental replacement of the title with English-only text.
- The cover must feel like a real 1:1 album jacket, with one coherent visual system, authentic indie-label metadata, and a finished printed-release presentation.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness

[INPUT]

- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Create a vertical moodboard / vision-board collage for personal goal visualization, designed like an editorial zine spread that feels hand-assembled, shareable, and Pinterest-ready.
Show a 1-year life theme board with travel, health, growth, and relationships translated into layered paper snippets, photos, typography, and handwritten affirmations.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main composition: a freeform collage that fills the full page with no rigid outer frame, where the central mass occupies about 70% of the canvas and smaller clippings spread toward the edges.
- Background treatment: warm cream paper base with subtle recycled-paper grain, faint fiber texture, and slightly uneven off-white tone.
- Spacing and framing: use overlapping paper edges, taped corners, torn fragments, and asymmetrical clusters; keep readable negative space around the top title and a few keyword stickers.
- Use {테마·목표}, {콜라주 요소}, {키워드}, {레이아웃}, {컬러 톤}, {타이포} as customizable content anchors.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Background layer — Build a full-bleed cream paper surface with light fiber grain, faint shadow pooling near edges, and a subtle scanned-zine texture.
2. Base collage layer — Arrange {콜라주 요소} as mixed clippings: travel snapshots, lifestyle photos, portrait cutouts, flowers, books, city night views, and texture swatches, each slightly tilted 3–8 degrees.
3. Goal headline area — Place {테마·목표} near the upper third as the main title block, combining bold Korean serif, small English sans-serif subline, and a hand-drawn marker accent under one key phrase.
4. Keyword cluster — Scatter {키워드} as 8–12 short sticky-note labels, stamped tags, or handwritten fragments around the central collage so they feel collected over time rather than aligned in a grid.
5. Connector doodles — Add hand-drawn arrows, circles, stars, underlines, and small check marks that visually connect goals to images, with imperfect pen pressure and casual sketch energy.
6. Layout behavior — Follow {레이아웃} by letting some paper corners curl, some photos overlap by 10–20%, and a few elements extend slightly beyond the safe margin for an authentic scrapbook feel.
7. Color application — Apply {컬러 톤} across tape, labels, icon doodles, and accent papers so the board stays cohesive even with many sources mixed together.
8. Typography treatment — Mix {타이포} with intentional hierarchy: title first, then short labels, then small caption notes, keeping the board editorial rather than poster-like.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard Bold or Noto Serif KR Bold for the main Korean title, Noto Sans KR / Inter for small notes, and a hand-drawn marker font for emphasis; title around 64–92 px, labels 22–34 px, micro-notes 16–20 px.
- Color palette: cream #F5EFE6, beige #DCCDBB, coral #E89A86, sage #A9B8A1, muted brown #7A614D, soft charcoal #2F2A26.
- Border/shadow: no hard box borders; use soft paper shadows with 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 12–18% opacity, plus slight natural cast shadows under taped items.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: top-down flat lay aesthetic, equivalent to a Sony A7R IV with a 35mm lens at f/5.6 for crisp paper texture and even collage clarity.
- Lighting: soft window light from upper-left at 45°, diffused through sheer curtains, with a gentle secondary fill from the lower-right to preserve readable shadows.
- Color grade: warm cream, beige, coral, and sage with slightly muted saturation, like an editorial scrapbook photographed for Kinfolk or The Creative Independent.

[6. MOOD]
A personal editorial vision board with a Kinfolk magazine spread feel — thoughtful, tactile, and quietly aspirational rather than commercial.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following Korean strings must appear exactly and cleanly if used in the design: "천천히", "진심", "여행", "운동", "독서", "새로운 사람", "꽃", "휴식".
- The collage must feel hand-assembled and layered, not like a rigid poster grid.
- Keep all Korean characters fully legible and correctly formed; no broken syllables, mirrored glyphs, or substituted Latin letters.
- Avoid any element that makes the board feel like an ad banner or a corporate presentation slide.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Hard outer frame boxes or repetitive panel borders
- Corporate ad-copy styling
- Synthetic CG-looking bokeh or plastic shine
- Overly perfect symmetry
- Text that is unreadable, misspelled, or mixed with garbled characters

[1. PURPOSE]
Yoga and Pilates pose infographic poster, 12-step sequence, designed for health/wellness social sharing and printable guide use.
Polished editorial layout that teaches a full routine at a glance with clear progression, readable pose labels, and realistic printed-poster details such as guide metadata, footer notes, studio contact text, and small wellness icons.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main composition: a vertical 3x4 or 4x3 grid with 12 evenly sized panels, each panel containing one pose illustration, pose name, breathing cue, and hold timing details.
- Overall poster should feel like a real yoga studio handout: full-frame vertical sheet, warm matte paper texture, faint ink grain, subtle sage-green dividers, charcoal typography, and small editorial annotations.
- Sequence title area at the top should span the full width and include {시퀀스 종류} as the primary Korean title, plus compact supporting metadata such as "12자세 시퀀스", "총 24분", "LEVEL 1–2", "VOL.12", and "2026.05 가이드".
- Grid block should sit below the header with a precise, readable structure; each cell should include a small pose number 01–12, a pose illustration, Korean pose name from {자세 리스트}, English pose name when appropriate, and timing/breathing notes from {자세 정보}.
- Background should be a calm matte paper texture in warm beige, with sage-green accents, muted olive section tags, charcoal text, and soft cream panel surfaces.
- Add realistic guide elements around the layout: small line icons for breath / alignment / rest, tiny arrow markers showing flow direction, a footer reminder strip, a QR-code-style square, studio contact line, and a small sponsor/credit area.
- Use {시퀀스 종류}, {자세 리스트}, {자세 정보}, {레이아웃}, {컬러 톤}, {인물 톤}, {비율} placeholders throughout the infographic content.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header band: place the sequence title at the top in a strong editorial headline area. Set main Korean title using {시퀀스 종류}; include small labels such as "YOGA · PILATES ROUTINE", "12 POSE FLOW", "VOL.12", "2026년 5월 업데이트", and "소요 시간 24분".
- Header details: add a slim divider line beneath the title, a small subtitle such as "호흡을 따라 천천히 이어가는 데일리 루틴", and compact category chips like "초보 가능", "매트 운동", "전신 밸런스".
- Grid block: render 12 pose panels in strict sequence order, reading left-to-right, top-to-bottom according to {레이아웃}, with consistent visual rhythm and clear spacing between cells.
- Each pose panel: show the pose illustration centered in the upper portion, with the Korean pose name and English pose name below, followed by breathing cycle and hold time in smaller type. Use {인물 톤} and {비율} for the figure style and body proportions.
- Sequence labels: make numbering clear and compact, e.g. 01–12, placed near the top-left or top-center of each cell for fast scanning. Add tiny flow arrows between selected panels so the sequence feels guided.
- Timing details: keep duration and breathing notes in a smaller secondary line so the pose name remains dominant; include realistic examples such as "4호흡", "30초 유지", "좌우 3회", or content from {자세 정보}.
- Micro guidance: include one short alignment cue per row or small side note such as "어깨 힘 빼기", "골반 정렬", "목 긴장 완화", "호흡 유지" without crowding the pose names.
- Footer strip: use a visually lighter bottom band for a routine note, safety reminder, page metadata, and credit text. Include Korean footer strings such as "통증이 있으면 즉시 중단하세요", "© 오늘의 매트 루틴", "@wellness.studio", "문의 02-1234-5678", and a QR-code-style block labeled "루틴 영상 보기".

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for Korean labels, with Bold 700 for headings and Medium 500 / Regular 400 for body text; size hierarchy should be clear, with the title roughly 2.5–3x larger than panel text.
- If English pose names appear, use a clean sans-serif such as Inter or Montserrat in small caps or regular weight.
- Color palette: warm beige #F3EBDD, sage green #A9B89A, muted olive #7E8B6A, charcoal #2F3432, soft cream #FAF7F1. Apply {컬러 톤} as the guiding palette direction.
- Use thin 1px separators, soft panel boundaries, subtle paper fibers, faint ink misregistration, tiny editorial symbols, and a gentle 4px y-offset, 10px blur shadow at 10% opacity where panels need separation.
- Pose illustrations may be refined flat editorial figures or soft semi-realistic fitness illustrations; keep anatomy believable, joints aligned, and the same drawing style across all 12 panels.
- Decorative details should support the guide: small breath icons, alignment dots, leaf-like line ornaments, calm geometric markers, and muted section labels that make the poster feel printed and practical.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: if using photoreal model references, present them like an 85mm f/1.8 portrait setup or a 50mm f/2 studio reference; if illustrated, keep the figure proportions clean and consistent with editorial fitness graphics.
- Lighting: soft diffused studio light from upper-left with gentle fill from the right, natural paper shadows, mild surface texture, and no harsh specular highlights.
- Color grade: muted wellness palette with beige paper, sage green accents, charcoal typography, soft cream panels, and slightly desaturated skin or line-art tones for a calm premium magazine spread feel.
- Realism details: include tactile printed-poster texture, slight paper grain, crisp Korean typography, carefully aligned grid columns, subtle ink density variation, and believable small-print footer information.

[6. MOOD]
Premium wellness magazine editorial — like a modern yoga studio handout designed with the clarity of Kinfolk and the polish of Monocle, but with enough real guide information to feel usable, printed, and content-rich.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 표시되어야 하는 문자열 — "시퀀스 종류", "자세 리스트", "자세 정보", "레이아웃", "컬러 톤", "인물 톤", "비율".
- Render Korean guide text clearly and naturally, including examples such as "12자세 시퀀스", "총 24분", "4호흡", "30초 유지", "어깨 힘 빼기", "골반 정렬", "통증이 있으면 즉시 중단하세요", "루틴 영상 보기", "2026년 5월 업데이트".
- If pose names are rendered, they must be legible, correctly spelled Korean, and aligned consistently across all 12 panels.
- All 12 panels must follow the same layout logic and visual hierarchy; do not vary panel structure randomly.
- Keep the poster vertical at 1024x1536, with the 12-pose grid as the dominant visual subject and all added metadata serving the yoga/Pilates guide concept.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[INPUT]
- reference_image: {참고 이미지}
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Personal color diagnosis card for an attached portrait photo, designed like a premium Korean beauty consultation editorial page rather than a flat template.
Vertical mobile-friendly i2i layout with a preserved portrait, diagnostic result panel, realistic color swatch system, date/location labels, short Korean captions, and subtle beauty-studio stationery details for social sharing and consultation use.

[AUTO-DIAGNOSE — CRITICAL]
Before rendering, perform an internal personal-color analysis of the attached portrait:
1. Examine skin undertone (warm/yellow vs cool/pink), vein color hint, hair tone, eye color, and overall atmosphere.
2. Determine the best-fitting season among 봄 웜(라이트/브라이트), 여름 쿨(라이트/뮤트), 가을 웜(딥/뮤트), 겨울 쿨(딥/브라이트).
3. Use that diagnosis to FILL all [AUTO]-marked fields ({진단 결과}, {추천 컬러 팔레트}, {피해야 할 컬러}, {추천 메이크업·옷}, {컬러 톤}) — do NOT use the placeholder string literally.
4. Render the diagnosed season clearly on the card; the result MUST vary based on the actual photo (different photos → different seasons).

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Left side 48%: {원본 보존} portrait stays dominant and cleanly integrated, cropped from mid-chest upward, with natural skin texture preserved and no beauty-filter smoothing. Add a realistic printed-photo feel: slight paper thickness, soft cast shadow, tiny corner registration mark, and a small caption strip below the portrait reading "오늘의 톤 체크".
- Right side 52%: diagnostic information column with clear hierarchy; top header, consultation metadata, result line, palette swatches, avoid colors, makeup/clothing tips, and small social-card details stacked in an editorial rhythm.
- Overall framing: balanced beauty-magazine diagnostic grid adapted to 9:16, with tactile paper layers, small divider rules, tiny index numbers, and subtle label stickers that support the card without covering the face.
- Background surface: warm off-white paper texture (#F4F0E6) with visible matte grain, faint pressed-paper fibers, and a lightly tinted wash matching {컬러 톤}.
- Include realistic micro content: date label "2026.05.01", session tag "PERSONAL COLOR CHECK", small handle "@tone.note", page marker "01 / 01", and compact Korean captions near the swatches.
- Use {진단 결과}, {추천 컬러 팔레트}, {피해야 할 컬러}, {추천 메이크업·옷}, {레이아웃}, {컬러 톤} placeholders throughout the layout.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header zone (top 12%): bold title block reading "퍼스널 컬러 진단 카드" with a small subtitle "피부 톤과 분위기를 함께 보는 뷰티 노트". Add issue-style metadata such as "VOL.05", "2026년 5월", "CONSULT NOTE", aligned to the right panel.
2. Portrait zone (left 48%): {원본 보존} image placed as the primary visual anchor, with soft realistic shadow, printed-photo edge thickness, and a small lower-left label reading "원본 보존". Add subtle transparent color-check tabs beside the portrait, matching {컬러 톤}.
3. Diagnosis result zone (right upper 18%): {진단 결과} displayed as the main result line in larger type, with the most important term visually emphasized. Include a small badge-style label "RESULT" and a Korean helper line "가장 자연스럽게 어울리는 톤".
4. Color swatch zone (right middle 22%): {추천 컬러 팔레트} shown as 4–6 evenly spaced rectangular swatches with tiny Korean labels beneath each chip, all aligned in a neat grid. Add realistic swatch-card details: subtle paper texture on each chip, tiny color-code style text such as "P-01", "P-02", and a caption "추천 컬러 팔레트".
5. Avoid-color zone (right lower 12%): {피해야 할 컬러} presented as 2–3 muted swatches or text chips in a subdued tone, clearly separated from the recommended palette with a thin taupe divider and the label "주의하면 좋은 컬러".
6. Styling tip zone (bottom right 16%): {추천 메이크업·옷} arranged as short readable lines for blush, lip, and clothing suggestions. Use realistic consultation labels: "BLUSH", "LIP", "OUTFIT", with Korean guidance lines such as "맑은 채도 유지", "탁한 회색기 줄이기" where appropriate.
7. Layout anchor zone: {레이아웃} is interpreted as a structured split composition with portrait left and analysis content right, enhanced by small page indicators, a date/location label "서울 · 퍼스널 컬러 스튜디오", and decorative but practical note-card marks.
8. Tone treatment: {컬러 톤} subtly affects accent lines, swatch framing, title highlights, sticker tabs, and small dividers while keeping skin tone accuracy as the top priority.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard and Noto Sans KR combination, title in Bold 700–800 at large size, result text in SemiBold 700, body in Medium 500, swatch labels in 12–14px small Korean text, metadata in condensed editorial-style uppercase.
- Color palette: off-white #F4F0E6, warm beige #D8C7AE, coral pink #F2A7A0, peach #F7C8A5, ivory #FFF8EE, pale gold #D9BE7A, soft taupe #A9967D, plus {컬러 톤} accents.
- Border/shadow: thin 1px divider rules in soft taupe, portrait shadow 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity, layered paper shadows around labels and swatch cards, refined editorial separators rather than heavy framing.

- Background treatment: decorative card background built from {배경·심볼}, rendered as a refined symbolic scene with layered illustration, antique paper texture, small celestial marks, ornamental plants, tiny stars, moon phases, and subtle Korean minhwa-inspired motifs.
- Color direction: use {컬러} as the dominant palette, with restrained gold accents for borders, icons, title ornaments, tiny corner glyphs, and foil-like line details.
- Typography zones: top roman numeral area, bottom card-name area, small edition label, artist/model credit line, and tiny deck metadata should be readable and integrated into the card design.
- Apply {원본 보존} so the face remains recognizable while costume, environment, and symbolic accessories change to tarot-card styling.
- Respect {비율} while keeping the final composition aligned to the 1024x1536 vertical tarot card format.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top header band: place the Roman numeral and card identity at the top center with a thin ornamental divider, tiny moon/star glyphs, and a small edition label such as "ARCANA PORTRAIT DECK · VOL.07".
2. Central portrait zone: transform the subject into the selected tarot archetype from {카드 종류}, keeping the face realistic and identity-preserving while adapting clothing, hairstyle accents, hand pose, symbolic prop, and posture to match {카드 톤}.
3. Symbolic background layer: build the scene around {배경·심볼} as the primary narrative element, integrating it behind and around the figure so the symbolism reads instantly through layered icons, atmospheric illustrated depth, and meaningful objects near the hands or shoulders.
4. Card frame details: add a refined border inspired by tarot decks, with fine linework, corner flourishes, inner rule lines, tiny constellation dots, small Korean decorative knots, and selective gold foil-like highlights.
5. Bottom title band: set the card name in Korean and English with balanced hierarchy, centered and separated from the artwork by a thin rule or decorative panel; include a small caption line using {카드 텍스트}.
6. Collector details: add believable printed-deck micro text such as "2026 한정판", "MODEL CREDIT · {카드 텍스트}", "ILLUSTRATED ARCANA SERIES", and a tiny production code like "NO. 014 / SEOUL" along the side or bottom edge.
7. Finish layer: make the surface look like a polished printed tarot card with subtle paper grain, slight ink misregistration at the edges, delicate vellum wear, controlled contrast, and realistic tactile thickness.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard Bold or Noto Sans KR Bold for the Korean title, with small-cap style Roman numeral treatment above; secondary labels can use Noto Serif KR or a classic serif similar to Cormorant Garamond for an antique tarot feel.
- Render short Korean card details clearly, for example: "2026 한정판", "오늘의 아르카나", "운명의 초상", "서울 에디션", and "MODEL · {카드 텍스트}" where appropriate.
- Color palette: base the design on {컬러}, with deep black or charcoal for text, parchment cream for title panels, and metallic gold accents used on borders, icons, title dividers, and symbolic ornaments.
- Border/shadow: use a thin decorative frame with a soft printed-card shadow, about 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 18% opacity, plus subtle paper-edge thickness and natural tabletop-like contact shadow if the card is shown as an object.
- Surface finish: antique paper texture, lightly worn but elegant, with a premium art-print look, gentle gold foil impression, and visible print grain in the illustration.
- Costume and props: add archetype-specific garments, jewelry, hand-held symbol, embroidered trim, charm strings, or celestial accessories that naturally fit {카드 종류} without covering the face.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: portrait reference interpreted like a studio fashion portrait on a 85mm f/1.8 lens, then translated into illustrated tarot-card composition; keep facial proportions natural and undistorted.
- Lighting: soft studio key light from upper-left at 45°, gentle fill from front-right, and a faint rim highlight to separate the figure from the symbolic background.
- Color grade: muted tarot illustration grade with indigo, burgundy, gold, cream, and deep green control points, plus a subtle aged-vellum warmth.
- Rendering: high-quality semi-realistic illustration with painterly facial detail, crisp printed typography, layered ink lines, and authentic collectible-card material texture.

[6. MOOD]
Premium mystical tarot deck art — vintage Rider-Waite meets Korean minhwa-inspired collectible card design, with a personal portrait-card feeling and the tactile realism of a limited-edition printed deck.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- The source face from {참고 이미지} should occupy the center of each cell with consistent crop and face scale, keeping the head silhouette readable across the full grid.
- Grid structure uses {그리드} with equal gutters; thin white dividing lines separate panels cleanly while allowing the artwork to feel like a printed silkscreen sheet.
- Preserve facial shape and identity through {원본 보존}, while swapping color relationships per panel using {컬러 페어링}.
- Use {배경} behind each face, including flat color fields, halftone dots, ink misregistration marks, and small screenprint texture accents that support the pop-art mood.
- Maintain {비율} framing as a square poster layout with the portrait grid as the dominant element, plus a compact exhibition information band integrated along the bottom or one outer edge.
- Add small decorative print details such as registration crosses, edition numbering, tiny color swatches, and a subtle ticket-stub graphic so the piece feels like a real pop-art event poster.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Panel layout: arrange the image as a precise grid of identical portrait crops, with each cell aligned to the same eye-line and head position for a poster-like rhythm.
- Face treatment: apply {처리} to simplify skin, hair, lips, and shadows into bold graphic planes while preserving recognizable likeness.
- Color variation: assign {컬러 페어링} across cells so each panel feels distinct but still part of one cohesive pop-art set.
- Separation rules: use thin white lines between cells and keep the gutters even, while allowing small print marks or caption strips outside the facial areas.
- Poster information band: include {포스터 제목}, {전시 날짜}, {장소}, {관람 정보}, {스폰서}, and {에디션 표기} in a clean Korean exhibition-poster layout.
- Poster finish: keep the entire composition flat, high-contrast, print-ready, and screenprint-like, with visible ink texture rather than photographic depth.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use bold sans-serif typography such as Helvetica Neue, Pretendard Bold, or Sandoll Gothic Neo; main title around 44–72 px equivalent, info text around 18–28 px equivalent, small edition notes around 12–16 px equivalent.
- Korean text should be sharp, readable, and intentionally placed as exhibition-poster text, not random background filler.
- Color palette: use saturated pop-art colors inspired by Marilyn Monroe-era Andy Warhol tones, including hot pink, tangerine orange, cobalt blue, lemon yellow, mint green, magenta, black, and white.
- Graphic details: allow halftone patterns, risograph grain, offset-print imperfections, ink bleed, registration crosses, small starbursts, price/ticket blocks, and color-test bars.
- Border/shadow: use thin 2–4 px white grid dividers, crisp black outlines, and subtle ink-edge separation where needed for facial clarity.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: source-photo look should feel like a straight-on studio portrait, 85mm f/2.0 equivalent framing, cropped tightly to the face for a classic headshot source.
- Lighting: even frontal studio light with low contrast, similar to a clean portrait reference used for silkscreen conversion; avoid dramatic side shadows.
- Color grade: vivid primary-and-secondary pop-art grading with flat ink-like fills, crisp black accents, bright posterized saturation, and screenprint paper texture.
- Material feel: matte exhibition-poster paper, slightly imperfect ink registration, tactile halftone dots, and clean vector-like facial outlines.

[6. MOOD]
Andy Warhol screenprint exhibition print — high-impact Pop Art gallery wall aesthetic with a classic Marilyn Monroe homage, updated as a contemporary Korean pop-art poster with playful event details.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: render the poster title exactly as “{포스터 제목}”.
- Render event details clearly: “{전시 날짜}”, “{장소}”, “{관람 정보}”, “{스폰서}”, and “{에디션 표기}”.

- The same person’s identity must remain recognizable in every panel.
- Each panel should show the face with consistent crop, perspective, and alignment.
- Keep the grid structure exact and evenly spaced.

- Broken Korean characters

K-drama character scene transformation from an attached portrait into a cinematic vertical still. Preserve the subject identity while re-styling wardrobe, environment, color, lighting, and small in-world details to match a specific drama mood.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Place the attached subject as the central hero in a vertical 1024x1536 frame, with the face and identity clearly preserved and the upper body occupying about 60% of the canvas.
- Use {원본 보존} as the identity rule for facial likeness, pose continuity, expression, skin tone, age impression, and natural proportions.

- Shape the emotional read with {장면 무드}, keeping the composition cinematic, story-rich, and grounded rather than poster-like.
- Apply {비율·구도} with layered foreground and background depth: a believable location, practical lights, textured surfaces, and a few narrative objects that support the character’s situation without overwhelming the face.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Portrait conversion layer: keep the original face structure, gaze direction, expression continuity, hairstyle logic, and skin tone continuity intact, while reinterpreting clothing and surrounding set elements to fit the selected drama world.
- Wardrobe layer: redesign the outfit to match {드라마 톤}, with realistic fabric textures, seams, folds, buttons, knit grain, coat lapels, uniform details, jewelry, watch, bag strap, scarf, or ID lanyard when appropriate; avoid costume-like exaggeration.
- Background layer: replace the original background with a drama-appropriate location that supports {장면 무드}, such as a rain-glossed Seoul alley, hospital corridor, law office archive room, police interview room, late-night convenience store, rooftop garden, subway platform, warm family restaurant, or emotionally tense apartment interior.
- Environmental detail layer: add believable Korean drama set dressing — wet pavement reflections, fluorescent ceiling panels, elevator signs, frosted glass doors, bulletin boards, files, coffee cups, umbrella stand, receipts, phone screen glow, wall clocks, framed family photos, handwritten notes, restaurant menus, street posters, or distant city lights depending on {드라마 톤}.
- In-world Korean text layer: if signage or props are visible, use short, fully legible Korean such as “진료실”, “회의실”, “오늘의 메뉴”, “출입문”, “새벽 2:13”, “서울역 방면”, or a phone notification like “부재중 전화 3통”; text must feel like part of the scene, not a graphic overlay.
- Lighting layer: use {라이팅} to create depth, separation, and film still realism, with controlled highlights, practical light sources, realistic reflections, and believable shadow falloff across the face, wardrobe, and background.
- Color layer: grade the full image using {컬러 톤}, ensuring the palette feels consistent across skin, wardrobe, props, signage, and background surfaces.
- Final polish layer: keep the frame cinematic and grounded, with seamless subject integration, natural lens behavior, realistic micro-texture, believable hair edges, and no over-sharpened compositing artifacts.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: do not turn the image into a poster or advertisement. Any text should appear as real set text, signage, phone UI, receipt print, name tag, elevator label, menu board, folder tab, or a tiny production-still style timestamp; use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR in medium weight when text is designed, and keep it naturally scaled.
- Color palette: derive the look from {컬러 톤}, but ground it with realistic drama-frame neutrals such as charcoal #2B2B2B, muted beige #D8CBB8, deep red #7A1F1F, cold gray-blue #7E8A97, warm tungsten #C79A62, rain-black asphalt #151719, and soft paper white #E8E1D5 when applicable.
- Texture and set dressing: include tactile surfaces such as wool, cotton, leather, glass, polished metal, rain droplets, paper grain, scuffed walls, wooden table edges, tiled floors, venetian blinds, or translucent curtains to make the still feel photographed on location.
- Framing and depth: use natural cinematic shadow separation, foreground occlusion if appropriate, subtle reflection layers, and a believable spatial relationship between the subject and environment.
- Facial realism: retain natural pores, fine hair strands, eye highlights, expression nuance, and asymmetry from the reference image; beautification must remain drama-realistic, not plastic or airbrushed.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: full-frame 85mm portrait lens look, f/1.8 to f/2.8, vertical cinematic framing, shallow but believable depth separation, realistic compression, natural edge falloff, and a still-frame quality similar to a high-end Korean television production.
- Lighting: cinematic film lighting with controlled side key and subtle fill, such as a 45° key from camera-left, gentle negative fill on the shadow side, practical lights in the background, and a faint rim light for separation.
- Color grade: apply drama-grade tonal treatment inspired by prestige Korean television stills — either desaturated tension, warm domestic glow, cool urban nocturne, elegant legal-drama neutrality, or melancholic rain-night contrast depending on {드라마 톤}.
- Image realism: allow authentic imperfections such as slight lens breathing, soft background signage, mild skin sheen, reflected neon, fabric lint, dust in practical light, subtle motion from passing traffic, and natural background extras blurred in depth when they support the scene.

[6. MOOD]
Prestige K-drama still — a frame you might expect from a high-end Korean series like Squid Game, Parasite, Goblin, or Extraordinary Attorney Woo, with cinematic realism, emotional clarity, lived-in Korean locations, and enough narrative detail to imply a larger scene before and after this moment.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: any visible Korean must be fully legible and correctly rendered without broken characters. Suitable short in-scene examples include “진료실”, “오늘의 메뉴”, “회의실”, “서울역 방면”, “부재중 전화 3통”, “새벽 2:13”, “예약석”, or “출입문”.
- Preserve the attached subject’s identity exactly: face, age impression, expression continuity, gaze, hairstyle logic, skin tone, and natural anatomy must remain consistent with the original photo.
- Keep the scene photorealistic and frame-like, with believable wardrobe, lighting, props, signage, reflections, shadows, and set integration.
- The added environment must support {드라마 톤}, {장면 무드}, {컬러 톤}, {라이팅}, and {비율·구도} without changing the core subject or making the image feel like an advertisement.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized celebrity likeness

[1. PURPOSE]
Seasonal concept portrait for SNS profile / display use, transforming the attached person into a Halloween, Christmas, Valentine, or other seasonal mood scene.
Maintain the original identity from the reference while shifting costume styling, room atmosphere, seasonal props, small profile-card text, and color story to match the selected season.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: {원본 보존} stays clearly recognizable, occupying the central portrait area with a tall 1024x1536 vertical profile-card composition.
- Seasonal styling: apply {시즌 컨셉} as the visible costume or theme layer, while preserving facial likeness, age impression, expression, and overall pose continuity.
- Background treatment: build {배경·소품} as a believable season-specific environment with layered foreground, midground, and background details such as candles, fabric, ornaments, gift boxes, roses, handwritten notes, party ribbons, or seasonal table objects.
- Color direction: drive the overall palette with {컬러 톤}, keeping skin tones natural and letting costume, props, and background accents carry the seasonal identity.
- Lighting direction: shape the scene with {라이팅} in a photographic way, including realistic catchlights, soft shadow falloff, and gentle reflections on glossy props.
- Profile-card overlay: add small, tasteful Korean text elements integrated into the image — {프로필 라벨}, {촬영 날짜}, {촬영 장소}, {한줄 캡션}, and {장식 태그} — placed like a modern SNS profile story card.
- Format: tall vertical upper-body portrait optimized for social media display, with enough visible styling around the subject to clearly communicate the season.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Foreground subject: render {원본 보존} as the sharpest element, with season-appropriate clothing, hair accessories, makeup tone, jewelry, and facial expression aligned to {시즌 컨셉}.
- Foreground props: include tactile seasonal details near the hands or lower frame, such as a pumpkin basket, candle holder, velvet ribbon, ornament, wrapped gift, rose bouquet, cocoa mug, heart-shaped card, or themed fabric texture depending on the season.
- Midground styling: place {배경·소품} around the subject as believable set dressing — for Halloween, carved pumpkins, taper candles, antique lace, paper bats, dried branches; for Christmas, warm fairy lights, pine garlands, ornaments, gift boxes; for Valentine, roses, satin ribbons, handwritten love notes, soft pink stationery.
- Background layer: use a photographic room, studio corner, party setup, decorated window area, or atmospheric seasonal backdrop in the tones of {컬러 톤}, with realistic depth and perspective.
- Text layer: render Korean profile-card details clearly: top small label “{프로필 라벨}”, date “{촬영 날짜}”, location “{촬영 장소}”, caption “{한줄 캡션}”, and tag line “{장식 태그}”. Text should feel printed, overlaid, or lightly embossed as part of a polished SNS story layout.
- Lighting layer: apply {라이팅} so highlights, shadows, fabric texture, candle glow, ornament reflections, and skin tone feel physically consistent with the chosen season and props.
- Finishing layer: use editorial retouching with natural skin texture, clean hair detail, realistic fabric folds, crisp seasonal objects, and a polished profile-photo finish.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use legible Korean micro-typography for the profile-card elements; combine a clean sans-serif label with one small handwritten-style accent for the caption or tag.
- Text placement: keep text integrated into the composition as a real SNS profile/story card detail, not as a large advertisement headline.
- Color palette: use the exact seasonal palette from {컬러 톤}, anchored by deep neutrals, warm accent tones, and restrained highlight colors.
- Seasonal realism: props should look physically present in the scene, with matching shadows, reflections, material textures, and scale relative to the person.
- Portrait priority: the subject’s face remains the emotional center while surrounding decorations, labels, and props provide context and seasonal richness.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: full-frame 85mm portrait lens at f/1.8 to f/2.8 for a natural subject-first seasonal portrait, or 50mm f/1.8 if a slightly wider upper-body framing is needed.
- Lighting: cinematic mixed light based on {라이팅} — for Halloween, candle-like warm key light with faint cool fill; for Christmas, soft tree-light sparkle with gentle window fill; for Valentine, diffused pink ambient light with a soft frontal key.
- Color grade: season-specific photographic grading with controlled contrast, realistic skin tone, and palette shifts toward {컬러 톤} rather than neon saturation.
- Texture: preserve visible fabric grain, hair strands, subtle makeup detail, paper texture on cards, wax texture on candles, glass shine on ornaments, and natural background depth.

[6. MOOD]
Editorial seasonal portrait — like a Vogue Korea holiday photoshoot mixed with a high-end lifestyle campaign and a polished SNS profile story card, festive, cinematic, personal, and realistic.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: render exactly readable Korean where used: “{프로필 라벨}”, “{촬영 날짜}”, “{촬영 장소}”, “{한줄 캡션}”, “{장식 태그}”.
- Identity constraint: {원본 보존} must remain clearly recognizable; preserve facial structure, age impression, and key likeness cues from the reference image.
- Layout invariant: the seasonal theme, props, lighting, and profile-card text must support the portrait without changing the person into a different identity.
- Realism invariant: costume, accessories, background items, and small text overlays must share the same photographic lighting and perspective.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / government certification marks
- Broken or unreadable Korean characters
- Celebrity face composites or unauthorized celebrity likeness blending

[1. PURPOSE]
Create an i2i social photo edit that turns one attached selfie into a believable AI friend-group portrait. Vertical phone-camera look for a casual social media post, with the warmth and minor imperfections of a real weekend snapshot: close faces, overlapping shoulders, small cafe props, urban background details, and a subtle story-style date/location caption.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject placement: keep the original person(s) as the visual anchor in the center 55% of the frame, with added friends distributed naturally to left and right so the group reads as a real clustered selfie.
- Background treatment: {장면} as a lived-in Korean urban setting with shallow depth, visible cafe terrace texture, small shop signs, glass reflections, street railings, menu boards, plants, and passing-light ambience.
- Spacing and framing: frame tightly from chest-up to half-body, with slight headroom, overlapping shoulders, partial arms near the edge, and asymmetrical spacing that feels handheld rather than staged.
- Identity handling: preserve {원본 보존} while expanding the scene into {합성 모드} without changing the core facial identity.
- Pose direction: use {포즈} so the group feels spontaneous, friendly, and slightly chaotic like a real group selfie.
- Social-post layer: add a small translucent mobile-story style location/date sticker and caption that does not cover faces, using the exact Korean text from {날짜 라벨}, {위치 라벨}, {캡션}, and {친구 태그}.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Hero cluster (center 60%): place the original selfie subject(s) as the focal point, with 3–4 believable companions integrated at matching perspective and eye level, each with distinct but harmonized styling such as denim jacket, knit cardigan, ball cap, soft bangs, layered hair, hoop earrings, or casual streetwear.
- Left side support: add one friend slightly behind the front row, leaning in toward the camera with a relaxed smile, matching the same lens distortion, skin-tone response, and daylight direction.
- Right side support: add another friend closer to the foreground edge, using a natural hand gesture or V sign, while keeping fingers anatomically correct and proportional.
- Foreground details: include realistic everyday objects such as {소품}, a phone strap, tote bag edge, sunglasses on a head, hair clip, paper cup sleeve, or cafe table corner to make the scene feel inhabited.
- Background environment: render {장면} with real street or cafe details, including Korean storefront lettering, terrace chairs, menu board fragments, warm window reflections, concrete wall texture, and small plants.
- Facial continuity: maintain the original person’s likeness from {원본 보존}, while varying clothing colors, hairstyles, makeup intensity, and expressions across the added people to make the group feel organic.
- Atmospheric finish: apply {라이팅} with subtle skin highlights, gentle shadow roll-off, realistic phone-photo contrast, slight motion softness on hair or hands, and natural catchlights.
- Canvas balance: keep the composition vertically weighted for {비율}, with the faces occupying the upper-middle area and the caption/sticker elements sitting near the top-left or lower third like a real social upload.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: render the Korean overlay text cleanly in a casual mobile UI sans-serif style. Use {위치 라벨} and {날짜 라벨} in small rounded translucent pills, with {캡션} and {친구 태그} near the lower third as a social post caption.
- Decorative micro details: add tiny mobile-social icons such as a heart, sparkle, pin marker, save/share glyph, or small white dot separators; keep them subtle and integrated into the phone-photo aesthetic.
- Color palette: use warm Portra-style neutrals, soft peach skin tones, muted denim blue, cafe beige, olive-gray environmental accents, creamy highlights, and soft black UI text/shadow accents; if any styling guide color is needed, anchor toward #E8D8C8, #C98E6B, #6E7A6A, and #2F2A28.
- Frame treatment: present as a full-bleed vertical social photo with natural handheld cropping, mild lens perspective, and realistic edge falloff; any overlay should feel like an in-app sticker rather than a poster layout.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: smartphone front-camera or 24mm equivalent wide-angle feel, f/2.0–f/2.8 look, with slight perspective stretch typical of an on-the-go group selfie.
- Lighting: {라이팅}, with soft directional daylight from upper-left or front-left, mild ambient bounce from surrounding walls, gentle highlights on cheeks and hair, and realistic cafe-window reflections.
- Color grade: Kodak Portra 400-inspired warmth with gentle highlight roll-off, slightly lifted shadows, restrained saturation for skin-friendly realism, and a faint casual film-grain texture.

[6. MOOD]
Candid Korean friend-group social photo — the relaxed, documentary-like energy of a genuine weekend meetup snapshot, with playful closeness, small personal accessories, real cafe-street atmosphere, and the feeling that someone quickly raised a phone and captured the moment.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: render exactly these visible Korean text elements: "{날짜 라벨}", "{위치 라벨}", "{캡션}", "{친구 태그}". Keep the letters sharp, correctly spelled, and not cut off.
- Identity invariants: preserve the attached selfie identity from {원본 보존}; if multiple versions are created, they must remain clearly related as the same person with believable outfit, hairstyle, and expression variation.
- Anatomy/layout invariants: hands must be anatomically correct, exactly 5 fingers per hand, with no duplicated limbs, warped faces, melted teeth, or mismatched eye directions.
- Group realism: all faces must align to a consistent camera angle, lens distortion, scale, and lighting direction so the photo reads as one coherent shot.
- Overlay placement: sticker labels and caption must stay secondary to the faces, placed in safe areas with enough contrast for readability.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters or misspelled Korean overlay text
- Celebrity composites or implying a real public figure is present
- Unwanted identity swap of the reference person

[1. PURPOSE]
Photoreal custom merchandise mockup sheet for personal brand use, arranged as a rich multi-product presentation for online shop listings, social sharing, and portfolio display.
Show one consistent {원본 디자인} applied across apparel, drinkware, phone accessory, keychain, and the selected {굿즈 종류}, with realistic packaging details and shop-ready labeling.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main composition: follow {레이아웃} as a polished 2x3 or 3x2 merchandise board filling the full vertical canvas, with product tiles arranged like a real boutique catalog shoot.
- Subject placement: each mockup sits on a tactile tabletop or paper backdrop, with the hero product slightly above center and supporting items angled naturally to show depth, scale, and material finish.
- Background treatment: {배경 톤} with seamless studio surface, subtle paper grain, matte tabletop texture, soft grounding shadows, and realistic contact shadows beneath every object.
- Framing direction: straight-on product presentation with controlled perspective, suitable for e-commerce while still feeling like an actual photographed brand sample kit.
- Brand label zone: include a refined header or footer card for {브랜드 이름}, plus small shop metadata such as ‘굿즈 샘플팩’, ‘NEW DROP’, ‘VOL.01’, ‘2026.05’, ‘SKU GD-0526’, and a tiny barcode-style price label.
- Realistic set dressing: include tasteful production details such as folded tissue paper, a small kraft hangtag, color swatch chips matching {컬러 톤}, a thin packing slip edge, clear acrylic keychain reflections, and a small care-label card without hiding the products.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Top row / left tile: a photoreal T-shirt mockup showing {원본 디자인} printed crisply on the chest area, with visible cotton weave, natural fabric folds, collar seam, sleeve hems, inner neck label, and a small hangtag reading ‘프리오더’ or ‘COTTON 100%’.
- Top row / center tile: a ceramic mug mockup with {원본 디자인} wrapped naturally around the curved surface, handle visible, ceramic lip thickness, glossy highlights, faint reflection on the tabletop, and a small coaster or product sticker nearby reading ‘머그 350ml’.
- Top row / right tile: a phone case mockup featuring {원본 디자인} centered on the back panel, accurate camera cutout, realistic edge thickness, satin or glossy plastic finish, and a tiny packaging sleeve label reading ‘PHONE CASE’ and ‘₩18,000’.
- Bottom row / left tile: a keychain mockup with {원본 디자인} scaled to fit the small surface cleanly, metal ring, clasp, acrylic or enamel material rendered with real reflections, and a backing card marked ‘키링 굿즈’.
- Bottom row / center tile: an extra product tile from {굿즈 종류}, styled as part of the same drop, with matching print placement, material-specific reflections, a small price tag, and packaging detail.
- Bottom row / right tile: a brand information tile using {브랜드 이름}, styled like a real shop insert card with Korean microcopy such as ‘굿즈 세트’, ‘한정 제작’, ‘배송 안내’, ‘@brand.shop’, a tiny barcode block, item code, and contact-style line ‘서울 작업실 제작’.
- Across all tiles: apply the same {원본 디자인} consistently, with matching color response and realistic material interaction across fabric, ceramic, plastic, acrylic, enamel, paper, and metal.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for label text, medium to semibold weight, 24–48px equivalent for the brand name and 10–18px equivalent for shop metadata, with precise Korean typesetting and believable print alignment.
- Color palette: base the sheet on {컬러 톤}, with neutral white #FFFFFF, soft beige #F4EFE6, charcoal #2B2B2B, muted gray #D9D9D9, and one or two small accent swatches derived from the design.
- Border/shadow: use soft product-card shadows, natural contact shadows, paper overlaps, thin printed dividers, and subtle corner radius where appropriate, matching a premium stationery-and-merch presentation.
- Surface finish: mix matte paper, cotton fabric, glazed ceramic, satin phone-case plastic, reflective metal rings, and clear acrylic highlights so each object feels physically distinct.
- Layout details: include small readable Korean labels such as ‘신상품’, ‘제작 샘플’, ‘옵션 선택’, ‘패키지 포함’, ‘₩7,500’, and ‘2026년 5월 제작’ only where they enhance the catalog realism.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: professional product photography look, equivalent to a Canon EOS R5 with a 50mm lens for the overall grid and a 85mm perspective feel for individual product clarity, f/8 to keep all product edges sharp.
- Lighting: large diffused studio softbox from upper-left at about 45°, very light fill from the right, gentle bounce under each item, and controlled specular highlights on ceramic, acrylic, plastic, and metal.
- Color grade: clean neutral whites with gentle warm beige balance, natural material colors preserved, slight contrast lift for catalog clarity, realistic print ink density, and no artificial cinematic tint.

[6. MOOD]
Premium e-commerce merchandise catalog with the warmth of a real maker studio sample shoot — refined, tactile, shop-ready, and personal-brand focused, like a curated Shopify product launch image or a boutique stationery brand drop.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: render {브랜드 이름} correctly if shown as text, and render added Korean labels accurately, including ‘굿즈 세트’, ‘신상품’, ‘제작 샘플’, ‘한정 제작’, ‘배송 안내’, ‘키링 굿즈’, ‘머그 350ml’, ‘프리오더’, and ‘2026년 5월 제작’.
- All mockups must share the same {원본 디자인} and maintain realistic product proportions.
- Each product tile must remain photorealistic, with correct reflections, folds, seams, shadows, print distortion, and edge geometry for the specific material.
- Keep shop details secondary to the merchandise: labels, barcode blocks, hangtags, packaging sleeves, and swatches should support the product story without covering {원본 디자인}.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

Transform the attached portrait photo into a richly detailed MBTI character-style editorial profile poster while preserving the person’s identity and facial features. [2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Subject placement: the original person stays as the central hero, occupying about 65% of the frame, with headroom of 8–10% and a natural upper-body crop that shows posture, hands, and a hint of clothing texture.
- Identity preservation: keep {원본 보존} exactly, including face shape, hairstyle, skin tone, age impression, distinctive features, and overall proportions from the source image.
- Character direction: express {MBTI} through pose, expression, hand gesture, desk objects, small personal items, and the emotional tone of {캐릭터 무드} without changing the person’s core appearance.
- Background treatment: place the character in a softly lit window-side desk scene with a pale paper-texture wall, muted wood desk surface, warm window reflections, stationery, a small plant, layered books, postcards, tape pieces, pens, and natural lifestyle details from {배경·소품}.
- Framing: use a vertical social-profile poster/card layout with a designed information zone near the lower or side area, allowing the MBTI label and small editorial notes to feel integrated with the portrait.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Portrait hero area (center 65%): convert the source person into a refined MBTI character illustration, keeping the original identity intact while adding subtle expressive styling aligned with {캐릭터 무드}; preserve realistic facial structure, believable skin shading, and recognizable hair flow.
- Scene layer (rear 25%): build a lived-in desk-by-window environment using {배경·소품}, with layered depth: window frame, curtain edge, pinned memo cards, calendar scrap, wooden desk grain, books, a notebook opened to handwritten Korean notes, and a small ceramic cup.
- Foreground lifestyle details: add books, notebook, flowers, tea cup, pencil, paper clips, phone charm, small sticker sheets, and one folded receipt or photo strip near the desk edge; keep these naturally scaled so the face remains the emotional focal point.
- MBTI profile label area: render {MBTI 라벨} as a refined editorial text panel, paired with small Korean microcopy such as "오늘의 성향", "PROFILE NO. 016", "2026.05.01", "서울의 오후", and a short caption line like "나다운 선택이 가장 좋은 답".

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard SemiBold or Noto Sans KR Bold for {MBTI 라벨}, 28–36px equivalent on 1024x1536, with crisp anti-aliased Korean text, balanced tracking, and readable hierarchy.
- Supporting typography: use smaller Korean captions in Pretendard Regular, 12–18px equivalent, including "오늘의 성향", "나다운 선택이 가장 좋은 답", "2026.05.01", "서울의 오후", "@my.mbti.note", and "01 / 04" where appropriate.

- Surface texture: subtle cotton-paper, fine matte illustration grain, lightly visible desk wood grain, paper fibers, fabric texture on clothing, ceramic cup texture, and soft ink edges; avoid glossy plastic rendering.
- Detail realism: Korean text should look intentionally designed and printed or handwritten, with real spacing, consistent baseline alignment, and plausible card-layout proportions.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]

[6. MOOD]
Editorial MBTI character portrait — a warm indie stationery-brand profile card with the softness of a lifestyle magazine spread, the intimacy of a personal journal page, and the polished charm of a modern Korean social-profile poster.

- The rendered result must clearly communicate {MBTI} through pose, props, microcopy, color mood, and the selected {캐릭터 무드}.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Full-screen smartphone profile UI fills the frame vertically, with a realistic status bar and app header at the top, the profile header occupying the top 26%, the bio and stats block 18%, highlights 13%, tab/navigation area 4%, and the 3x3 grid preview filling the lower 39%.
- Background is a real mobile app canvas in warm white with subtle gray separators, native UI chrome, tiny status indicators, bottom navigation icons, and screen-capture-like precision so the interface feels authentic.
- Place {아이디·이름} prominently in the profile header, {자기소개} directly beneath it, {팔로워·팔로잉} in the stats row, {9그리드 컨셉} across the nine-post preview, and {하이라이트 5개} as five circular highlight icons under the bio area.
- Include realistic Instagram profile details: top status bar time “오전 9:41”, Wi‑Fi/battery icons, username handle line, small “프로필 편집” and “공유하기” pill buttons, tiny add-person icon, grid/reels/tagged tab icons, save/share/heart/comment micro icons visible within selected feed thumbnails, and a bottom nav row.

- Keep the profile content aligned to a centered mobile column and left-aligned text blocks following standard Instagram spacing, with realistic density and readable UI hierarchy.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Top header area: show a native app status bar, a top username row with {아이디·이름}, a down-chevron, notification/menu icons, and an avatar circle on the left with a warm lifestyle portrait-style thumbnail or soft abstract profile photo.
2) Identity block: beside and beneath the avatar, show {아이디·이름} as the main identity line, a small handle-style variant beginning with “@”, the category label “디지털 크리에이터”, and compact action buttons labeled “프로필 편집”, “공유하기”, and a small person-add icon button.
3) Bio block: set {자기소개} under the name in two to three natural short lines, with realistic line breaks, secondary gray text, link-style blue-gray text, location pin text, and hashtag-like descriptors that look native to a Korean influencer profile.
4) Stats row: render {팔로워·팔로잉} as a balanced numeric row with bold counts and lighter labels, using the exact proportions of a mobile social app profile; include “게시물”, “팔로워”, and “팔로잉” labels clearly.

7) Micro UI details: add tab icons above the grid, a thin active-tab underline, tiny carousel/reels markers on appropriate thumbnails, small like/comment/save glyphs on one or two visible post tiles, and a bottom navigation bar with home/search/create/reels/profile icons.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for the UI text, with semibold for the username, regular for bio text, medium-bold for counts, and compact caption-weight text for hashtags and micro labels; size hierarchy should mimic a real phone app profile screen.
- Color palette: pure white #FFFFFF, soft gray #E9E9E9, medium gray #8E8E93, charcoal #1C1C1E, warm beige #DCCCB8, sage #B8C6B1, muted sand #CBB89D, soft cream #F7F2EA, and subtle link blue-gray #57758A.

- Photo-tile treatment: each grid image should feel like a real smartphone lifestyle photo, with natural shadows, fabric texture, ceramic cups, paper grain, street signage blur, mirror reflections, and warm daylight color consistency.
- UI realism: preserve native app spacing, tap-target proportions, icon scale, status bar alignment, and bottom navigation balance; text should look rendered by an actual mobile interface rather than placed as poster typography.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]

- Lighting: evenly lit digital screen presentation with a matte device-screen feel, soft ambient realism in the embedded photo thumbnails, and no harsh reflections or glare hotspots over legible UI text.
- Color grade: neutral white interface with warm beige and muted sage accents, softened contrast, natural photo warmth, and subtle lifestyle editorial cohesion.
- Detail rendering: high-resolution Korean UI text, clean vector-like icons, crisp gutters, realistic thumbnail imagery, and small but legible micro labels such as “게시물”, “릴스”, “태그됨”, “프로필 편집”, “공유하기”, “저장”, and “공유”.

Premium social-media brand identity mockup — calm Korean lifestyle influencer page with an Aesop-inspired warm beige and sage aesthetic, but with enough native UI density, feed variety, captions, hashtags, and micro-interactions to feel like a real active Instagram profile screenshot.

[1. PURPOSE]
Create a vertical smartphone chat screenshot mockup that looks like a real KakaoTalk conversation, suitable for social posts, meme-style storytelling, UI realism tests, or fictional chat-based content.
Make it read like an actual mobile messenger capture with believable status bar details, conversation rhythm, timestamps, read marks, and a functional input area.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Full-screen smartphone chat UI fills the entire 1024x1536 vertical frame as a direct app screenshot.
- Top status bar and header area occupy about 12% of the frame, showing {휴대폰 상태바}, the profile/name bar with {대화 상대}, a small profile circle, participant count if appropriate, and standard chat controls.
- Main conversation area occupies the central 72%, with alternating message bubbles arranged vertically, natural gaps between message groups, and believable scrolling position.
- Bottom input area occupies about 16%, including a text input field, plus button, emoji/sticker button, voice or send icon, and {입력창 문구} as placeholder text.
- Background treatment: KakaoTalk-style yellow chat background with subtle UI layering, date chips, small gray system labels, and app-native separators.
- Add realistic chat-room microdetails such as a pinned notice strip, small unread counters, delivery/read indicators, and one or two tiny sticker-style reactions when called for by {이모티콘·반응}.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Status bar: render {휴대폰 상태바} at the very top with believable phone UI icons, battery, signal, Wi-Fi, and current time in small Korean-friendly system UI styling.
2. Header area: render a realistic KakaoTalk-style top bar with the contact name {대화 상대}, a small profile circle, back arrow, search icon, menu icon, and soft separator line.
3. Room notice: include {채팅방 안내} as a slim in-chat notice or pinned banner under the header, using compact gray text and a small speaker/pin icon.
4. Conversation body: place {대화 내용} as alternating left/right chat bubbles, with the sender side visually distinct and the self messages right-aligned in yellow-tinted or white app-style bubbles depending on the selected UI tone.
5. Timestamp placement: show {시간·날짜} in small gray UI text centered between message groups, matching normal messenger spacing and weight.
6. Reaction details: insert {이모티콘·반응} naturally within the flow of the conversation, with tiny emoji-sized stickers, tap reactions, or read receipts placed next to the relevant bubbles.
7. Bottom composer: render {입력창 문구} inside the message input field, plus attachment/emoji icons and a send/mic button, so the screenshot feels like a live chat screen rather than a cropped static image.
8. UI realism layer: use faithful KakaoTalk-like proportions, bubble corner radii, padding, line breaks, small time labels beside bubbles, and realistic vertical scroll continuity.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use a clean Korean system UI look similar to Pretendard or Apple SD Gothic Neo, medium weight for names and regular weight for messages, with small timestamp text around 12–14px and body text around 26–32px in screen scale.
- Color palette: Kakao yellow #FEE500, white #FFFFFF, light gray #F2F2F2, medium gray #8E8E93, deep text black #111111, plus soft system-blue or muted gray accents for icons when useful.
- Bubble styling: rounded message bubbles with natural padding, accurate tail-less Kakao-style geometry, small gray time marks beside bubbles, and read labels such as “읽음” or “1” placed at realistic baseline height.
- Header styling: compact mobile UI bar, profile thumbnail as a simple believable avatar, Korean name text aligned with app conventions, and icon spacing that feels touch-friendly.
- Microcopy styling: date chips, notice text, unread counters, and input placeholder should look like real app UI text rather than headline typography.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: simulated screen capture, straight-on orthographic presentation, no perspective distortion, no photographic lens look.
- Lighting: flat digital UI appearance with crisp pixel-like clarity and app-native color rendering.
- Color grade: accurate app-screenshot color balance, saturated Kakao yellow with neutral whites and clean grayscale UI accents.
- Rendering quality: sharp vector-like interface edges, legible Korean glyphs, consistent baseline alignment, and screenshot-level precision.

[6. MOOD]
Authentic mobile messenger screenshot realism — casual, immediate, and believable, like a fictional KakaoTalk chat captured during an everyday conversation.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문자열이 화면에 정확히 보여야 함:
  - {대화 상대}
  - {대화 내용}
  - {시간·날짜}
  - {이모티콘·반응}
  - {휴대폰 상태바}
  - {채팅방 안내}
  - {입력창 문구}
- 화면 안에는 실제 메신저처럼 “읽음”, “1”, “오늘”, “공지” 같은 작은 UI 문구가 자연스럽게 포함되어도 좋음.
- All Korean characters must render sharply and correctly with no broken jamo, no missing spacing, and no accidental Latin replacements.
- Chat layout must follow real messaging app conventions: status bar at top, profile/name header, timestamps inline between message clusters, self messages right-aligned, other messages left-aligned, and composer bar at bottom.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity face composites or impersonation
- Real private phone numbers, addresses, or personal identifiers

studio:prompts3:ours-312.content:
[INPUT]
- reference_image: {참고 이미지}
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Create an i2i receipt-review composite where handwritten Korean feedback is naturally written over a real receipt, bill, or ticket photo for Instagram, blog, or diary use.
Keep the result as an authentic personal food-review memo: a photographed receipt with practical transaction details, quick pen marks, and believable everyday context rather than a promotional ad.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Base document fills the square frame: {원본 보존} is preserved as the underlying photographed paper, with receipt edges, folds, curled corners, thermal-print texture, small stains, and slight perspective remaining visible.
- Keep realistic receipt content visible: store name, order number, table or takeout label, itemized menu rows, prices, tax/total area, payment line, approval number, and a small barcode or QR-style payment block may remain or be reconstructed from the original reference if appropriate.
- Main annotation zone: the center and lower-middle area carry the handwritten review, while original item lines remain readable enough to feel like a real food receipt.
- Location/date line: place {가게·날짜} near the upper third or a naturally blank area of the receipt, aligned as if written quickly by hand with a real pen.
- Rating and short comment: {별점·메모} sits beside or slightly below the date line, sized larger than the rest so it reads as the emotional anchor.
- Recommendation marks: {추천 메뉴 표시} should appear directly on specific menu lines in the receipt, with circles, stars, arrows, check marks, or underlines drawn in pen ink only.
- Add small realistic review-memo details: a tiny handwritten “재방문 의사 있음”, “혼밥 추천”, or “다음엔 매운맛” note may be placed in the margin if it fits the receipt, without covering the required strings.
- Handwriting treatment: {손글씨 톤} should follow the paper perspective and real ink pressure, including slight stroke variation, tiny pen skips, uneven ink pooling, and natural hesitation marks.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Background layer — keep the photographed receipt, bill, or ticket intact, with visible paper fiber, thermal print density, fold shadows, thumb-smoothed creases, and natural contact shadows from the original capture.
2. Receipt information layer — maintain or enrich believable printed receipt details such as “어쩌면식당”, “주문번호 0429-17”, “테이블 3”, “김치볶음밥 8,500”, “바질크림파스타 13,000”, “오늘의 샐러드 6,500”, “합계 28,000원”, “카드 승인”, “VAT 포함”, and a small barcode/QR area near the bottom if the original layout supports it.
3. Header note area — write {가게·날짜} in a compact handwritten style near the top section, using a slight rightward slant and realistic pen start/stop marks.
4. Rating line — place {별점·메모} in the most readable open space, with the stars drawn as handwritten marks rather than typed glyphs.
5. Item emphasis layer — apply {추천 메뉴 표시} directly over the relevant printed menu rows, using hand-drawn circles, asterisks, arrows, or underline strokes that follow the receipt’s printed alignment and paper perspective.
6. Margin memo layer — include one or two tiny diary-like Korean side notes, such as “소스 진짜 맛있음”, “친구 데려오기”, or “점심 웨이팅 10분”, written smaller than the main rating to add realism.
7. Ink integration — render {손글씨 톤} as if written on the original paper, with subtle transparency variation where the paper is textured, folded, glossy, or shadowed.
8. Final composite check — ensure the handwritten elements feel physically attached to the document, not floating above it, and keep original receipt details legible enough to support authenticity.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: handwritten Korean only for added notes; emulate casual pen writing with medium stroke weight, irregular baseline, slight pressure variation, and human inconsistency rather than font-like perfection.
- Printed receipt text: monospaced thermal-receipt style with imperfect ink density, slight fading, tiny alignment shifts, and plausible Korean menu/price formatting.
- Color palette: paper whites and creams from {컬러 톤}, with black, deep blue, and small red receipt-print accents; keep ink saturated but naturally absorbed into the paper.
- Paper and environment: allow natural receipt aging, tabletop grain, faint food smudges, tiny oil spots, coffee-ring traces, clipped paper corners, and realistic edge shadows when present or visually appropriate.
- Composition polish: preserve the casual phone-photo feel, including slight skew, uneven paper flatness, and believable document texture.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: realistic smartphone document photo aesthetic, equivalent to a 26mm wide smartphone lens at f/1.8 with minimal distortion correction.
- Lighting: soft ambient indoor light from above-left, low contrast, with gentle shadow falloff and no harsh flash hotspot.
- Color grade: neutral paper white with slightly warm cream highlights, black ink, subdued red print accents, realistic blue or black pen marks, and restrained overall saturation.
- Detail rendering: high-resolution paper fibers, thermal print grain, subtle compression from a real phone image, and readable handwritten strokes at square social-media size.

[6. MOOD]
Everyday diary snapshot — feels like a real handwritten note made right after eating, photographed on a casual cafe or restaurant table, similar to a personal scrapbook food review rather than a commercial graphic.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문자열: "홍대 어쩌면식당", "2026.04.29", "★★★★★", "가성비 갑, 또 올게요".
- The required strings should appear as handwritten review text, naturally arranged as {가게·날짜} and {별점·메모}, with the star rating clearly readable.
- Optional printed receipt microtext may include realistic Korean details such as “주문번호 0429-17”, “테이블 3”, “합계 28,000원”, “카드 승인”, and menu item names, but it must not conflict with the required strings.
- Handwriting must remain readable and naturally imperfect, but the required Korean text strings must not be misspelled, duplicated incorrectly, or turned into broken characters.
- The handwritten marks must sit on top of the original receipt content in a physically plausible way, matching paper perspective, fold shadows, ink absorption, and pen contact.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
