[1. PURPOSE]
Mixed-media portrait editorial poster built from an input face photo, combining photography, hand-drawn illustration, collage paper, painterly overlays, and realistic magazine-cover publishing details.
Designed like a contemporary Korean art magazine cover / gallery zine page with a vertical editorial composition, printed texture, issue metadata, short feature blurbs, and collectible indie-publication realism.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Subject placement: {원본 보존} is the clear focal point, occupying about 55–65% of the frame, with the face slightly off-center so collage layers, cover typography, and paper fragments wrap naturally around the portrait.
- Pose direction: {포즈} with the head angle preserved naturally so the identity remains readable and the portrait still feels photographed before being remixed.
- Background treatment: {배경} fills the full canvas with visible paper grain, torn-edge accents, layered page fragments, taped corners, photocopy marks, faint registration crosses, and subtle overlapping magazine scraps.
- Editorial cover layout: build the image as a real zine/magazine cover with a masthead area at the top, issue number, date label, price, barcode block, model-name credit, small spine/credit text, and 2–3 short Korean feature headline blurbs arranged around the portrait.
- Layering and spacing: integrate textural marks, cut-paper shapes, paint splashes, and printed labels around the forehead, hair, shoulders, and side edges while keeping key facial features clear and expressive.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Base portrait layer: preserve the likeness from {원본 보존} cleanly, then blend it into an editorial mixed-media treatment without flattening facial structure.
- Line art layer: add hand-drawn contour lines around the jawline, nose bridge, cheek outline, eyelid crease, collar, and hair edge, using fine black ink strokes that look sketched on top of the photo.
- Mixed element layer: express {혼합 요소} through visible media combinations such as translucent tracing paper, kraft-paper scraps, risograph dots, handwritten arrows, masking tape strips, paint daubs, scanned fabric fibers, and sliced magazine typography.
- Collage layer: place irregular paper cutouts around the face and shoulder area, with torn magazine fragments overlapping the background edges, lightly crossing hair or clothing, and avoiding obstruction of the eyes or mouth.
- Paint layer: add controlled paint splashes, dry-brush marks, graphite smudges, and acrylic streaks in small clusters near the outer frame and one shoulder, especially along one side of the composition for asymmetry.
- Texture layer: overlay vintage magazine halftone, kraft paper fibers, ink bleed, small dust specks, misregistered print color, and slight print noise across the full poster, keeping the skin tones readable.
- Typography layer: embed {타이포} as part of the collage structure, mixed with realistic cover details such as “VOL.247”, “2026년 5월호”, “₩7,500”, “EDITORIAL NOTE”, and “MODEL CREDIT: 오늘의 얼굴”; make the typography feel cut, stamped, pasted, or printed rather than floating digitally.
- Feature blurbs: include 2–3 short Korean magazine lines, for example “나다운 결”, “종이 위의 초상”, “불완전한 아름다움”, set near the left/right margins or lower third as supporting cover copy.
- Barcode and credits: add a small barcode area near the lower corner with tiny catalog text, plus vertical spine-style micro text along one side reading “MIXED MEDIA PORTRAIT / SEOUL ART ZINE / ISSUE 247”.
- Color balance: apply {컬러 톤} consistently across the collage fragments, paint accents, typographic blocks, and background paper so the piece feels unified and print-authentic.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Noto Serif KR or Nanum Myeongjo style for Korean cover text, plus a condensed serif like Cormorant Garamond for English accents; combine 400–700 weights, sizes ranging from tiny 8–12 px credits to 18–46 px blurbs, with slight print misregistration and uneven ink pressure.
- Magazine metadata: include readable cover details in Korean/English mix: “VOL.247”, “2026년 5월호”, “ISSN 1226-0526”, “₩7,500”, “서울 / 아트진”, and a small model-name credit line such as “모델 크레딧: 첨부 인물”.
- Color palette: follow {컬러 톤} with specific surfaces in mustard #C8A23A, deep cyan #0E6A78, charcoal #2B2B2B, and cream #F4EBD8; keep accents muted, editorial, and tactile.
- Border/shadow: use subtle paper-edge shadows, 3px y-offset with 10px blur at 14% opacity, torn-paper rough edges, taped overlaps, folded-corner hints, and layered print depth.
- Graphic details: add small arrows, crop marks, ink stamps, page-number-like labels, torn caption strips, and hand-numbered notes so the cover feels physically assembled and photographed/scanned.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: full-frame editorial portrait look, 85mm f/1.4 with shallow depth of field, crisp facial detail, and a slightly compressed perspective.
- Lighting: soft studio key light from upper-left at about 45°, with gentle fill from front-right and a faint rim on the hairline to separate the subject from the textured background.
- Color grade: muted vintage print grade with cream, mustard, deep cyan, and charcoal; slightly desaturated highlights, warm paper whites, rich ink-like shadows, and realistic CMYK-style print variation.
- Material realism: surfaces should look scanned, pasted, brushed, torn, and printed, with tactile fibers, paper thickness, overlapping shadows, ink bleed, halftone dots, and imperfect handmade alignment.

[6. MOOD]
Contemporary mixed-media fashion editorial — as if a Korean independent art magazine cover were remixed by a collage artist, annotated by hand, printed on textured zine paper, and photographed for a gallery publication.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following verbatim Korean strings must appear correctly if rendered as part of the design: 첨부 인물 사진 정체성·표정 유지, 옆모습(side-facing) 또는 3/4 각도, 손그림 라인 드로잉 (얼굴 윤곽 강조), 콜라주 종이 조각, 페인트 스플래시, 빈티지 잡지 텍스처, 머스타드·딥 시안·차콜 + 크림 — 빈티지 잡지 결, 크라프트·잡지 페이지 텍스처, 살짝 찢어진 가장자리, 작은 영문 세리프 또는 한글 명조, 콜라주 일부로 박힘
- Additional Korean cover strings should be rendered cleanly and legibly where used: 나다운 결, 종이 위의 초상, 불완전한 아름다움, 2026년 5월호, 서울 / 아트진, 모델 크레딧: 첨부 인물.
- Preserve the subject’s identity, facial expression, and overall likeness from the reference image.
- Keep the portrait anatomically correct and maintain natural facial proportions under all collage overlays.
- Any visible hand-drawn lines must follow believable facial contours and should not distort the eyes, nose, or mouth.
- Cover text, barcode, collage scraps, paint, and stickers may overlap hair, clothing, or background, but must not hide the eyes, nose, or mouth.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized likeness substitution

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean traditional folktale illustration poster, vertical storybook front-cover composition for children’s book / exhibition print.
Classic Joseon-era tale mood with a modern editorial finish, designed to clearly read as {표지_제목} while feeling like a real printed Korean folktale book cover with publication details, series labeling, and decorative cover craft.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Single vertical cover layout: top 12–15% contains a decorative hanji title plaque for {표지_제목}, the central 70% presents the narrative scene, and the lower band contains subtitle, author, publisher, and price/ISBN information.
- Primary subject placement must follow {이야기_장면}, with {등장인물} arranged as the emotional focal point in the lower-middle or center zone.
- Background should keep a traditional Korean landscape feel using {배경_소품}, with layered depth from foreground story props to distant clouds, birds, mountains, rooflines, and ink-wash sky elements.
- Add a realistic book-cover information system: {책_정보}, {표지_부제}, {작가_표기}, {출판_표기}, {가격_ISBN}, plus a narrow side strip or small corner label that feels like a premium children’s classic series.
- Use {장식_요소} to frame the illustration with Korean decorative graphics such as dancheong corner motifs, cloud scrolls, lotus petals, magpie feathers, bojagi-inspired geometry, or hand-inked vines.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Background base: warm matte hanji-paper texture with visible fiber grain, cream-beige field, faint ink wash clouds, and slightly uneven pigment absorption to anchor the folklore setting.
- Main scene: render {이야기_장면} as the dominant action moment, with clear narrative emotion, flowing brush rhythm, and readable silhouettes.
- Characters: place {등장인물} in natural hanbok styling, with expressive Korean faces, age variety, braided or topknot hair details, norigae, jeogori folds, durumagi layers, beoseon socks, and historically inspired accessories.
- Story props: integrate {배경_소품} as narrative cues that support the plot, including tactile details like cracked gourd skin, straw roof texture, wooden threshold, woven baskets, silk pouches, coins, jewels, waves, lotus petals, or offering vessels depending on the selected tale.
- Cover typography: set {타이포} in a clean book-cover hierarchy, with {표지_제목} large and centered, {표지_부제} below it or in the lower band, and smaller metadata arranged like a real Korean children’s book cover.
- Publication details: include {책_정보} near the top or side label, {작가_표기} near the lower third, {출판_표기} at the bottom, and {가격_ISBN} as a small printed block or barcode-like publishing detail.
- Color system: apply {컬러_톤} across clothing, sky accents, props, title plaque, and decorative frame, with gold highlights for magical emphasis and mineral-pigment depth.
- Print realism: include slight paper shadow along the title plaque, ink bleed at brush edges, stamped-looking but non-official publisher mark, and subtle registration texture as if printed on premium art paper.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Illustration style: {화풍}, combining Korean folk painting rhythm, oriental ink wash, children’s publishing clarity, and modern editorial polish.
- Typography: Korean serif display type for the title, similar to Noto Serif KR or Batang-inspired letterforms, bold weight, large size; subtitle and metadata in a simple Korean sans serif like Pretendard Medium.
- Color palette: use {컬러_톤} with matte paper cream #F3E9D7, deep ink black #1C1B18, muted vermilion #C84B3A, indigo blue #345B8C, ochre yellow #D6A63A, jade green #4E7C59, and restrained gold #C9A24A.
- Decorative system: hand-inked outline accents, dancheong-pattern corner pieces, thin cloud-scroll dividers, small flower or magpie motifs, and a soft paper-shadow separation around title and metadata plaques.
- Material finish: matte hanji, mineral pigment, dry brush edges, light emboss feel on the main title, and tactile printed-paper depth suitable for a museum shop book cover.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: illustrated poster look with a 50mm editorial framing equivalent, slightly elevated front view, straight cover perspective, clean vertical composition.
- Lighting: diffuse museum-gallery lighting with soft overhead ambient fill and gentle side contrast, emphasizing ink texture, hanji fibers, raised title details, and gold accents without harsh specular shine.
- Color grade: warm cream + mineral pigment + subdued gold, with slightly aged hanji tonality and controlled saturation for a museum-grade folklore print.

[6. MOOD]
Traditional Korean folktale editorial — like a premium children’s storybook cover seen in a museum exhibition catalog, with the elegance of a modern reinterpretation of 민화 and the warmth of an old tale being read aloud at home.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the rendered main title must exactly match {표지_제목}; if using 흥부전, the title string must appear as 흥부전; if using 심청전, the title string must appear as 심청전.
- Visible Korean cover text should include clear, legible strings from {표지_제목}, {표지_부제}, {책_정보}, {작가_표기}, {출판_표기}, and {가격_ISBN}.
- Story consistency: the depicted action, characters, clothing, props, and atmosphere must match {이야기_장면} and form one coherent Korean folktale cover.
- All characters must look clearly Korean and traditional, with authentic hanbok shapes, period-inspired accessories, and expressive storybook emotion.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity face composites
- Counterfeit award badges or government emblems

[INPUT]

[1. PURPOSE]
Seasonal beverage campaign advertising poster, premium K-pop-inspired commercial key visual for social media, retail display, and outdoor-style promo.
Vertical 3:4 poster that combines a stylish model, clear product heroing, realistic campaign details, and a headline copy system with polished Korean advertising typography.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: {모델 묘사} occupies the central 55–60% of the frame, with the product integrated beside or in hand as a secondary hero.
- Layout: {비율·구도} with strong vertical hierarchy; headline/campaign masthead at the upper 18%, model mid-frame, product hero, launch details, and sponsor strip in the lower 22%.
- Background treatment: {시즌·무드} rendered as a cinematic lifestyle set with season-specific props, tactile surfaces, fabric movement, condensation, light reflections, and realistic depth cues that support ad readability.
- Product handling: {제품 배치} with the label facing camera, crisp condensation highlights, accurate can/bottle geometry, edge highlights preserved, and packaging silhouette clearly visible.
- Add realistic poster information: small campaign date label, limited edition note, launch event details, venue/time line, ticket or QR-style block, sponsor/retail partner area, and fine-print credit text.
- Use {브랜드·제품}, {시즌·무드}, {모델 묘사}, {버전}, {제품 배치}, {시그니처 카피}, {비율·구도} as user-configurable content anchors.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header zone (top 18%): place the brand/product identity as a strong campaign title treatment, aligned center or slightly left depending on composition balance. Include a small issue-like campaign label such as "SEASON DROP 2026", "VOL.08", and "2026 SUMMER CAMPAIGN" near the title.
2. Hero zone (mid 55–60%): position {모델 묘사} as the dominant figure with fashion-editorial posture, natural facial expression, clean skin detail, styled hair, accessories, and clear separation from the background.
3. Product zone (lower-mid or side hero): place {브랜드·제품} as a crisp commercial packshot or handheld product element, ensuring the label is fully legible and front-facing. Add realistic beverage cues such as condensation beads, ice glints, splash highlights, fruit/herb garnish, or reflective tray surfaces when suitable for {시즌·무드}.
4. Seasonal styling zone: build the environment from {시즌·무드} cues, using props, fabrics, lighting accents, surface materials, seasonal color accents, and background set pieces that reinforce the chosen seasonal identity.
5. Copy zone (lower 18–22%): set the main slogan "{시그니처 카피}" in a bold, high-contrast advertising lockup. Add 2–3 short Korean supporting blurbs that do not overpower the slogan, such as "청량감 업그레이드", "한정 시즌 에디션", "지금 가장 빛나는 맛".
6. Event / retail detail zone: include compact poster-style information in Korean: "런칭 팝업 2026.05.18–05.24", "성수 플래그십 스토어", "OPEN 11:00–20:00", "입장 무료 · 현장 시음", plus a small QR/barcode-like ticket block labeled "TICKET / QR".
7. Sponsor / credit zone: add a narrow bottom strip with tiny sponsor-style text such as "OFFICIAL PARTNER", "STORE GUIDE", "@brand_korea", "photo by campaign studio", and model-name credit "MODEL: JIYUN" while keeping it visually secondary.
8. Finishing zone: apply {버전} look through contrast, tonal separation, highlight control, realistic reflections, and print-ad finishing so the image reads as a polished global beverage campaign poster.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard Bold or Noto Sans KR Bold for the main copy, with 44–72px headline scale, tight leading, and slightly expanded tracking for premium ad clarity.
- Supporting text style: Pretendard Medium or Nanum Gothic at 18–28px for campaign details, event lines, sponsor strip, QR label, and secondary brand lines, using a clear editorial grid.
- Korean text hierarchy: largest text should be "{시그니처 카피}" or the product campaign title; supporting blurbs must be short, realistic, and readable.
- Color palette: derive from {버전} and {시즌·무드}; for dark campaigns use black #0B0B0D, deep gold #B8944A, and charcoal #2A2A2E; for light campaigns use ivory #F7F3EA, sky blue #BFE8FF, and cool white #FFFFFF.
- Graphic elements: include tasteful seasonal decorative marks such as thin diagonal rules, small sparkle icons, splash shapes, rounded ticket boxes, QR/barcode block, sponsor strip, and subtle product glow effects.
- Border/shadow: subtle soft drop shadow, 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 18% opacity; product edges may use a thin rim light instead of a hard outline.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial commercial photography, full-frame 85mm f/1.4 portrait look for the model and product, with controlled background compression and sharp packshot detail.
- Lighting: studio key light at 45° from upper-left, soft fill from front-right, and a gentle rim light separating hair, shoulders, product edges, condensation droplets, and glass/metal highlights.
- Color grade: choose either high-contrast noir gold for the dark version or bright clean aqua-cream for the light version, with premium beverage-ad colors, crisp skin tones, glossy product reflections, and realistic print-poster contrast.
- Surface realism: show believable fabric texture, cool condensation, wet highlights, ice or splash reflections, acrylic/glass surfaces, paper-poster grain, and depth-of-field falloff appropriate to the campaign set.

[6. MOOD]
Global beverage campaign editorial — somewhere between a Vogue Korea beauty spread and a high-end Pepsi/Cola-style commercial poster, with fashion-forward polish, retail launch energy, seasonal freshness, and broadcast-grade finish.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following Korean string must appear exactly and cleanly in the rendered image: "이 순간을 즐겨".
- Korean text accuracy: supporting Korean poster text may include "청량감 업그레이드", "한정 시즌 에디션", "런칭 팝업 2026.05.18–05.24", "성수 플래그십 스토어", "입장 무료 · 현장 시음", and "지금 가장 빛나는 맛"; render all Korean characters cleanly and naturally.
- Korean text accuracy: preserve the chosen visible brand/product wording, season wording, model description cues, version label cues, product placement cues, and ratio/composition cues only as layout guidance; do not render placeholder braces.
- Product anatomy/layout invariants: product label must be readable, straight, and not warped; model hands must look natural with anatomically correct fingers.
- If multiple product elements appear, keep the same brand identity and consistent packaging design across the whole poster.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness

[INPUT]

- output_size: 1024x1536
- format: vertical local store banner / handmade poster advertisement

[1. PURPOSE]
Local store banner advertisement in a rough vintage indie-punk style, designed like a handmade street poster for a neighborhood bakery or café opening campaign.
Vertical 1024x1536 banner composition for storefront display, community bulletin boards, and social-media-friendly promo use.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject is a tape-made local promo banner filling most of the vertical canvas, photographed like a real paper-and-duct-tape poster laid on a tabletop.
- Background surface should feel tactile and handmade: kraft paper, brown corrugated cardboard, and coarse fabric texture layered with visible fiber grain, wrinkles, stains, staple marks, marker smudges, and torn paper scraps.
- Place {매장명} as the local store name near the top, {매장·이벤트} as the contextual store/event descriptor, and {메인 카피} as the primary headline in the upper-middle hero area.
- Add realistic promo details: {행사기간}, {영업시간}, {주소}, {연락처}, {티켓·쿠폰정보}, and {스폰서·협력} arranged as handwritten labels, taped memo strips, and small bottom information blocks.
- Use {비주얼} as the key visual treatment, with black, gray, and yellow duct tape partially crossing the layout like an intentionally rough street-poster collage.
- Include small decorative graphics such as marker arrows, star bursts, price-tag stickers, torn coupon tabs, tiny coffee cup / bread doodles, and a small QR-style square printed on a taped scrap.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Top band (upper 15%): rough marker handwriting with the store name {매장명}, a tiny issue-like promo label “LOCAL DROP 05”, and spray/stencil accents that feel pasted up by hand.
- Main hero zone (middle 45%): large tape-collage composition where {비주얼} dominates, with black, gray, and yellow duct tape diagonals crossing kraft paper, cardboard, and fabric layers.
- Headline lockup (center-upper): set {메인 카피} in bold hand-drawn marker lettering, slightly uneven stroke width, as if written directly on the paper with permanent marker.
- Context line (near headline or lower-middle): place {매장·이벤트} in a smaller rough stencil or distressed sans serif style so it reads like a real local event notice.
- Event detail strip (lower-middle): add “기간 {행사기간}”, “시간 {영업시간}”, and “장소 {주소}” on separate taped paper strips with marker underlines and hand-drawn arrows.
- Coupon / ticket area (lower 20%): show {티켓·쿠폰정보} as a torn voucher stub with perforation dots, a small QR-style square, and stamped-looking text “현장 제시”.
- Sponsor / neighborhood area (bottom 10%): include {스폰서·협력}, {연락처}, and small community-board style microtext, with rough dividers made from tape and marker lines.
- Background finish (full frame): build from {배경 텍스처} with visible creases, scuffs, tape residue, uneven paper edges, staple holes, and soft shadows where tape overlaps.
- Color handling: let {컬러 톤} guide the whole piece, with muted kraft beige as the base, saturated yellow tape accents, charcoal tape, warm brown cardboard, and deep black handwritten text for contrast.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use bold hand-drawn marker lettering for the main copy, with supporting English-like spray/stencil typography in a distressed sans serif; keep the strokes thick, imperfect, jittery, and authentically hand-made.
- Korean lettering must be clear and legible even when surrounded by tape, doodles, scratches, coupon tabs, and handwritten information blocks.
- Color palette: kraft beige, mustard yellow, matte black, warm brown cardboard, charcoal gray; optional hex references #D8C3A5, #E0B400, #111111, #6B6258, #4B3F34.
- Edge / shadow treatment: irregular torn-paper edge framing with soft tape shadows, 4px y-offset, 10px blur, about 18% opacity, with layered real-material depth rather than flat vector cleanliness.
- Decorative details should feel like a real neighborhood flyer: marker arrows, handwritten price notes, small doodles, coffee/bread icons, coupon perforations, tape wrinkles, thumbprints, scuffed corners, and pasted scrap-paper labels.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: top-down editorial poster capture, 35mm lens look at f/5.6 with slight perspective flattening, as if photographed on a tabletop in a small studio.
- Lighting: diffused overcast-style softbox from upper-left at 45°, minimal fill from lower-right, with gentle tape gloss highlights and soft shadow falloff.
- Color grade: desaturated kraft beige with muted mustard yellow and deep charcoal black, slightly gritty contrast and a documentary street-print finish.

[6. MOOD]
Indie street-poster campaign — part zine, part neighborhood shop flyer, with the raw handmade energy of a small local popup announcement, including real-world event information, coupon utility, and neighborhood bulletin-board charm.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문자열: “테이프앤크럼”, “동네 빵집 — 신메뉴 출시 / 또는 카페 그랜드 오픈”, “오픈 기념 — 첫 잔 무료”, “5월 10일–5월 12일”, “오전 8시–밤 9시”, “서울 마포구 와우산로 27길 14”, “문의 02-3141-0527”, “쿠폰 제시 시 아메리카노 1잔 무료”, “협력: 서교동 상점회”.
- Layout invariant: the main headline “오픈 기념 — 첫 잔 무료” must remain the clearest focal text while tape, doodles, coupon tabs, and information strips add realism around it.
- The banner must read as a rough vintage indie-punk local store advertisement with tactile duct tape, kraft paper, marker handwriting, event details, coupon information, and neighborhood sponsor microtext.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters or garbled Hangul
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized likenesses

[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1536x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Cookbook recipe magazine spread for a single featured dish, designed like a real editorial recipe feature with generous food photography, ingredient list, cooking method, chef note, captioning, issue metadata, and magazine production details.
A premium double-page layout suitable for a printed cooking magazine or recipe book, with the richness of a photographed editorial spread rather than a sterile mockup.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Left page: large food photo occupies about 60% of the full spread width, framed edge-to-edge with a narrow inner gutter and a realistic printed-page crop. The dish from {음식 사진} should feel freshly plated, with visible sauce sheen, pasta texture, steam warmth, table surface detail, and natural food styling elements that support {요리명·국가}.
- Right page: structured editorial column stack with title, ingredient list, cooking steps, chef comment, prep metadata, and magazine sidebars, aligned on a neat 12-column grid using {레이아웃}.
- The overall layout should clearly separate the hero dish from the text-heavy recipe information while still feeling like one cohesive magazine spread with a visible center gutter, page numbers, section labels, and subtle paper fold realism.
- Background treatment: soft paper-like off-white base with subtle magazine print texture, faint fiber grain, realistic ink density variation, and gentle page curvature near the center fold.
- Use {요리명·국가} as the main recipe title hierarchy at the top of the right page, with strong visual emphasis and a small editorial kicker above it.
- Use {재료} in a readable list block, and place {셰프 코멘트} as a highlighted pull-quote or side note.
- Add recipe-magazine details: issue label, date label, page numbers, section marker, small barcode/pricing area, photo caption, chef credit line, difficulty/time/serving badges, and a short Korean recipe intro paragraph.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Hero image area (left page): present the dish from {음식 사진} as the main visual, filling the page with realistic food texture, shallow depth impression, crisp highlight control, glossy sauce detail, herb flecks, plate rim detail, and an editorial tabletop scene that naturally belongs in a cookbook shoot.
- Left-page overlay/caption: add a small caption block near the bottom or outer margin with Korean editorial text such as "천천히 끓인 라구의 깊은 풍미", a photographer credit "Photo. Studio Table", and a page number like "p.034".
- Title block (right page top): set {요리명·국가} in a large serif headline with magazine-style spacing, aligned to the top grid and separated by thin rules. Above it include a small section label: "RECIPE JOURNAL · PASTA SPECIAL" and issue/date text: "VOL.247 · 2026년 5월호".
- Metadata strip: beneath the title, include compact badges or labels in Korean: "조리시간 2시간 30분", "난이도 중", "2–3인분", "예상비용 ₩18,000".
- Ingredients block (right page upper-middle): display {재료} as a compact but highly legible list, with consistent line spacing, small circular bullets or short separators, and a small heading "INGREDIENTS / 재료".
- Recipe body block (right page middle): reserve space for step-by-step cooking instructions in clean short paragraphs, numbered 01–04, using realistic Korean placeholder copy such as "향채소를 잘게 다져 약한 불에서 볶는다", "고기를 넣고 갈색빛이 날 때까지 익힌다", "와인과 토마토 페이스트를 넣어 졸인다", "우유를 더해 천천히 끓인 뒤 파스타와 버무린다".
- Chef note block (right page lower): place {셰프 코멘트} in an italic or quoted editorial box with a subtle tinted background, fine border, quotation mark detail, and label "CHEF'S NOTE".
- Sidebar elements: include a small "PAIRING TIP" box with Korean text like "산미가 있는 레드와인과 잘 어울립니다", plus a tiny nutrition-style row "칼로리 620kcal · 단백질 28g · 소금 1.4g".
- Footer area: include magazine-like metadata styling, page number treatment, barcode/pricing area, small caps labels, section marker "DINING / WEEKEND TABLE", and editorial credit text such as "Recipe. 편집부 테스트 키친 · Styling. 한지우".

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use {타이포}; title in Noto Serif KR or Nanum Myeongjo Bold, 42–56 px equivalent; body in Pretendard or Noto Sans KR Regular, 18–24 px equivalent; small caps labels in a condensed sans style; numerals and issue labels may use a refined editorial grotesque.
- Color palette: {컬러 톤} with fade beige #E8DDCF, charcoal #2B2B2B, warm amber #C98A3A, tomato brown #7A3E25, herb olive #6F7A3A, and paper white #F6F1E8.
- Border/shadow: thin 1px charcoal rules, very light print grain, subtle shadow under the photo panel only, 8px blur, 12% opacity; include faint registration-like crop ticks, small divider lines, and realistic ink-on-paper softness.
- Layout detailing: use visible magazine hierarchy with kicker, headline, dek paragraph, ingredient list, numbered method, pull quote, captions, credits, barcode block, and page folios. Keep all text blocks aligned to the editorial grid while allowing the food photograph to feel abundant and tactile.
- Decorative graphic elements: warm amber rule lines, small circular bullets, recipe category tags, tiny icons for time/serving/difficulty, and subtle page fold shading that reinforces the printed double-page spread.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial food photography look, 50mm lens at f/2.8 or 85mm macro at f/4, clean top-down or slight 30° angle depending on plated composition.
- Lighting: soft natural window light from upper-left, gentle fill from right, controlled specular highlights on sauce and pasta, realistic shadow falloff across the plate, table linen, utensils, and page surface.
- Color grade: warm editorial paper tones, beige + amber + deep brown balance, slightly muted contrast like a high-end cookbook spread.
- Food realism: emphasize authentic ingredient detail from {재료}, including browned meat sauce, tomato paste depth, pasta strands or ribbons, grated cheese dusting if appropriate, tiny herb garnish, sauce cling, and natural plating imperfections.
- Print realism: include slight paper grain, barely visible halftone texture in the photograph, ink absorption around Korean text, center gutter compression, and page-edge shadows to make the spread feel physically photographed or scanned from a premium magazine.

[6. MOOD]
Premium cookbook editorial — feels like a high-end food magazine spread with warm kitchen storytelling, appetizing realism, and the polished recipe design of Bon Appétit, Kinfolk-style paper tactility, and a contemporary Korean lifestyle magazine sensibility.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문자열이 정확히 보여야 함.
  - "라구 알라 볼로네제 (이탈리아)"
  - "다진 소고기 300g / 양파 1개 / 당근 1/2개 / 셀러리 1대 / 토마토 페이스트 3T / 레드와인 1컵 / 우유 1컵 / 파스타"
  - "2시간 천천히 끓이는 인내가 깊은 맛의 비결입니다."
- Additional Korean editorial text should be readable and magazine-realistic, including examples such as "VOL.247 · 2026년 5월호", "조리시간 2시간 30분", "난이도 중", "2–3인분", "INGREDIENTS / 재료", "CHEF'S NOTE", "Recipe. 편집부 테스트 키친", and "p.035".
- Layout invariant: left page is image-dominant, right page is text-dominant, both aligned as a single cohesive magazine spread with visible center gutter and printed-page realism.
- Korean and English typography must be clean and correctly rendered with no broken characters.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

studio:prompts3:ours-289.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Vertical food infographic for a Korean recipe card, combining ingredient list, cooking steps, nutrition facts, and small editorial metadata in a polished cookbook-magazine layout.
Designed for card news, blog posts, mobile recipe saving, and cookbook-style sharing with clear Korean readability and a realistic printed-page feel.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Overall layout: a tall single-page infographic with a top editorial header and hero food photo occupying about 30% of the canvas, a middle recipe information section occupying about 42%, and a bottom nutrition plus CTA block occupying about 18%, with practical outer margins around 40–48px.
- Subject placement: {요리명} appears as the main header near the top, supported by recipe metadata such as serving size, cook time, difficulty, issue/date label, and a small creator credit; the plated dish photo sits directly beneath with ingredient accents and food-styling details around the frame.
- Background treatment: warm cream paper texture with visible subtle grain, faint cookbook scan texture, soft warm shadows, lightly tinted off-white cards, and small realistic tabletop details such as a linen corner, tiny herb flakes, salt grains, measuring spoon, or chopstick edge that support the recipe theme.
- Spacing and framing: use a structured editorial grid with readable section blocks, thin divider lines, numbered markers, small caption labels, slide indicator, and a balanced mobile-first hierarchy for dense Korean text.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header area: set {요리명} as the largest title, bold and centered-left or centered depending on {레이아웃}; add a small magazine-style label line such as "오늘의 레시피", "VOL.247", "2026년 5월호", and creator credit "@home_table" near the top edge.
2. Food photo area: place a realistic overhead or slightly angled plated dish photo in a rounded rectangle frame with soft shadow; include natural matching garnish, steam or glossy sauce highlights when appropriate, and a small caption strip reading "한눈에 보는 레시피" or "COOK NOTE".
3. Quick info strip: directly below or beside the hero photo, add three compact badges for "2인분", "예상 시간 25분", and "난이도 보통", using icons such as a bowl, clock, and flame/star.
4. Ingredient area: list {재료 리스트} under the Korean section label "재료" as compact bullet points, ingredient chips, or small illustrated ingredient tiles; include tiny quantity markers, shopping-note styling, and a side label "장보기 메모" when space allows.
5. Cooking steps area: present {조리 단계} as 4 numbered step cards or a vertical timeline under "만드는 법", using action-matched illustrated icons such as wash, slice, stir-fry, boil, plate, season, or serve; add a small highlighted "TIP" note box with a short Korean cooking hint.
6. Nutrition area: show {영양 정보} in a structured bottom summary panel labeled "영양 정보" and "1인분 기준", with bold numeric callouts, aligned labels, tiny bar indicators, and a small footnote line for serving context.
7. Card news details: include a page indicator such as "01/05", tiny save/share/bookmark micro icons, and a bottom CTA line reading "저장하고 다시 보기"; keep these details small but visible like a real social recipe card.
8. Layout note area: follow {레이아웃} as the organizing logic, keeping the composition editorial, content-rich, and easy to read on mobile.
9. Color emphasis: apply {컬러 톤} consistently across title accents, icons, dividers, badges, step numbers, and key nutritional numbers.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for body text in medium weight, with the title in Pretendard ExtraBold or Nanum Myeongjo Bold; title size should be significantly larger than body text for clear hierarchy, while micro labels use condensed medium-weight Korean sans serif.
- Color palette: derive the palette from {컬러 톤}, with specific implementation using cream #F6F0E6, charcoal #2F2F2F, kimchi red #C73A2C, muted warm gray #B8B0A6, and small herb-green or sesame-beige accents when they support the food.
- Border/shadow: use thin 1px charcoal or warm-gray rules, rounded cards with 16px radius, soft drop shadows at 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity, and occasional hand-drawn divider strokes or dotted guide lines for a printed recipe-book feeling.
- Editorial details: add realistic micro text blocks, small captions, recipe badges, page number, decorative dividers, and subtle food-themed icons; make them look intentionally typeset rather than floating randomly.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial food photography look, shot on a 50mm lens at f/4 for the hero dish, or a top-down 35mm equivalent for a flat-lay ingredient style.
- Lighting: soft diffused window light from upper-left, with a gentle fill from the right, natural shadows under the plate and paper cards, and controlled appetizing highlights on sauces, grains, vegetables, or broth.
- Color grade: warm cream and natural food tones with restrained red accents, slightly desaturated to keep the infographic readable while preserving appetizing texture in the plated food.
- Material realism: paper grain, printed ink edges, ceramic plate texture, wooden tabletop warmth, linen weave, tiny crumbs or sesame seeds, and realistic food surface detail should be visible at close inspection.

[6. MOOD]
Modern Korean cookbook infographic — feels like a premium food magazine recipe spread adapted into a social card news format, warm, useful, appetizing, and ready to save.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 표시되어야 하는 문자열: "{요리명}", "{재료 리스트}", "{조리 단계}", "{영양 정보}".
- Additional Korean labels must render cleanly if included: "오늘의 레시피", "재료", "만드는 법", "영양 정보", "1인분 기준", "2인분", "예상 시간 25분", "난이도 보통", "장보기 메모", "TIP", "저장하고 다시 보기", "01/05", "2026년 5월호".
- Layout integrity: the page must remain a single vertical infographic with clear section separation, and the nutrition block must stay at the bottom.
- Text legibility: all Korean characters must render cleanly with no broken glyphs, truncation, or overlap.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[1. PURPOSE]
Local Korean restaurant lunch menu advertising poster for SNS feed, neighborhood noticeboard, and A4-style print flyer.
Designed to communicate lunch set options, pricing, hours, location, phone contact, and a practical coupon-style callout with a warm local eatery atmosphere.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main composition: {비주얼메인} placed in the center 45–55% of the frame, with {매장명} and a bold “LUNCH MENU” headline at the top 15–18%, then menu pricing, time, address, and contact information anchored in the lower 30%.
- Background treatment: matte warm beige paper with lightly visible kraft-paper fibers, subtle wood-table edge, small realistic dining details such as chopsticks sleeve, spoon, folded napkin, stainless cup reflection, soy-sauce stain dot, and a tiny receipt clip used as atmosphere around the food area.
- Framing direction: vertical poster hierarchy with strong top-to-bottom reading flow; maintain clear separation between hero food photography, menu price grid, time strip, and footer contact area.
- Use {매장명}, {업종}, {런치메뉴}, {런치시간}, {시그니처카피}, {주소}, {전화번호}, {휴무안내}, {주문안내}, {포스터날짜}, {스폰서문구}, {쿠폰문구}, {대표해시태그} as editable text elements.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top header band: place {매장명} as the primary masthead in large bold Korean type, with {업종} as a smaller descriptor underneath; add “LUNCH MENU” in condensed English lettering and a small date label “{포스터날짜}” near the corner.
2. Hero food zone: feature {비주얼메인} as the visual centerpiece, shot to look freshly plated and appetizing, with visible rice, side dishes, steam, glossy sauce texture, stew surface, sesame garnish, and realistic tableware proportions; use a slight shadow underneath to lift it from the printed poster background.
3. Signature copy zone: set {시그니처카피} near the hero image or just below it, styled like a short promotional slogan on a red brush-stroke ribbon or paper sticker.
4. Menu list zone: present {런치메뉴} in a stacked price-board layout with dotted leaders, won pricing, and thin charcoal divider lines; group the list inside a light rice-white panel so items scan quickly.
5. Time and order strip: display {런치시간} as a compact chili-red strip near the menu list; add {주문안내}, {전화번호}, and a small takeaway-bag or phone icon treatment for practical ordering information.
6. Footer information area: include {주소}, {휴무안내}, {대표해시태그}, and {스폰서문구}; add {쿠폰문구} as a small tear-off coupon box or stamp-like rectangle with scissors mark, plus simple decorative graphics such as rice-grain dots, chili pepper illustration, steam lines, and thin rule dividers.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Sans KR Bold for the main title, Pretendard SemiBold for menu items, and Noto Sans KR Regular for supporting details; headline around 64–88px, menu text around 30–40px, time text around 24–28px, footer details around 18–24px.
- Color palette: follow {컬러톤}; recommended palette warm beige #F3E7D3, wood brown #B98B62, dark charcoal #2B2B2B, chili red #D94B3D, rice white #FFF8EF, sesame yellow #E7C66A.
- Layout system: follow {레이아웃}; use a strong rectangular menu panel, dotted price leaders, small date badge, coupon box, footer contact bar, and consistent left/right alignment for fast readability.
- Border/shadow: add a soft realistic drop shadow under the food image (0px x-offset, 6px y-offset, 16px blur, 18% opacity), thin charcoal divider lines at 1–2px, and a slightly darker kraft-paper outer frame for a printed flyer feel.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: top-down food poster feel with a 50mm lens look at f/5.6, or a gentle 45° food-photography angle using a 35mm prime for a more natural restaurant-ad look.
- Lighting: soft diffused daylight from upper-left, subtle fill from right, realistic highlights on glossy sauce and soup surface, faint steam over hot dishes, no harsh flash reflections.
- Color grade: warm beige and wood tones balanced with rich red-brown food color, slightly muted contrast, clean editorial restaurant print finish with tactile paper texture.

[6. MOOD]
Neighborhood lunch-special poster with the practical editorial charm of a Korean local diner ad: friendly, filling, affordable, and believable as something taped near an office building elevator or shared on a local SNS account.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the rendered poster must contain these strings exactly as written: "한솔식당", "한식 백반·찌개 전문", "제육 정식 9,000원 / 김치찌개 정식 8,500원 / 된장찌개 정식 8,000원 / 제육 + 계란말이 10,500원", "평일 11:30 ~ 14:30", "오늘의 든든한 한 끼", "서울 마포구 월드컵북로 12길 8", "02-3141-0824", "매주 일요일 휴무", "포장 주문 가능", "2026년 5월 점심 특선", "인근 사무실 단체주문 환영", "점심시간 음료 1잔 서비스", "#마포점심 #한식백반 #오늘뭐먹지".
- Layout requirement: menu prices must be aligned and readable; separate the food image, menu panel, time strip, coupon box, and footer information into clear poster zones.
- Food depiction requirement: if side dishes are visible, show them as a complete set of 4 or more small banchan portions with realistic plating proportions.
- Print realism requirement: include tactile paper grain, believable tableware shadows, and small local-flyer details such as coupon perforation marks, date badge, and contact footer.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Illegible pricing or duplicated menu lines
- Celebrity composites or fake celebrity endorsements

[1. PURPOSE]
Surreal ice cream advertising poster, vertical campaign key visual for a confectionery brand. Premium commercial poster for print, retail display, subway lightbox, and social media sharing, featuring a giant central product hero with realistic campaign information and polished Korean ad typography.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Use {구도}: place the product hero slightly below center, taking about 55–60% of the frame height, with the headline zone above and a dense but orderly campaign footer below.
- Build the scene around {브랜드·제품명} as the visual anchor: the ice-cream form must read instantly as a luxurious product sculpture, with the surreal melting glacier or fruit-and-syrup burst clearly visible.
- Use {배경} as a bright studio-paper environment with a cool gradient, frosty condensation mist, tiny suspended ice shards, glossy syrup droplets, and subtle paper grain so the poster feels like a real photographed campaign set.
- Integrate natural product-ad elements: close-up frost crystals, melting ridges, fruit pulp, wafer crumbs, cold vapor trails, reflective puddles of syrup, and a soft grounded shadow beneath the hero.
- Arrange supporting poster information around the hero without blocking it: a top campaign label, 2–3 short feature lines, a small promo badge, QR-style square, date and purchase information, sponsor/collaboration strip, and footer lockup.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Top campaign zone (15–20%): place {시그니처 카피} in bold Korean sans-serif, centered or slightly left-aligned, with a small upper label reading {출시 정보} and a secondary line {영문 보조 카피}.
- Feature headline cluster: add 2–3 realistic Korean ad lines near the main copy, such as {제품 특징}, {가격 문구}, and {해시태그}; use varied type sizes like a real seasonal poster hierarchy.
- Main hero zone (middle 55–60%): render the {비주얼 컨셉} as the main object cluster, dramatically enlarged, glossy, and sculptural; melting edges should look surreal, cold, appetizing, and physically lit.
- Material detail zone: emphasize semi-frozen sheen, soft condensation, micro frost, translucent syrup skins, crushed ice, and realistic highlight rolls on the ice cream surface; fruit elements should look freshly cut with vivid pulp and splashes frozen mid-air.
- Color zone: apply {컬러 톤} as the dominant palette, balancing product-specific hues against icy whites and pale blues so the composition feels cold, crisp, and high-contrast.
- Poster information zone: include {캠페인 기간}, {구매 안내}, {QR 문구}, and a small QR-like square graphic at the lower-right; include {후원·협업} as a slim sponsor/collaboration strip.
- Bottom lockup zone (8–12%): place {브랜드·제품명} as a polished brand signature with a barcode-like retail graphic, small nutrition-style microcopy, and a compact legal/campaign note line.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use {텍스트 톤}; main Korean copy should feel like Pretendard Black, 44–64 px equivalent, with precise baseline control; secondary information should use Noto Sans KR Regular or Pretendard Medium in smaller sizes.
- Text hierarchy: headline first, product name second, feature lines third, then campaign date, price, QR prompt, and sponsor strip; keep all Korean text sharp and intentionally typeset.
- Color palette: use the product color plus icy neutrals such as #F7FBFF, #DDEEFF, #BFE8FF, and a subtle mint or strawberry accent depending on the product tone.
- Graphic details: add thin dividers, small circular promo badge, translucent ice-blue panels, barcode/QR-style blocks, and tiny snowflake or splash icons that match a premium Korean confectionery campaign.
- Shadow and depth: use a soft grounded shadow under the hero, 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 18% opacity, plus believable reflections and contact shadows in syrup or melt puddles.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: high-end studio product photography, shot on a Phase One IQ4 with an 80mm lens at f/8, front-facing advertising composition.
- Lighting: large overhead softbox at 45° from upper-left, with a faint cool fill from the right and crisp specular highlights to show the icy surface.
- Color grade: clean commercial grade with cool whites, minty greens or strawberry pinks, and restrained blue shadows; keep saturation controlled but vivid.
- Surface realism: macro-level frost crystals, condensation beads, semi-translucent ice edges, thick glossy syrup, and fresh fruit fibers should be visible where appropriate.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean ice cream campaign key visual — a Hyundai department-store seasonal ad meets a surreal product poster aesthetic, polished like a high-end food editorial, with lively summer retail details and a collectible limited-edition feeling.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following strings must appear exactly as written: "여름은 한 입에", "빙그레 — 메로나 시그니처".
- Include the poster information as readable Korean text: "2026 SUMMER LIMITED", "2026.06.01 – 08.31", "전국 편의점·마트 동시 출시", "권장소비자가 ₩1,800", "차가운 멜론 풍미 · 부드러운 크림감", "QR로 가까운 매장 찾기", "#한입에여름".
- The product must remain the clear central hero and feel oversized, luxurious, cold, appetizing, and commercial.
- If fruit, syrup, ice shards, QR/barcode graphics, or decorative campaign badges appear, they must look physically believable, sharply printed, and integrated into the poster design.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Crooked, illegible, or misspelled typography
- Low-resolution, muddy, or overly plastic-looking ice cream texture

[INPUT]

[1. PURPOSE]
8K hyper-real food editorial advertising poster, vertical 3:4 format for social media, store display, and digital campaign use.
Create a premium food feature page that combines magazine-cover polish with practical advertising information: product hero, seasonal campaign copy, price, event details, store contact, and small editorial callouts.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- The main hero subject occupies the center 55–60% of the frame, with {식품} styled as the dominant focal point and {제품브랜드} treated as supporting packaging, label, or brand presentation.
- Composition should follow a refined vertical editorial poster layout: top masthead and headline band, central food hero zone, side caption tags, and bottom information strip with price, date, venue, and contact details.
- Background treatment: warm white or soft beige seamless surface with subtle natural paper, matte ceramic, linen, or stone texture, plus realistic shadow falloff that makes the food feel physically present.
- Add natural food-ad details around the hero: ingredient fragments, crumbs, droplets, seeds, garnish, a small spoon, folded linen, sample card, barcode sticker, or tiny tasting note card that supports the product story.
- Use {구도} as the structural composition guide, but keep the layout polished, commercial, and easy to read at mobile poster scale.
- Use {레이아웃} as the text zoning guide, with visible separation between headline, tagline, editorial feature bullets, and lower purchase/event blocks.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top zone (top 15–20%): place a magazine-style masthead label reading {상단라벨}, issue/date text reading {발행정보}, a bold main Korean campaign headline reading {메인카피}, and a compact English tagline reading {영문태그라인}. Add a small barcode-style block or campaign code reading {캠페인코드} near the top-right or lower-right edge.
2. Hero zone (middle 55–60%): render {식품} with crisp surface detail, vivid natural texture, realistic moisture, powder, sugar, skin, crumb, or juice details depending on the food. If {제품브랜드} is a package, show it as a secondary object with realistic label placement, folds, reflections, and accurate perspective.
3. Editorial callout zone: integrate 2–3 small feature headlines in Korean, such as {특징카피1}, {특징카피2}, and {특징카피3}, placed as small caption cards, circular sticker tabs, or thin-line annotation labels pointing toward the food.
4. Lower information zone (bottom 15–20%): place {가격}, {행사일시}, {장소}, {티켓정보}, {매장명}, {주소}, and {연락처} in a tidy infographic row or stacked micro-card system, using thin dividers, small icons, and clear alignment.
5. Sponsor and social zone: include a small sponsor/support line reading {스폰서문구}, hashtag text reading {해시태그}, and micro social icons for save/share/scan as printed graphic elements.
6. Text layering: use {텍스트톤} for the main typography style, with Korean micro-copy integrated as supporting captions, ingredient notes, price tags, and event labels.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard Bold or Inter Bold for the headline, Noto Sans KR Medium for Korean subtext, and a strong size hierarchy that clearly favors the hero image while keeping campaign information readable.
- Color palette: use the natural tones of {컬러톤}, with off-white #F4F0E6, warm beige #E9DDC8, soft shadow gray #B9B1A4, and product-specific accent colors derived from the food.
- Graphic system: add refined editorial dividers, small sticker labels, barcode/campaign-code typography, price tags, ingredient callout cards, and a compact sponsor area that feels like a premium printed advertising poster.
- Border/shadow: apply soft poster-card depth with 4px y-offset, 12px blur, and 15% opacity, plus tactile paper grain and subtle ink-like typography edges.
- Layout polish: align all text blocks to a consistent grid, use generous line spacing for Korean captions, and make every price, date, and contact line legible.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: medium-format studio food photography look, Phase One IQ4 with 80mm lens at f/8 for sharp texture and controlled depth, or a 100mm macro look for close detail.
- Lighting: softbox key light from upper-left at 45°, gentle fill from the front-right, subtle rim light on the far edge, creating clean realistic shadows on the background.
- Color grade: premium editorial grade with warm cream highlights, rich natural product saturation, and slightly muted beige shadows; maintain clean contrast with appetizing food color and realistic print-ready tones.

[6. MOOD]
Premium food magazine editorial — like a Kinfolk meets Bon Appétit campaign spread, with refined studio styling, appetizing realism, market-poster usefulness, and high-end commercial polish.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following Korean strings must appear exactly as rendered text when used in the design: "{메인카피}", "{한글보조카피}", "{특징카피1}", "{특징카피2}", "{특징카피3}".
- Practical poster information must remain legible and correctly spelled in Korean: "{가격}", "{행사일시}", "{장소}", "{티켓정보}", "{매장명}", "{주소}", "{연락처}".
- Any ingredient, packaging, barcode-style campaign code, sponsor line, and hashtag text must remain clean, readable, and visually integrated with the food editorial layout.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or face swaps

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean rooftop twilight cinematic close-up portrait for editorial/social use. Emphasize a natural candid expression, real Seoul rooftop atmosphere, city-night bokeh, and romantic dusk details that feel like a captured moment rather than a studio mockup.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject placement: {모델 묘사} placed slightly off-center in a tight close-up, occupying about 55–65% of the vertical frame, with the face as the primary focal point and the eyes carrying the strongest emotional weight.
- Background treatment: {장면} rendered as a believable Seoul rooftop at twilight: soft urban lights, distant skyline silhouettes, apartment windows, faint road trails, rooftop railings, safety mesh, water-tank or HVAC silhouettes, a few potted plants, and warm string-light bokeh falling naturally out of focus.
- Framing direction: portrait orientation, chest-up to close-up crop, shallow depth of field, with enough upper-corner room for subtle social/editorial date and location labels without competing with the face.
- Pose/action: {감정} with a natural hand gesture that shades the eyes or blocks the last sunlight, keeping the pose relaxed, candid, and physically believable.
- Social/editorial overlay: add small tasteful Korean diary-card details such as “서울, 옥상에서”, “2026.05.01 19:24”, “@rooftop.diary”, and a small caption sticker reading “바람이 좋은 저녁”; keep them secondary and integrated into the photograph.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Subject layer: Render {모델 묘사} with crisp facial detail, soft natural skin texture, tiny catchlights in the eyes, realistic pores, flyaway hair strands catching the backlight, and clothing fabric texture appropriate to an evening rooftop portrait.
2. Scene layer: Place {장면} behind the subject as an evening Seoul skyline with glowing windows, distant road lights, rooftop railings, safety fence lines, small planters, concrete floor texture, and subtle river or high-rise highlights depending on the background reading.
3. Lighting layer: Apply {라이팅} as the key visual cue, with warm dusk light outlining the hair and cheekbones, cooler city fill from the front-right, tiny reflections from rooftop bulbs, and soft environmental bounce from nearby concrete and glass.
4. Composition layer: Use {구도} to isolate the face from the background, with the strongest sharpness on the eyes, gentle falloff toward the shoulders and hands, layered bokeh behind the head, and natural rooftop depth cues in the blurred distance.
5. Color layer: Apply {컬러 톤} across skin, sky, rooftop surfaces, and bokeh; keep pink/coral sunset tones in the highlights and cyan-blue urban accents in shadows, distant windows, and reflected city light.
6. Camera layer: Recreate the look of {카메라·렌즈} with portrait compression, shallow DOF, realistic optical bokeh, slight highlight bloom around small lights, and a premium high-resolution editorial finish.
7. Emotion layer: Express {감정} through micro-expression only—subtle squinting, slight smile tension, softened jaw, calm breathing posture, and relaxed shoulders—like an intimate rooftop snapshot between takes.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: include small clean Korean social/editorial text overlays only: “서울, 옥상에서”, “2026.05.01 19:24”, “@rooftop.diary”, and “바람이 좋은 저녁”; use crisp modern sans-serif lettering in white or warm off-white with subtle translucent backing where needed for readability.
- Color palette: use warm pink, coral, peach, dusk orange, and restrained cyan-blue; suggested accents #F7A6A1, #FFB07A, #FFD7C2, #6DCFD6, #1F2A44.
- Graphic accents: allow tiny diary-style tags, a small location-pin icon, a subtle heart/save micro icon near the lower edge, and soft translucent sticker shapes that feel like a real social portrait card.
- Environmental detail: include realistic rooftop textures such as painted metal railings, concrete parapet edges, faint dust, plant leaves, cable lines, distant antennas, and glowing apartment windows, all controlled by shallow focus.
- Border/shadow: use natural portrait shadow, gentle edge contrast, and atmospheric falloff from foreground to background; any overlay graphics should remain light, photographic, and secondary.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Sony A7R V look with 85mm f/1.2 portrait compression, shot at ISO 400, f/1.8, shallow focus and clean subject isolation.
- Lighting: twilight backlight from behind-left with dusk sky glow, plus diffuse city-light fill from the front-right; bokeh highlights from distant buildings, traffic, rooftop bulbs, and apartment windows.
- Color grade: warm pink-coral sunset mids and highlights with cool cyan urban shadows, cinematic contrast, slightly lifted blacks, polished editorial saturation, realistic skin color, and soft highlight bloom around city lights.

[6. MOOD]
Cinematic Seoul rooftop portrait — like a still from a late-night K-drama and a polished social diary cover, intimate, breezy, romantic, and grounded in real rooftop details.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: render all on-image Korean text cleanly and legibly: “서울, 옥상에서”, “2026.05.01 19:24”, “@rooftop.diary”, “바람이 좋은 저녁”.
- Anatomy/layout invariants: face must remain anatomically correct, fingers must look natural and fully formed if hands are visible, and the background must stay softly out of focus to preserve the twilight portrait mood.
- Realism: preserve natural skin texture, believable rooftop scale, correct perspective on railings and skyline, and realistic depth-of-field separation.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness

[INPUT]

- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean office lunchtime candid portrait, colleague-point-of-view daily-life cut, magazine-like slice of workplace realism.
Portrait-oriented social content that feels like an observed lunch break moment in a modern Korean office, enriched with believable desk details, lunch-hour objects, and subtle social-diary graphic labels.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Camera viewpoint should feel like an adjacent coworker standing or seated slightly to the side, using {시점·앵글} to look naturally across the desk rather than directly front-on.
- The main subject occupies about 55–60% of the frame, placed slightly off-center so the lunch setup, desk objects, and office environment remain visible around them.
- Background treatment: gray-and-wood office desk, computer monitor with faint work windows, keyboard, mouse, small potted plant, reusable tumbler, lunch container or convenience-store meal, chopsticks, sticky notes, ID lanyard, neutral office walls, and lightly blurred midday workspace detail.
- Keep a portrait-like office snapshot rhythm with headroom that feels natural, while the desk surface anchors the lower third with realistic lunchtime texture and small everyday items.
- Add subtle social portrait-card details: a small date/location label near one corner, a tiny caption sticker, and 1–2 understated tag-like graphics that feel like a Korean workplace diary post rather than a heavy poster overlay.
- Use {시점·앵글}, {모델 묘사}, {장면}, {라이팅}, {컬러 톤}, {카메라·렌즈}, {비율} placeholders naturally across the composition.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Framing block: build a candid portrait composition from a coworker’s perspective, with the subject framed from upper torso to head, and the desk edge cutting across the lower foreground for lived-in office realism.
2. Subject placement: position {모델 묘사} in a relaxed, mid-action pose — slightly leaning on the desk, holding chopsticks, opening a lunch box, reaching for an iced coffee, or making a small hand gesture — so the moment feels captured rather than posed.
3. Environment detail: keep {장면} clearly readable in the frame with one monitor edge, a keyboard, office stationery, a plant, lunch packaging, a phone facedown or showing a muted notification glow, and a few realistic desk traces that reinforce the lunchtime office setting.
4. Light behavior: use {라이팅} so the face receives soft mixed illumination, with gentle shadow separation on the jawline, subtle highlight on hair and shirt folds, and small reflections on the tumbler, plastic lid, or monitor bezel.
5. Color behavior: apply {컬러 톤} across the whole frame, keeping skin tones natural while the office surfaces sit in muted beige-gray harmony with restrained warm amber accents from wood, coffee, lunch packaging, and sticky-note color.
6. Graphic diary layer: include small Korean on-image text elements that sit lightly on top of the photo, such as a corner date/location label, a short caption, and tiny tag stickers, all aligned cleanly and not covering the face.
7. Capture feel: render with {카메라·렌즈} so the image looks like a quick, realistic workplace snapshot with mild background compression, small handheld imperfections, and a human coworker perspective.
8. Final polish: preserve a casual documentary finish, with no dramatic staging, no fashion-shoot exaggeration, and no overly polished studio look.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard Medium 28–34px for small captions, Pretendard Bold 42–54px only if a slightly larger diary label is needed, and tiny Pretendard Regular 18–22px for micro tags or location/date metadata.
- Required Korean text style: all visible text should be clean, legible Korean, like a social diary card or workplace photo note.
- Suggested on-image Korean text: date/location label “2026.05.01 FRI · 을지로 오피스”, small caption “점심시간, 잠깐의 리셋”, tags “#팀런치” and “#오후도화이팅”.
- Color palette: faded beige, soft gray, warm amber accents, muted wood brown, off-white office neutrals; keep saturation low and matte while allowing natural lunch colors and real object textures.
- Graphic accents: add small rounded label stickers, a subtle translucent beige caption pill, a tiny location-pin icon, or a warm amber dot marker; keep them integrated with the candid photo mood.
- Surface detail: show realistic paper fibers, desk wood grain, matte monitor plastic, condensation on an iced drink, lunch-box plastic, and soft fabric texture on clothing.
- Border/shadow: if any card-like overlay or sticker edge appears, apply a very soft drop shadow with 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 12% opacity.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Fujifilm X-T5, 35mm f/2, ISO 400, f/2.8, handheld casual framing with a realistic office snapshot feel.
- Lighting: mixed office fluorescent ceiling light plus soft natural window light from one side, with the brightest area coming from the window side and a gentle fill across the face.
- Color grade: faded beige and gray base with warm amber micro-accents, slightly lowered contrast, matte magazine-style workplace color treatment.
- Texture realism: preserve natural skin texture, slight hair flyaways, fabric folds, desk dust specks, cup condensation, and faint monitor reflections for a real workplace lunch-hour feeling.
- Depth behavior: softly separate the subject from the background while keeping nearby desk objects recognizable; the coworker POV should feel intimate and casual, not staged.

[6. MOOD]
Indie workplace editorial — a quiet slice-of-life frame that feels like a candid still from a modern Korean office diary or a Kinfolk-style human moment, with the warmth of a real lunch break shared between colleagues.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: render on-image Korean text cleanly and correctly. Use readable strings such as “2026.05.01 FRI · 을지로 오피스”, “점심시간, 잠깐의 리셋”, “#팀런치”, “#오후도화이팅”.
- Text placement: keep date/location, caption, and tags small and secondary; they must not cover the face, hands, or main lunch action.
- Anatomy/layout invariants when relevant: hands must remain anatomically correct with exactly 5 fingers per hand if visible; the coworker-point-of-view angle should stay natural and casual, not distorted or fisheye.
- Maintain {비율} as a vertical portrait social-content composition matching the 1024x1536 output size.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness

- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Dreamy pastel music player background wallpaper, vertical mobile-friendly interface backdrop. Designed as a rich soft visual UI scene for playlist covers, music app promos, lo-fi aesthetic social posts, and dreamy music mood boards.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main player module sits centered, occupying about 52% of the frame height, surrounded by layered pastel atmosphere, floating music-themed stickers, and soft translucent interface details.
- Background is a smooth {배경 그라데이션} with lavender-to-baby-pink depth, faint cloud haze, bokeh glints, translucent bubbles, tiny star specks, and soft vinyl-light reflections.
- Keep the composition tall and balanced, with {플레이어 디자인} as the focal structure and {곡 정보} placed to read clearly near the main module.
- Build a realistic wallpaper-like layout with small decorative playlist labels, micro waveform graphics, lyric snippets, floating note icons, and subtle album-promo details around the player.
- Include a compact bottom metadata area with a date label, playlist tag, and tiny credit text so the image feels like a finished music-poster UI rather than a blank mockup.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Top zone (upper 20%): soft gradient field with faint cloud-like haze, tiny star specks drifting diagonally, a small rounded label reading "DREAM TAPE VOL.03", and a tiny date mark "2026.05 / SEOUL".
- Center zone (middle 55%): render {플레이어 디자인} as a polished dreamy interface object, with a circular LP or cassette illustration, glossy album-art surface, clean song title and artist text, a slim progress bar, visible play button, previous/next controls, small shuffle/repeat icons, and soft reflections.
- Song card details: place {곡 정보} as the main song metadata, supported by short Korean UI text such as "새벽의 멜로디", "아티스트: 루나웨이", "03:24", "dream pop mix", and a tiny label "오늘의 추천곡".
- Info strip (around center-lower): place {곡 정보} in small, crisp text aligned with the player module, maintaining clear hierarchy and easy readability; add tiny credit text "Cover by pastel studio" and "playlist no. 247".
- Decorative layer (throughout background): apply {포인트 디테일} as scattered micro doodles, tiny hearts, stars, music notes, crescent moons, floating stickers, pearl-like dots, glassy blur flares, and miniature waveform ribbons that feel suspended in air.
- Bottom zone (lower 18%): include a soft mini tracklist preview with 3 short Korean lines: "01 꿈의 파도", "02 별빛 산책", "03 안녕, 여름밤", plus a small rounded CTA-style tag "지금 재생 중".
- Typography layer: set all text using {텍스트 폰트}, with thin elegant letterforms for the interface, slightly bolder Korean song title, and tiny editorial microtext for realism.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Inter Light or Helvetica Neue Thin for English UI text, with Pretendard Light for small Korean support text; use 22–34px for main labels, 12–16px for secondary details, and 8–10px for tiny credit and metadata text.
- Color palette: use lavender #c9b8e0, baby pink #ffd9e6, soft lilac #eadff7, milk white #fff9fc, pale rose accent highlights, and occasional powder-blue glints for depth.
- Border/shadow: use translucent rounded glass panels, soft ambient glow around the player with a 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 16% opacity drop shadow, subtle inner highlights, and delicate glossy reflections.
- UI detail density: include believable music-player micro elements such as timestamps, equalizer bars, small playlist chips, waveform fragments, and lyric-sticker accents while preserving the centered vertical hierarchy.
- Text rendering: Korean text should look printed or rendered directly into the graphic, not handwritten unless {텍스트 폰트} implies a handwritten style.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: front-facing digital poster composition, equivalent to an 85mm f/1.8 portrait look with very shallow depth feel and clean graphic focus.
- Lighting: soft diffused studio light from upper-left with a faint secondary fill from lower-right, plus subtle luminous bloom around the central player and small glass highlights on UI surfaces.
- Color grade: pastel lavender-pink grade with milky highlights, low contrast, slightly hazy highlights, soft bloom, and a dreamy UI finish.
- Rendering quality: polished high-resolution digital artwork with realistic glassmorphism, layered translucent materials, soft grain, detailed typography, and gentle depth separation between foreground player, midground stickers, and background haze.

[6. MOOD]
Dream-pop playlist cover — a soft editorial blend of Tokyo stationery branding, pastel album-promo graphics, cozy bedroom listening mood, and Y2K digital UI nostalgia.

[7. CRITICAL]

[1. PURPOSE]
Cinematic urban portrait poster of a young Korean office worker in rainy Gangnam at night, designed like a real Seoul noir film still with premium editorial-poster finish.
Vertical single-subject portrait optimized for social sharing and poster readability, enriched with authentic rainy-street detail, believable city signage, and subtle Korean poster typography.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Subject placement: {모델 묘사} occupies the central 55–60% of the frame, framed from mid-thigh or waist-up depending on crop, with the face kept in the upper-center third for strong poster impact.
- Pose direction: {자세} with a natural shoulder angle, slight head turn, and a tense-but-composed expression that feels captured mid-moment after leaving work late at night.
- Background treatment: {배경} rendered as layered Gangnam street depth: wet asphalt reflections, neon color bleed, taxi brake lights, crosswalk stripes, bus-stop glass, convenience-store glow, raindrops on nearby surfaces, and subtle mist.
- Scene context: {장면} presented as a real urban night environment, with depth separation between subject and city lights; include passing silhouettes, car light streaks, puddles, curb reflections, and rain-slick building façades to make the location feel lived-in.
- Framing: use a cinematic vertical poster frame with readable upper and lower poster areas: title and issue/date details near the top or side, small credits and barcode-style block near the bottom, without covering the subject’s eyes or key facial expression.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Main portrait layer — {모델 묘사} placed as the hero subject, sharply focused with realistic skin texture, rain-sheened hair strands, fine droplets on eyelashes and coat fabric, damp collar edges, and believable office-worker styling.
2. Pose and expression layer — {자세} to imply motion and weather resistance, with the gaze angled slightly off-camera for a cinematic pause rather than a direct ad-style look.
3. Environment layer — {장면} anchored by wet pavement, blurred storefront neon, crosswalk paint, taxi tail lamps, bus-stop reflections, faint office-tower windows, and passing car light streaks that create depth behind the subject.
4. Background atmosphere — {배경} built with layered reflections, diffuse haze, rain trails, glass reflections, out-of-focus street signs, and low-contrast city lights so the subject remains the visual anchor while the world feels real.
5. Lighting layer — {라이팅} to create a strong side contour on the face and shoulders, with rain highlights catching on hair, coat fabric, cheekbones, and the umbrella-less silhouette edges.
6. Color layer — {컬러 톤} applied across shadows, reflections, typography, and highlights for a filmic night-city contrast without oversaturation.
7. Camera realism layer — {카메라·렌즈} with shallow depth of field, crisp subject separation, natural low-light grain, slight handheld street-photo energy, and realistic motion blur only on background cars and rain streaks.
8. Format layer — {비율·구도} maintained as a tall portrait with cinematic headroom, balanced lower-frame street context, and poster information integrated like a premium Korean cinema key visual.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: add refined Korean poster/editorial text using Pretendard SemiBold, Noto Sans KR Bold, or a clean Korean gothic typeface; combine one large title line with small issue/date/credit lines and a barcode-style information block.
- Main title text: set bold Korean cover/poster line such as “강남, 비가 내린 밤” in crisp white or pale cyan, aligned vertically along one side or placed in the upper third.
- Supporting poster details: include small realistic text elements such as “VOL.282”, “2026.05.01”, “SEOUL NIGHT PORTRAIT”, “모델: 김지아”, “퇴근 후 11:42 PM”, and a small barcode area with tiny production-credit text at the bottom.
- Color palette: use deep teal, charcoal, amber, muted cyan, wet asphalt gray, and neon magenta accents derived from {컬러 톤}; let the palette appear in street reflections, signage glow, typography, and rain highlights.
- Graphic treatment: allow thin editorial divider lines, small corner registration marks, a subtle film-poster credit strip, tiny location/date labels, and a barcode block, all integrated naturally with the rainy cinematic portrait.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Canon R5 look, 50mm f/1.4, ISO 1600, f/1.8, 1/200, shallow depth of field with realistic low-light city portrait rendering.
- Lighting: neon backlight combined with street-lamp side light, with reflected fill from wet pavement and a faint rim highlight on hair and coat edges.
- Color grade: cinematic teal-orange grading inspired by Cinestill 800T night photography, with cool cyan shadows and warm amber practical lights.
- Material realism: emphasize wet wool or trench-coat texture, damp hair separation, transparent rain streaks, puddle reflections, glass glare, asphalt grit, and tiny droplets catching neon light.
- Poster finish: premium Korean noir one-sheet aesthetic, high-resolution editorial sharpness on the face, soft bokeh background, natural film grain, and believable optical imperfections from rain and low light.

[6. MOOD]
Rain-soaked urban film still — a Park Chan-wook / Korean noir poster mood with the polished night-city tension of modern Seoul cinema, late-night office fatigue, and the feeling of one private moment inside a busy Gangnam street.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: render Korean text cleanly and legibly. Use short exact strings such as “강남, 비가 내린 밤”, “모델: 김지아”, “퇴근 후 11:42 PM”, “2026.05.01”, and “오늘도 지나간다”.
- Poster detail accuracy: include a believable small barcode-style block, issue/date label “VOL.282”, compact credit text, and 2–3 short Korean feature blurbs such as “비 오는 도시의 얼굴”, “퇴근길의 긴장”, “서울의 밤빛”.
- Anatomy/layout invariants: face, hands, and hair must look anatomically correct; if one hand is visible, fingers must be natural and complete; rain should not obscure the facial expression.
- Preserve the impression of a real late-night Gangnam street scene, not a studio set; background signage, vehicles, reflections, and pedestrians should feel photographic and location-specific.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness
