[1. PURPOSE]
Technical specification exploded-view sheet for products and vehicles, designed like a printed engineering manual page with a realistic title block, bill of materials, revision metadata, and assembly notes. Detailed reference-style diagram for documentation, assembly guidance, catalog presentation, or service manual use.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: {대상 사물} as the central technical object, occupying about 55–65% of the canvas width.
- Composition: {분해 모드} with all parts spaced along a vertical or diagonal assembly axis, each component floating at consistent intervals so the assembly order is visually readable.
- Labels: {라벨링} placed beside each part with thin leader lines that point to the exact attachment point; include part codes such as A-01, B-03, C-12.
- Background: {배경} with engineering-paper grid, coordinate ticks, small crosshair marks, dimension rulers, and a realistic printed-sheet texture.
- Document header: Add a top title block reading “{문서 제목}”, with model name “{모델명}”, drawing number “{도면 번호}”, revision “{개정 번호}”, date “{작성일}”, scale “{축척}”, and page mark “{페이지 표기}”.
- Data panels: Add a right-side or bottom bill-of-materials table titled “{부품표 제목}” with 6–10 rows, including 번호, 부품명, 재질, 수량, 비고; add a small notes panel with “{정비 메모}”.
- Typography placement: {텍스트 폰트} used for captions, item numbers, part names, title block, BOM table, and engineering notes, aligned with precise grid spacing.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Center field: Render {대상 사물} as a detailed exploded diagram, with the largest body shell near the center and smaller internal parts arranged outward in logical assembly sequence.
2. Part hierarchy: Separate major assemblies first, then subcomponents, then tiny fasteners; preserve consistent spacing so the viewer can trace how the object reassembles.
3. Annotation system: Add {라벨링} to every visible component, using fine arrow lines, small numerals, compact bilingual part names, part codes, and callout bubbles when appropriate.
4. Surface treatment: Use {라인 톤}; keep materials realistic or lightly illustrative, with clear edges, accurate proportions, screws, brackets, rubber seals, wiring, clips, lenses, panels, and fasteners rendered as distinct pieces.
5. Background detail: Use {배경} as a technical sheet backdrop with coordinate grid, crop marks, ruler ticks, small inset detail boxes, and faint blueprint-style measurement guides.
6. Specification panels: Include a title block, revision strip, material legend, BOM table, and one or two enlarged inset diagrams showing tiny assemblies such as bolt sequence, gasket layer, hinge mechanism, connector pin layout, or wheel/brake module.
7. Readability layer: Ensure all text remains sharp and mechanically aligned; use consistent leader-line weight, table grid lines, numbered callout circles, and clear correspondence between labels and parts.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: {텍스트 폰트} with regular to medium weight, small caption size, tight but readable line height, and crisp vector-like rendering.
- Color palette: {배경} plus black, charcoal, cool gray, steel silver, pale blueprint blue, and restrained red/orange warning accent for important callouts.
- Technical markings: Include realistic drawing metadata such as “DWG”, “REV”, “SCALE”, “SHEET”, tolerance notes, torque values, material abbreviations, and inspection check boxes.
- Border/shadow: Use fine technical border lines, title-block dividers, table rules, and extremely subtle part shadows when needed for separation, such as 2px y-offset, 8px blur, 10% opacity.
- Detail density: The sheet should feel like a believable engineering documentation page, with useful annotations, measurements, codes, and assembly notes rather than a plain product render.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: front-facing technical product-shot perspective, equivalent to an 85mm lens or a corrected orthographic render to minimize distortion and keep proportions accurate.
- Lighting: even studio lighting from both sides with soft overhead fill, no dramatic shadows, no colored gels, and high edge clarity for small parts.
- Color grade: neutral white, steel gray, charcoal, and blueprint blue accents, with controlled contrast and zero cinematic warmth.

[6. MOOD]
Precision engineering catalog plate — like an MIT design lab schematic mixed with a premium industrial product manual, with authentic Korean service-manual details and production-ready specification tables.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: all rendered captions must be clean, fully legible, and free of broken Korean characters.
- Include readable Korean title and metadata: “{문서 제목}”, “모델명: {모델명}”, “도면번호: {도면 번호}”, “개정: {개정 번호}”, “작성일: {작성일}”, “축척: {축척}”, “{페이지 표기}”.
- Include a parts table with realistic Korean entries such as “프론트 하우징”, “알루미늄 프레임”, “고무 실링”, “M4 육각볼트”, “센서 모듈”, “브래킷”, “와이어 하네스”, “커버 패널”.
- Every leader line must point to the exact matching part; label text, part code, and target component must correspond one-to-one.
- The exploded layout must remain logically ordered, with no missing parts, no merged parts, and no visually ambiguous assembly relationships.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or recognizable public figures
- Incorrect arrow-to-part mapping

[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Photorealistic paparazzi-style wedding after-party cut, vertical editorial scene for viral social posts and Threads-style sharing.
Korean couple running toward camera in a glamorous late-night city street, captured like an intrusive celebrity photo just outside an after-party venue.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Subject placement: {커플 묘사} occupies the lower-middle 55% of the frame, moving diagonally from background depth toward the lens, with flash bloom, flying veil edges, and urgent body language filling the vertical frame.
- Background treatment: {배경} with wet reflective pavement, blurred car headlights, neon signage, faint mist, hotel-lounge entrance glow, valet area, and glossy black cars forming a believable late-night urban corridor.
- Spacing and framing: {비율·구도} with paparazzi perspective, slight low-angle tilt, tight street-side crop, imperfect horizon, and the feeling that the photographer stepped into the curb lane at the last second.
- Action emphasis: {장면} should read instantly as a candid post-party escape, with motion in the veil, dress hem, tuxedo lapels, bouquet ribbon, and clasped hands.
- Environmental realism: include {환경 소품} and {주변 인물} as secondary details, partially flash-lit or motion-blurred, never stealing focus from the couple.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Foreground flash zone: intense direct flash burst from camera position, catching facial highlights, dress sequins, bouquet petals, tuxedo velvet pile, raindrops on fabric, and wet asphalt reflections; keep the flash realistic and harsh, not beauty-soft.
- Couple focus zone: {커플 묘사} rendered with sharp facial realism, natural Korean features, slightly wind-tousled hair, believable skin texture, flushed cheeks, and spontaneous laugh expression.
- Motion cues: {장면} with subtle motion blur on running legs, fluttering veil, swinging bouquet, loose bow tie, and a trailing coat hem, while faces and linked hands remain mostly sharp.
- Street layer: {배경} extending into a dark urban corridor with glossy parked black cars, valet cones, taxi glow, diffuse neon color blocks, damp curb texture, and thin atmospheric haze.
- Text-in-world layer: natural physical Korean signage and printed details only, including {장소명}, {간판 문구}, {행사 날짜}, and {커플 이름} on believable surfaces such as a venue sign, valet board, small invitation card, or window reflection.
- Lighting layer: {라이팅} as the dominant look, with hard frontal flash overpowering ambient light, colder night-time base, and small warm pools from street lamps and venue sconces.
- Camera layer: {카메라·렌즈} captured as a real candid editorial photo, with flash falloff, slight grain, imperfect edge crop, and tabloid-style immediacy.
- Framing layer: {비율·구도} with energetic diagonal composition, visible foreground curb texture, flash-lit puddles, cropped bystanders, and layered reflections adding depth.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: no designed graphic overlay; all readable text must be physically present in the photographed world, printed or lit on real objects, with clean Korean rendering.
- Color palette: cold white flash, blue-gray asphalt, neon cyan, muted magenta, warm amber streetlight, deep black tuxedo tones, ivory veil highlights, red tail-light streaks, and silver highlights from sequins.
- Texture/detail: preserve tactile realism in wet asphalt, velvet tuxedo, sequined dress, bouquet petals, smeared mascara edge, champagne droplets, paper invitation stock, car paint reflections, and flash-lit skin texture.
- Border/shadow: use the natural photographic frame with hard flash shadows under chins, behind legs, beneath shoes, and on nearby car doors, plus glossy reflections on wet ground.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Canon R5, 50mm f/1.8, ISO 1600, 1/200, direct on-camera flash; candid street photography look with visible flash falloff.
- Lighting: harsh paparazzi flash from the camera front, strong contrast, deep shadow pockets, plus faint warm street practicals, reflected car headlights, small secondary paparazzi flashes, and cool urban ambient fill.
- Color grade: cool white and steel-blue base with warm sodium-vapor accents, neon reflections, slightly crushed blacks, subtle grain, and glossy tabloid realism.

[6. MOOD]
{무드} — elite after-party paparazzi capture, like a glossy tabloid frame from a late-night K-drama premiere aftermath, with cinematic chaos, celebrity energy, rain-slick romance, and mischievous escape momentum.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: render scene text clearly and naturally: venue sign “{장소명}”, valet board “발렛 파킹”, taxi light “심야택시”, small invitation/card text “{커플 이름} · {행사 날짜}”, and neon/window text “{간판 문구}”.
- Anatomy/layout invariants: faces must look like real Korean bride and groom, anatomically correct hands, exactly 5 fingers per hand, no extra limbs, no warped bouquet stems, no duplicated people.
- The couple must clearly feel like they are running toward the camera together, with linked movement, shared laughter, and believable forward momentum.
- Keep the image as a real paparazzi photograph, not a posed wedding catalog image; include environmental messiness such as puddles, valet cones, blurred guests, confetti scraps, and flash glare.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity face composites or real public figure likeness
- Counterfeit press ID cards or fake legal documents

[INPUT]

- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Create a cinematic 3-panel vertical sequence from one portrait reference image, designed like a film still storyboard for social sharing, diary-style profile content, and editorial mood.
Preserve the subject identity exactly while turning an ordinary moment into a late-afternoon cafe narrative with small realistic details, tactile props, and gentle on-image Korean diary labels.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject placement: the same person appears across all 3 panels, with the figure occupying about 55–65% of each panel depending on the cut; face, hairstyle, age impression, body silhouette, and distinctive features must stay consistent with {원본 보존}.
- Panel structure: vertical 3-cut sequence, stacked top-to-bottom with refined cinematic gutters; each cut has a distinct framing scale that follows {컷 흐름}.
- Background treatment: late-afternoon cafe window scene guided by {시퀀스 무드}, including warm interior wood, glass bottles, flowers, books, teacups, dessert plate, spoon, folded receipt, napkin, condensation on glass, window reflections, and tableware arranged naturally as described in {감성 오브젝트}.
- Composition flow: use window light, tabletop lines, hand movement, cup steam, and book edges to lead the eye from panel 1 to panel 3; the panels should feel like consecutive frames from the same quiet afternoon.
- Social diary detail: add a small date/location label and short Korean caption from {날짜·장소 라벨} and {짧은 캡션}, integrated like a tasteful film diary overlay rather than a poster.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Panel 1 (wide establishing shot): show the person in the cafe environment with the window, table, books, flowers, bottles, a teacup or latte, and small lived-in details such as a receipt, bookmark, pastry crumbs, or water ring; subject feels situated in a real cafe space.
- Panel 2 (medium shot): crop to a half-body view with a small action moment, such as turning a page, pausing with a cup, touching the book spine, brushing hair aside, or looking away in thought; keep posture and facial identity aligned with {원본 보존}.
- Panel 3 (close-up detail shot): focus on hands, teacup, book edge, flower stem, spoon reflection, steamed glass, or a quiet facial detail; emphasize tactile realism, natural skin texture, porcelain reflections, paper fibers, and soft depth separation.
- Lighting continuity: apply the same visual lighting logic across all panels using {라이팅}, with visible atmospheric glow, mild flare, window reflection, and natural light falloff that feels physically consistent.
- Tone continuity: all three panels must share the same filmic grade defined by {컬러·톤}, with consistent highlight warmth, shadow color, contrast, grain, and saturation.
- Camera realism: maintain a photographed, not illustrated, look; use the stated capture feel of Sony A7R V with a 50mm f/1.4 and ISO 400 aesthetic, plus slight handheld softness, organic film imperfections, and believable optical depth.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: include very small Korean film-diary typography: frame numbers from {프레임 라벨}, a date/location label from {날짜·장소 라벨}, and one short caption from {짧은 캡션}; use thin off-white or faded beige text with slight print softness, placed along a gutter edge or lower corner without covering the face.
- Color palette: warm amber, faded cyan, cream beige, muted wood brown, soft shadow gray, with the exact tonal direction of {컬러·톤}.
- Panel separation: subtle cinematic panel gutters with soft editorial print-like shadow, approximately 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity; the layout should feel like a vertical film strip or magazine diary spread.
- Surface texture: lightly faded film grain, faint dust specks, gentle halation, small lens bloom, tabletop patina, paper texture, cup reflections, and natural cafe glass reflections; keep the finish like a printed cinema editorial spread.
- Decorative tags: add 1–2 tiny diary-style tags from {데코 태그} such as a handwritten sticker label, small dot marker, or faint film code, harmonized with the warm cafe scene.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Sony A7R V look, 50mm f/1.4, ISO 400; panel 1 feels like a 50mm environmental portrait, panel 2 a tighter mid-shot, panel 3 a close detail crop with shallow depth of field.
- Lighting: late-afternoon natural light entering from the window side as backlight or side light, with visible lens flare, light bloom, floating dust particles, window reflections, and soft steam highlights; keep the illumination direction coherent across all 3 panels.
- Color grade: Kodak Portra 400-inspired warm amber highlights with softly faded cyan shadows, low-contrast filmic roll-off, restrained saturation, mild halation around highlights, and a tactile analog print feeling.

[6. MOOD]
Late-afternoon cinematic cafe still — a quiet frame from a Wong Kar-wai-inspired mood board mixed with Kinfolk editorial softness, personal diary warmth, and realistic cafe atmosphere.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: all visible Korean text must be clean and legible. Use exact rendered examples such as “{날짜·장소 라벨}”, “{짧은 캡션}”, “{프레임 라벨}”, and “{데코 태그}”.
- Identity/layout invariants: the person’s face, hairstyle, age impression, and overall identity must remain consistent with {원본 보존}; all 3 panels must clearly read as one connected sequence with matching color grading.
- The 3 panels must follow the wide / medium / close-up progression from {컷 흐름}.
- Realistic details must support the cafe story: condensation, cup steam, paper fibers, table scratches, reflections, crumbs, receipts, and flowers should look physically present, not pasted on.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals, fake certificates, or misleading institutional marks
- Broken Korean characters, garbled Hangul, or unreadable text
- Celebrity composites or transforming the reference person into a different public figure

studio:prompts3:ours-265.content:
[INPUT]
- reference_image: {참고 이미지}
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Create a tiny-planet fisheye travel selfie collage from one attached selfie, preserving the person’s identity while making it look like a vivid real city-travel memory captured during a busy sightseeing day.
Designed as a shareable portrait-plus-landmark souvenir image with strong travel-postcard energy, layered with authentic travel ephemera, date labels, captions, stickers, and city-specific details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: {원본 보존} must be the clear focal point, placed slightly above the center at the top of the spherical tiny-planet, with realistic selfie posture and natural facial perspective.
- City wraparound: {여행 도시·랜드마크} should curve around the lower half of the frame as a circular horizon ring, creating the classic tiny-planet effect with recognizable street life, vehicles, signs, pavement, trees, lamps, and skyline fragments.
- Perspective: {구도} with the subject occupying roughly 20–25% of the frame and the landmarks forming a continuous orbit around them like a panoramic sightseeing loop.
- Lens feel: {렌즈} with exaggerated edge bending, radial compression near the center, and the surrounding city visibly warped into a globe-like panorama.
- Stamp and label area: integrate {스탬프 효과} in the upper-right sky area without covering the face, as if stamped onto the printed travel selfie; add a small date/location label nearby reading "2026.05.01 · 런던" and a tiny handle "@travel.diary".
- Collage details: add realistic postcard-style overlays such as a small torn ticket stub, map-pin sticker, subtle washi-tape corner, tiny caption tag reading "오늘의 순간", and a handwritten-style Korean note "나다운 여행 기록" while keeping the face and landmarks readable.
- Background treatment: natural sky and urban color field with smooth film-like fade, believable clouds, atmospheric depth, and real street textures that support the travel snapshot feeling.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Center hero: preserve the attached selfie person’s facial identity exactly, keep the face sharp and natural, and place them slightly above the tiny-planet center.
2. Planet body: bend the full city scene into a spherical ring so {여행 도시·랜드마크} appear miniaturized yet recognizable around the lower perimeter, including sidewalks, crosswalk stripes, building façades, railings, street signs, greenery, and moving-tourist ambience.
3. Landmark placement: position iconic elements like Big Ben, the London Eye, a red double-decker bus, and a red phone booth at different points of the orbit for clear visual variety, with small realistic details such as window reflections, stone texture, clock-face detail, bus route signage, and streetlight silhouettes.
4. Lens distortion: apply strong fisheye warping consistent with an 8mm ultra-wide look, with the highest curvature at the frame edges and the least distortion at the subject center.
5. Travel mark: place {스탬프 효과} at the upper-right, printed like a vintage passport stamp in slightly uneven ink, with "VISITED", city name, and date readable; add a smaller secondary stamp line in Korean such as "여행 인증".
6. Caption system: include small decorative travel-card text blocks: "런던 산책", "하루 한 장면", "CITY SNAP", and "#여행기록 #셀카콜라주" in compact supporting type, arranged like stickers around the sky and planet edge.
7. Color finish: keep {컬러 톤} with restrained saturation, gentle contrast, a lightly faded film print texture, warm reds preserved, and tactile postcard-paper grain.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use bold condensed sans-serif for the stamp, with a secondary small text line in a clean Noto Sans KR style; keep lettering compact and travel-postcard-like.
- Korean caption text: render short Korean labels clearly: "오늘의 순간", "나다운 여행 기록", "런던 산책", "하루 한 장면", "여행 인증", plus small hashtag-style text "#여행기록 #셀카콜라주".
- Color palette: deep red, London bus red, navy, warm gray, cream paper white, muted steel blue, all aligned to {컬러 톤}.
- Border/shadow: subtle soft shadow under the spherical planet form, with a faint 2–4px blur and low-opacity vignette to emphasize depth.
- Print treatment: lightly grainy film texture, faded highlights, slightly desaturated analog postcard finish, soft ink bleed on the stamp, realistic tape translucency, and tiny paper fibers in overlay elements.
- Realism: keep all overlays physically plausible as printed or sticker-like elements on a travel collage, with soft shadows, slight misalignment, and varied paper opacity.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 8mm fisheye ultra-wide travel selfie look, strong barrel distortion, high center sharpness, edge stretching similar to a GoPro fisheye / action-cam panorama.
- Lighting: daylight travel lighting with soft overcast diffusion or open-shade city light, even skin tones, no harsh flash, mild edge rim from ambient sky reflection.
- Color grade: natural urban colors with a slightly faded film scan look, subtle teal-gray shadows, warm reds preserved, and moderate highlight roll-off.
- Texture realism: visible city materials such as stone, glass, metal railings, asphalt, bus paint, phone-booth gloss, and soft sky haze should remain present after fisheye bending.

[6. MOOD]
Travel souvenir editorial — like a stylish tourist postcard meets a social-media fisheye selfie, with a playful but polished city-memory feel. The image should feel like a real day out: energetic, personal, slightly nostalgic, and full of small travel-record details.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구가 정확히 보여야 함: "VISITED", 도시명, 날짜, "오늘의 순간", "나다운 여행 기록", "런던 산책", "하루 한 장면", "여행 인증"
- Preserve the subject’s face and identity from the reference photo exactly; do not change facial structure, age impression, or recognizable features.
- The tiny-planet layout must remain spherical, with the person centered above the orbiting city and the landmarks wrapped around the lower half.
- The stamp must stay in the upper-right area and remain fully legible.
- All added stickers, captions, date labels, ticket-stub details, and map-pin graphics must support the travel selfie collage and must not cover the eyes, nose, mouth, or key landmarks.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized likeness replacement

[INPUT]
- reference_image: {참고 이미지}
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean encouragement coupon set for personal gifting, 4-panel 2x2 grid, using the attached portrait as the same person across every panel.
Designed as a warm anniversary / birthday / consolation card that feels like a handmade keepsake, but with realistic printed-coupon details such as serial numbers, date labels, tiny usage notes, stickers, perforation marks, and tactile paper texture.
The final image should feel like a finished personal gift sheet photographed on premium stationery, suitable for {용도}, with {텍스트 톤} kept affectionate, sincere, and natural.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- The canvas is a vertical 2x2 grid with four equal coupon panels, following {레이아웃}; each panel occupies roughly 48% of the width/height with narrow cream gutters between cards.
- Keep {원본 보존} as the top priority: the face, body type, hair, and overall identity must remain consistent across all four panels.
- Each panel should contain one realistic printed coupon card with a warm pastel background, a clear person image or illustration cutout, and a coupon title + short explanation + small coupon metadata.
- Use {쿠폰 4종} as the four coupon themes, arranged so each card feels distinct but visually unified.
- Background outside the cards should be a soft cream-beige paper field with visible premium stationery grain, faint fibers, gentle shadows, and a few subtle handmade details such as washi tape corners, tiny heart stickers, clipped paper tabs, or pencil-like doodle marks.
- Add realistic coupon features: small serial number, “사용기한”, “받는 사람”, “1회 사용 가능”, tiny barcode/QR-like decorative block, dotted cut line, and a small check box area.
- Keep the person visually dominant in each panel, integrated with the coupon design through shadows, cutout edges, and overlapping text plaques.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Panel 1 (top-left): massage coupon card, with the same person shown in a relaxed massage / care-giving pose; card background in coral pastel. Place the title near the top, add a small caption below, and include details such as “No. COUPON-001”, “사용기한: 오늘부터 1년”, and “피로한 날 바로 사용”.
- Panel 2 (top-right): meal-treat coupon card, with the same person in a friendly eating or serving pose; use mint pastel background and keep the text layout consistent with panel 1. Add a small illustrated plate, spoon, steam doodle, price-tag style label “₩0 마음결제”, and detail line “메뉴 선택권 포함”.
- Panel 3 (bottom-left): hug coupon card, with the same person in a gentle embrace pose; use lilac pastel background, soft shadowing, and centered visual balance. Add a small heart sticker, dotted border accent, “즉시 사용 가능”, and a tiny note area reading “힘든 날 꺼내 쓰기”.
- Panel 4 (bottom-right): walk-date coupon card, with the same person in a light walking pose; use warm beige or pale peach background, with the title aligned to match the other cards. Add small walking-route doodles, a mini calendar tag, venue-style line “동네 한 바퀴 또는 좋아하는 길”, and “날씨 좋은 날 추천”.
- Make all four panels feel like they belong to one set through matched corner radius, identical margin rhythm, repeated typography placement, shared micro-label system, and consistent print shadows.
- If text is layered on top of the person image, keep it separated by clear spacing and use semi-opaque cream or pastel text plaques for readability.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard SemiBold for coupon titles, 30–36px; Pretendard Regular or Noto Sans KR for descriptions and metadata, 16–22px; optional hand-drawn accent font only for tiny decorative marks and affectionate sticker labels.
- Color palette: use {컬러 톤} while preserving cream beige #F4EBDD, coral #F4A79B, mint #BFE7D3, lilac #D9C7F0, pale peach #F8D9C6, charcoal text #2F2A28, off-white paper #FFF8EF, muted rose #D87973.
- Border/shadow: each card with rounded corners, 18–24px radius, soft drop shadow 0 8px 20px rgba(0,0,0,0.10), thin off-white border for separation, subtle paper edge thickness, and faint printed ink texture.
- Keep all visible main text in Korean, with simple personal gift-card styling rather than commercial ad-copy styling.
- Add small realistic stationery elements inside the design: dotted perforation lines, tiny checkboxes, micro barcode area, circular date stamp graphic without implying official certification, hand-drawn hearts, stars, food steam lines, walking route dots, and small corner tapes.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: natural portrait photography feel, Canon EOS R5 with 85mm f/1.2 lens look, shallow depth of field, realistic subject cutout edges, gentle contact shadows where the portrait overlaps coupon graphics.
- Lighting: soft window light from upper-left at about 45°, gentle fill from front-right, no harsh highlights, even skin tone preservation, realistic paper shadows in card gutters.
- Color grade: pastel stationery palette with creamy whites, muted coral, mint, and lilac; low contrast, slightly desaturated, print-friendly, warm personal keepsake finish.
- Surface realism: matte paper, faint grain, subtle printed halftone/ink absorption, soft raised sticker edges, slight curl or thickness on coupon cards.

[6. MOOD]
A handmade personal gift-card set with the polished warmth of a Korean stationery brand and the gentle editorial feel of Kinfolk-style layout design, enriched with sincere everyday details that make the coupons feel actually usable and personally prepared.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구가 정확하게 보여야 함:
  - 마사지 1회권
  - 밥 사주기
  - 꽉 안아주기
  - 산책 데이트
- Additional Korean text should be readable and realistic, such as “받는 사람: 당신”, “발행일: 2026.05.01”, “사용기한: 오늘부터 1년”, “1회 사용 가능”, “마음이 필요할 때 꺼내 쓰기”, “No. COUPON-001”.
- Identity consistency: all four panels must show the same person based on {원본 보존}; do not change face shape, hairstyle, or body proportions.
- All 4 panels must remain a consistent 2x2 coupon grid with matching card structure and readable Korean typography.
- The result must look like a real printed personal coupon sheet photographed or rendered with tactile paper, sticker, shadow, and ink detail, not a sterile flat mockup.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness

[1. PURPOSE]
Japanese lifestyle magazine cover, A4 vertical editorial front page for a calm living-and-design publication. Photoreal magazine cover suitable for i2i portrait substitution, with a premium printed-paper layout, realistic editorial cover information, and a restrained tonal palette.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: {표지 인물} placed slightly right of center, occupying about 42% of the frame height, with the gaze directed just past camera for a quiet editorial feel.
- Cover masthead: {잡지 이름} at the top-left in a compact serif treatment, clearly legible and integrated with the editorial grid.
- Issue metadata: {이슈 번호}, {발행일}, {가격} positioned around the masthead and upper-right, like a real monthly lifestyle magazine.
- Main feature title: {특집 제목} and {메인 헤드라인} placed across the lower-middle or lower-left area, sized as the primary cover story without hiding the face.
- Feature headlines: {서브 헤드라인 1}, {서브 헤드라인 2}, {서브 헤드라인 3} arranged in two slim editorial text groups on the left and right edges of the portrait.
- Background scene: {배경·소품} arranged on a warm wood surface, with lived-in domestic details that naturally belong in a Japanese lifestyle cover.
- Barcode and print details: place a small barcode block with {바코드 번호} near the lower-right corner, plus a tiny printer note and page-style micro text for magazine realism.
- Spine credit: {스파인 크레딧} set vertically along the far left edge like a real printed magazine spine marker.
- Color atmosphere: {컬러 톤} across the paper, props, and shadows, with subtle depth rather than strong contrast.
- Typography system: {타이포} applied as a refined magazine hierarchy with Japanese-lifestyle editorial balance.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header zone (top 14%): place {잡지 이름} as the masthead in a compact serif style; add {이슈 번호}, {발행일}, and {가격} as small publication metadata nearby with careful tracking.
2. Portrait zone (center 58%): render {표지 인물} as the primary cover subject, cropped from mid-torso upward, with natural skin texture, relaxed posture, and a believable magazine-photo finish.
3. Still-life layer (lower-left and lower-mid): arrange {배경·소품} so the wood table, flower vase, ceramic mug, open book, folded linen, and small household objects form a quiet diagonal leading line toward the subject.
4. Cover-story zone (middle-lower 28%): typeset {특집 제목}, {메인 헤드라인}, and the three feature headlines as real cover blurbs, mixing Korean serif text with tiny English support notes.
5. Print-commerce zone (bottom 8%): include the barcode with {바코드 번호}, tiny issue price {가격}, printer registration micro-marks, and a small publisher line; keep these elements realistic and secondary.
6. Spine and edge detail: add {스파인 크레딧} vertically along the left edge, with a faint paper-edge tone and slight offset-print softness.
7. Print realism: include subtle paper grain, faint ink softness, tiny halftone texture in shadow areas, and slight tonal variation like a real offset-printed cover, not a digitally over-sharpened composite.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Noto Serif KR or 본명조 for Korean editorial copy, Garamond or Playfair Display for English support text, and a small serif masthead style for the magazine name; keep weights medium to regular with clear editorial hierarchy.
- Cover text hierarchy: masthead first, issue metadata second, main feature third, supporting headlines fourth, barcode and spine credit fifth.
- Color palette: use {컬러 톤} with concrete tones such as ivory #f3ece0, warm oak brown, mist gray, tea beige, and soft charcoal for text.
- Editorial details: include issue number, publication date, price, barcode, two to three Korean feature headlines, a tiny publisher note, and vertical spine credit to make the cover feel physically printed.
- Border/shadow: add a barely visible soft drop shadow under the subject, about 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 12% opacity, plus a faint paper-edge vignette for print realism.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Hasselblad X2D 100c with 80mm f/4, medium-format editorial portrait framing, crisp but gentle detail.
- Lighting: soft north-facing window light from upper-left at roughly 45°, with a weak bounce fill from lower-right and no hard specular highlights.
- Color grade: muted ivory, oak, tea beige, and cool gray with slightly lifted blacks and low saturation, matching a restrained Japanese lifestyle editorial look.

[6. MOOD]
Quiet Japanese lifestyle editorial — calm living, handmade objects, morning-window light, thoughtful domestic rituals, and a premium printed-paper atmosphere.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 표지에 반드시 아래 문구가 정확히 렌더되어야 함: "일상의 정성", "느리게 고르는 물건", "집 안의 작은 계절", "차와 책이 있는 오후".
- Issue realism: "{이슈 번호}", "{발행일}", "{가격}", "{바코드 번호}"가 실제 잡지 표지처럼 작게 포함되어야 함.
- Cover layout invariants: magazine cover must remain vertical A4 proportion, the portrait must be the dominant focal point, and the overall design must look like a real printed magazine rather than an advertisement.
- No identity drift if using i2i: keep the source person’s facial identity and natural expression consistent.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Fake celebrity composites or unauthorized public-figure likeness mixing
- Illegible barcode numbers when a barcode is present

[1. PURPOSE]
Threads-style viral daily-life photo card, candid spill moment on city pavement. Designed for social cover, blog header, and short-form thumbnail use with a playful “oh my matcha” mood, but rendered as a real found moment with street texture, accidental details, and believable urban context.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Vertical 9:16 framing with the spilled drink occupying the lower 35–45% of the frame, a shadowed upper zone taking about 20%, and enough surrounding pavement to show the accident happened in a real public walkway.
- Main subject is the {음료 종류} overturned from {컵 종류}, positioned slightly left of center so the spill trail leads diagonally toward the bottom-right with droplets, foam streaks, and thin run-off lines.
- Background surface: {장면·장소}, rendered as dark gray tile or concrete with realistic seams, scuffs, dust, small pebbles, faint dried water marks, sunlit patches, and subtle wear from foot traffic.
- Include natural everyday details near the spill: a loose lid or straw, one or two melting ice cubes, a crumpled napkin edge, a tiny receipt corner, fallen leaf fragments, and small splash speckles that make the scene feel captured seconds after impact.
- A single strong human shadow, referencing {그림자}, should enter from the top edge and stretch downward, implying a person holding a phone just outside the frame.
- Preserve a candid, accidental snapshot composition with slight top-down angle from {구도}, avoiding posed product staging while still making the spill visually readable and share-worthy.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Ground plane: establish the pavement first with realistic tile seams, scratches, tiny grit, uneven surface sheen, old stain marks, and slight reflectivity so the liquid can catch light naturally.
2. Spill subject: place {컵 종류} on its side with {음료 종류} visibly spreading outward in a thin stream and a wider puddle, including foam bubbles, separated watery edges, a longer streak trail, and scattered droplets that suggest recent motion.
3. Accident details: add a displaced cup lid, straw or straw wrapper, wet napkin corner, small ice pieces, and a partial receipt with tiny Korean café text such as “영수증”, “아이스 말차”, or “₩5,800” only if legible and naturally cropped.
4. Shadow layer: overlay {그림자} across the upper portion, crisp enough to be legible but softened at the edges by late-day light, with the shadow shape implying a quick phone snapshot rather than a staged scene.
5. Light behavior: apply {시간대·광원} so the liquid highlights sparkle subtly, wet pavement glints around the puddle, and the surrounding concrete stays cool, muted, and tactile.
6. Camera feel: follow {구도} with a casual handheld snapshot look, slight micro-tilt, mild lens distortion, and phone-photo immediacy as if captured quickly before cleaning up.
7. Mood balance: keep the moment awkward-but-funny and everyday, matching {무드}; the storytelling should come from the spill, shadow, scattered objects, and timing rather than dramatic acting.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: allow only tiny incidental real-world text on a cropped receipt, cup sleeve, or sticker if it fits the scene; set any Korean text cleanly and legibly, for example “오늘도 말차”, “영수증”, “아이스 말차”, or “₩5,800”.
- Optional social-photo cue: a very small, natural-looking caption sticker near the lower edge may read “아… 내 말차” or “쏟았다”, but it must feel like a casual phone-post annotation, not an advertisement.
- Color palette: use muted charcoal gray, concrete slate, pale lime green, off-white foam, translucent ice, faded paper beige, and warm amber highlights; anchor the drink color to the {음료 종류} default.
- Border/shadow: use natural ground contact shadow under the cup, realistic cast shadows from nearby street elements, and soft reflected light around wet liquid; avoid artificial outlines.
- Surface treatment: realistic phone-photo texture, slight grain, subtle compression softness, small imperfections, and clean color separation between the drink, paper details, ice, and pavement.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: smartphone main camera look or Sony A7C with a 35mm lens at f/2.8, close documentary snapshot framing, ISO 200.
- Lighting: late-afternoon golden side light from the upper-right or upper-left depending on pavement angle, creating long shadows, wet highlights, and a gentle shine on the spill trail.
- Color grade: muted urban neutrals with soft lime-green emphasis, warm highlights, restrained contrast, and authentic casual social-photo tonality similar to a quick Threads viral post.

[6. MOOD]
A candid social-media spill shot with a Threads viral “oh my matcha” everyday-accident vibe — funny, slightly embarrassing, tactile, and real, like a quick Kinfolk-meets-phone-photo street snapshot taken seconds after the cup fell.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: if any tiny receipt, cup sleeve, or caption-sticker text appears, it must be correctly written Korean such as “아… 내 말차”, “쏟았다”, “영수증”, “아이스 말차”, or “₩5,800”; do not render broken characters.
- Shadow-only person rule: no visible face, body, hands, or shoes; only the human shadow may appear.
- The drink must be clearly spilled and not upright or neatly staged; the cup, liquid trail, droplets, lid, ice, and wet pavement should all support the accidental story.
- The image should feel natural and unfiltered, with realistic street debris, tactile pavement texture, and a real accidental capture look.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized likeness

[INPUT]

- language: Korean

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean convenience-store new dessert SNS poster, square 1:1 promotional ad with cute but premium food-photography finish.
Designed for Instagram, in-store display, blog thumbnails, product-launch banners, and a realistic convenience-store dessert-week promotion.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject placement: {원본 보존} as the hero element, centered and occupying about 58–62% of the frame, with the cut surface clearly visible and appetizing.
- Composition direction: follow {음식 구도}; either a vertical 3-stack of the dessert or a single hero cutaway angle that makes the interior layers easy to read, with a lively retail-poster crop.
- Background treatment: {배경 컬러} smooth promotional backdrop with subtle rounded graphic panels, small sparkle accents, diagonal color blocks, and convenience-store campaign energy.
- Props and spacing: lower area anchored by a white ceramic plate; scattered pistachio crumbs, chocolate fragments, kadaif strands, tiny cocoa dust, and a partially opened dessert wrapper around the base; add {소품·배경} naturally as supporting food-styling elements.
- Rear depth layer: softly blurred chocolate bar, white cup, folded napkin, mini spoon, and small shelf-card or price-pop shape in the rear with shallow depth separation.
- Text layout: top title block, mid-lower subtitle, price badge, benefit bubbles, date/event strip, sponsor/store area, and small footer information placed around the hero without covering the most important cut surface details.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Hero area (center 60%): extract the dessert cleanly from {참고 이미지} and composite it sharply onto the poster background, preserving the original cocoa powder matte tone, the kadaif yellow interior, pistachio green, and white chocolate details.
2. Base layer: place a glossy white porcelain plate slightly below center, with pistachio pieces, chocolate shards, thin kadaif strands, cocoa powder speckles, and a few cream-colored crumbs naturally scattered near the front edge for realistic retail-food styling.
3. Rear depth layer: add softly blurred supporting props behind the dessert—one chocolate bar, one white cup, a folded receipt-like strip, and a small convenience-store shelf label—kept lower in contrast so the dessert remains dominant.
4. Title zone (top 15–20%): render {메인 타이틀} in a large Korean ad-style headline with strong stroke presence and shadow, centered or slightly arced for campaign energy; apply {텍스트 톤} to the lettering personality.
5. Subtitle zone (under title): place {서브 카피} in smaller, clean sans-serif type with enough tracking to stay readable on a square social post.
6. Tag/bubble zone: place {말풍선·태그} as small promotional stickers around the hero, not overlapping the cut face; use them as price/benefit callouts together with short tags such as “NEW”, “4,800원”, “리얼 카다이프”, and “피스타치오 진함”.
7. Event information strip: add a compact lower or side ribbon with realistic poster details: “출시 기념 05.01–05.14”, “전국 편의점 순차 입고”, “냉장 디저트 코너”, “1인 2개 한정”.
8. Sponsor / retail footer: add a small sponsor-style area at the bottom with micro text, barcode-like product block, QR-style square, contact line, and store notice text such as “신상 디저트 위크”, “문의 1588-0000”, “일부 매장 제외”.
9. Decorative graphic elements: add rounded sticker shapes, small hearts, sparkles, check marks, soft halftone dots, and cream/chocolate swooshes that match the color palette and make the poster feel printed and campaign-ready.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use bold Korean sans-serif such as Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Sans KR Black for the main title, paired with a handwritten accent only if needed for emphasis; subtitle in Pretendard Medium or Noto Sans KR Regular at compact size.
- Color palette: {배경 컬러} as the primary base, plus cocoa brown, pistachio green, cream white, warm chocolate beige, and small yellow highlight accents; keep contrast high and retail-friendly.
- Border/shadow: use a soft drop shadow under the dessert with about 4px y-offset, 12px blur, and 15% opacity; title can have a thick dark-brown outline and a subtle 2–3px shadow for sticker-like legibility.
- Surface finish: polished commercial poster texture with believable printed-ad details, clean product reflections, subtle paper/poster finish, and crisp digital campaign graphics.
- Retail realism: include readable micro-layout details such as product price, release period, store notice, mini barcode block, tiny social handle “@duzzonku_official”, and small footer credit “PHOTO BY DESSERT LAB”.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 85mm f/2.8 product-photo look or 70mm macro-style product framing, tight composition with shallow depth of field.
- Lighting: bright studio softbox from upper-left at about 45°, with gentle fill from the front-right and a faint rim light to separate the dessert from the background; natural shadow edges, no harsh specular blowout.
- Color grade: fresh pistachio green + cocoa brown + milk-white commercial grade, slightly warm and vivid, with crisp contrast suitable for a convenience-store launch poster.
- Food texture: cocoa powder should look velvety and dry, pistachio spread should look thick and rich, kadaif should show crisp fibrous strands, and white chocolate detail should have a creamy satin finish.

[6. MOOD]
Korean convenience-store launch campaign — playful retail dessert ad with a polished commercial food-photography feel, like a real Instagram product poster for a new refrigerated dessert release.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문구: “두바이초코 쿠키의 정석”, “리얼 카다이프로 완성한 오리지널 두쫀쿠”, “4,800원”, “피스타치오 함량이 높은 RICH PISTACHIO SPREAD”, “두 번 구워 고소한 REAL KADAIF”, “NEW”.
- Add realistic Korean poster details where they fit: “출시 기념 05.01–05.14”, “전국 편의점 순차 입고”, “냉장 디저트 코너”, “1인 2개 한정”, “신상 디저트 위크”, “문의 1588-0000”, “일부 매장 제외”, “@duzzonku_official”.
- Preserve the dessert identity exactly: cocoa powder tone, kadaif yellow layer, pistachio green layer, and white chocolate detail must remain faithful to the reference image.

[1. PURPOSE]
Modern Michelin-style course menu card for a fine-dining restaurant, designed as a premium editorial print piece for menu books, social posts, reservation pages, and table presentation.
The image should feel like a real photographed menu card placed in an upscale dining room: refined typography, tactile paper, believable restaurant details, and a polished luxury hospitality atmosphere.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Vertical menu-card layout with {비율}, shown as a premium printed card on warm ivory stock, front-facing with a subtle real-paper texture and refined table-service context.
- {레스토랑 이름} sits in the upper zone as the primary masthead, with a smaller bilingual subtitle treatment beneath it such as “FINE DINING · SEOUL” and “시그니처 테이스팅 메뉴”.
- {메뉴 컨셉·시즌} appears near the top as a compact seasonal line, separated by thin charcoal rules, with small service details nearby: “DINNER TASTING”, “2026 SPRING”, “예약제 운영”.
- The core menu block occupies the middle portion of the card, with each course aligned in a disciplined grid and clearly spaced like an actual tasting menu.
- Bottom zone holds {가격·페어링} as a concise pricing and pairing footer, supported by realistic restaurant information: “와인 페어링 선택 가능”, “알레르기 및 식이 제한은 직원에게 말씀해 주세요”.
- Add restaurant-card details that make the design feel authentic: address line, reservation phone, website, service hours, small menu code, table number line, chef credit, sommelier note, and subtle decorative dividers.
- Use {한글 폰트}, {영문 폰트}, and {컬러 톤} consistently, with elegant hierarchy and refined editorial spacing.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header area (top 16%): set {레스토랑 이름} as the dominant title, with elegant serif presence and subtle contrast between English and Korean where applicable; include small supporting text such as “CHEF’S SEASONAL COURSE”, “서울 파인다이닝”, and “EST. 2026”.
- Seasonal line (top 10% below header): place {메뉴 컨셉·시즌} in a small italic or light sans-serif style, with thin charcoal divider lines above and below; include a date label such as “2026년 5월 디너 코스” and a tiny issue-style menu code like “MENU NO. 0526”.
- Menu body (middle 56%): list {코스 메뉴} as 4 to 6 distinct course entries; each entry should be arranged as course number, course name line, and a short description line, with consistent vertical rhythm and fine gray separators between items.
- Course formatting: each course should read like a refined fine-dining menu, with English small caps or uppercase emphasis followed by Korean support text, then a 1–2 line descriptive note; add realistic Korean microcopy such as “제철 허브”, “숙성 소스”, “오늘의 산지”, “셰프 추천 구성”.
- Include small side annotations beside the course list where appropriate: “AMUSE”, “FISH”, “MAIN”, “DESSERT”, “PETIT FOUR”, plus concise Korean notes in smaller type.
- Pricing footer (bottom 18%): set {가격·페어링} in a smaller sans-serif style aligned with the menu column width; add “WINE PAIRING ₩95,000”, “NON-ALCOHOL PAIRING ₩55,000”, “SERVICE CHARGE INCLUDED” if it complements the placeholder.
- Footer information: include “예약 02-0000-0000”, “서울시 강남구 테헤란로 00길 12”, “www.restaurant.kr”, “런치 12:00–15:00 · 디너 18:00–22:00”, and a small credit line “Executive Chef 김도윤 · Sommelier 이서현”.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use a mix of Pretendard, Noto Serif KR, Noto Sans KR, Trajan, Garamond, and Inter; masthead weight around 600–700, body text 300–400, small caps or uppercase at 12–18px equivalent, footer at 18–24px equivalent.
- Color palette: pure white / ivory #FAFAF6 background, charcoal #2A2A2A text, soft gray #888888 dividers and secondary text, optional warmer ivory highlight within the same restrained family from {컬러 톤}.
- Print details: use hairline rules, tiny section markers, subtle letterpress-like impression, embossed-looking restaurant name, fine paper grain, and a faint soft shadow at 5% opacity to lift the card from the surface.
- Decorative elements should stay premium and restaurant-appropriate: small divider dots, understated corner registration marks, refined rule lines, tiny menu-code text, and delicate table-card numbering.
- The card may be presented on a realistic fine-dining surface such as pale linen, matte stone, or warm oak, with very subtle hints of a folded napkin edge, silver cutlery glint, or glass reflection near the outer edge without obscuring the text.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial flat-lay print look simulated as if captured on a Phase One IQ4 with an 80mm lens at f/8, perfectly front-facing and distortion-free.
- Lighting: bright diffused daylight from upper-left, soft shadow falloff to lower-right, resembling a quiet Michelin dining room at late morning.
- Color grade: neutral cream and charcoal monochrome with restrained cool-gray accents, no saturated hues, no warm color spill.
- Material realism: crisp ink edges, slight paper fiber, gentle debossed title texture, realistic print registration, and soft ambient reflections from a luxury dining table setting.

[6. MOOD]
A quiet Michelin dining-room editorial — like a modern luxury menu page from a Kinfolk-meets-French-gastronomy print spread, but with enough real restaurant information, pricing, service notes, and tactile paper detail to feel genuinely photographed and usable.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following strings must appear exactly as written: {레스토랑 이름}, {메뉴 컨셉·시즌}, {코스 메뉴}, {가격·페어링}.
- Include readable Korean restaurant details: “2026년 5월 디너 코스”, “예약 02-0000-0000”, “서울시 강남구 테헤란로 00길 12”, “런치 12:00–15:00 · 디너 18:00–22:00”, “Executive Chef 김도윤”.
- Ensure all menu lines remain legible, evenly spaced, and aligned with a strict editorial grid.
- The final image must look like a real premium printed fine-dining course menu card, not a blank template.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[1. PURPOSE]
Michelin restaurant-style wine list card, dark cellar editorial page for fine dining menu presentation.
Elegant vertical menu layout with bilingual serif typography, designed as a real guest-facing wine selection card with pairing guidance, glass/bottle pricing, sommelier notes, and venue utility details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Top header band (14-16%): {레스토랑·바 이름} set as the main title area, centered with refined serif hierarchy, a small cellar label, date/service line, and thin mustard-gold divider rules.
- Main content field (68-72%): structured wine entries stacked in a polished column, each entry aligned to the same left edge with strong vertical rhythm, including wine name, region, vintage, glass/bottle price cue, and pairing note.
- Bottom utility band (12-14%): {가격대}, tasting-course note, address/contact line, corkage/service information, and a tiny barcode-style reservation block, separated by a thin gold line.
- Background should be a deep charcoal-to-black matte premium stock paper with visible fine paper grain, faint cellar shelf texture, subtle debossed grapevine contour lines, and warm foil-like gold details.
- Use {한글 폰트}, {영문 폰트}, {컬러 톤}, and {비율} consistently across the entire page.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header area: Set {레스토랑·바 이름} at the top in large elegant serif, with wide tracking and a small secondary line below reading “SOMMELIER CELLAR LIST · 2026 봄 디너 셀렉션”; add a thin gold rule beneath for Michelin-like restraint.
- Service metadata: Add compact Korean microtext near the header such as “디너 서비스 18:00–22:30”, “와인 디렉터 추천”, “TABLE WINE CARD No. 027”, and “글라스 / 보틀 가격 표기”.
- Wine list block: Render {와인 리스트} as 5-7 stacked entries, each entry broken into four sub-lines: wine name in English serif small caps, origin/vintage/ABV in light italic microtext, Korean tasting note, and pairing text from {페어링 가이드} as a compact line with a subtle arrow cue.
- Entry details: For realism, include small price markers beside each entry such as “GL ₩18,000 · BT ₩92,000”, “BT ₩148,000”, “PAIRING +₩32,000”, while keeping {가격대} as the official bottom price range reference.
- Entry separators: Place thin horizontal gold dividers between wine entries, with tiny vintage-dot markers, understated section labels like “WHITE”, “RED”, “SPARKLING”, or “DESSERT”, and a faint vertical alignment guide in antique gold.
- Price and pairing footer: Place {가격대} and a short footer note in small sans-serif at the bottom, aligned cleanly: “코스 페어링 3잔 / 5잔 선택 가능”, “콜키지 1병 ₩30,000”, “예약 문의 02-000-2026”, and “서울 중구 다이닝로 27”.
- Utility finishing: Add a small reservation barcode area, page code “WINE LIST · P.01”, and micro credit line “Curated by Head Sommelier Min Jae Kim” in the lower margin.
- Typography hierarchy: Make the wine names the most prominent text after the title, while origin, vintage, pairing guidance, prices, and venue details remain smaller and quieter.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Use Noto Serif KR or 본명조 for Korean text, and Trajan / Bodoni / Playfair Display for English serif headings; pair with a small clean sans-serif such as Inter or Noto Sans KR for secondary details.
- Color palette: Use {컬러 톤} strictly, centered on deep charcoal #1a1410 to black background, mustard gold #c9a55c lines and headers, and cream #f0e8d6 body text.
- Border/shadow: Use hairline gold rules, delicate corner ticks, faint foil-stamped monogram details, and an ultra-soft paper shadow only if needed, around 2px y-offset, 8px blur, 10% opacity.
- Decorative texture: Add subtle matte paper grain, very faint cellar-map contour marks, tiny gold registration dots, and low-contrast debossed vine-line details so the card feels printed and handled in a luxury restaurant.
- Letter spacing: Slight tracking on English headers and small caps; tighter tracking on Korean body text to preserve editorial elegance.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: flat editorial poster composition, simulated as a printed luxury menu page, 50mm standard lens look with minimal perspective distortion, front-on orthographic presentation.
- Lighting: soft studio top-light with very subtle side fill, producing a faint paper sheen, tactile foil highlights, and readable cream typography against the dark stock.
- Color grade: dark espresso, black, muted antique gold, and warm cream, with restrained contrast and polished fine-dining warmth.
- Material realism: The final image should feel like a photographed premium menu card on thick black paper, with crisp ink edges, slight foil impression, and believable print density.

[6. MOOD]
Michelin-star cellar menu — inspired by a Kinfolk x luxury hotel wine list spread, with the understated precision of a fine-dining sommelier booklet, enriched by realistic restaurant service information and tactile dark paper luxury.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문자열: {레스토랑·바 이름}, {와인 리스트}, {페어링 가이드}, {가격대}, {한글 폰트}, {영문 폰트}, {컬러 톤}, {비율}.
- Include realistic Korean menu text such as “와인 디렉터 추천”, “코스 페어링”, “글라스 / 보틀”, “예약 문의”, “콜키지”, “디너 서비스”, and short pairing notes that match the fine-dining wine theme.
- Layout invariants: exactly one page, vertical orientation, dark background, luxury wine-list card structure, readable bilingual typography, and coherent menu pricing details.
- All wine entries should remain legible, evenly spaced, and aligned into a refined list structure suitable for a Michelin-style cellar card.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[INPUT]

[1. PURPOSE]
Michelin-informed fine-dining single-item signature menu card for an à la carte restaurant display, table insert, reservation preview, and social-media menu introduction.
Cream-ivory paper feel with muted gold rules, classic serif typography, precise menu information, and a refined luxury restaurant identity that feels like a premium tasting-menu booklet page.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Vertical single-page menu card in {비율}: upper area for restaurant identity and menu metadata, center area for the signature dish title and description, lower area for price, pairing, origin, allergy, reservation, address, and contact details.
- Background treatment: warm cream / ivory matte paper texture with subtle fibers, slight letterpress impression on gold rules, soft tactile printed-paper realism, and delicate tonal variation across the sheet.
- Composition should feel premium and readable: a thin gold top rule, small section label, centered restaurant name, generous dish title block, elegant divider marks, and structured footer information with restaurant-card realism.
- Use {레스토랑 이름}, {지점명}, {시그니처 메뉴}, {메뉴 부제}, {메뉴 설명}, {셰프 노트}, {가격}, {와인 페어링}, {원산지 안내}, {알레르기 안내}, {운영 정보}, {주소}, {연락처}, {예약 안내}, {메뉴 코드}, {소셜 핸들}, {한글 폰트}, {영문 폰트}, {컬러 톤} placeholders.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Top metadata band (upper 8%): place a small caps English label such as SIGNATURE À LA CARTE with wide tracking, plus {메뉴 코드} and a seasonal line such as SPRING DINNER SELECTION; separate it with a very thin muted-gold rule.
- Brand line (upper 15%): place {레스토랑 이름} as the primary brand text, centered in a refined serif or high-contrast display serif; set {지점명} below in smaller type, then add a small gold dot, short rule, or tiny fork-and-leaf line ornament.
- Main dish title block (upper-mid 22%): render {시그니처 메뉴} as the largest text element, elegant and highly legible; set {메뉴 부제} as a lighter secondary line below, using smaller tracking and softer charcoal.
- Description block (mid 20%): place {메뉴 설명} in 2–3 calm lines with refined line-height; add {셰프 노트} as a smaller chef’s note line beneath, introduced with the Korean label 셰프 노트.
- Informational divider row (mid-lower 12%): create three compact columns or neatly stacked rows for 원산지 {원산지 안내}, 알레르기 {알레르기 안내}, and 페어링 {와인 페어링}; use hairline gold separators and small serif labels.
- Price block (lower left 9%): set {가격} prominently but not louder than the dish title, followed by a small VAT 포함 note; align with the lower information grid for a realistic menu-card hierarchy.
- Restaurant footer (lower 14%): include {운영 정보}, {주소}, {연락처}, {예약 안내}, and {소셜 핸들} in small clean text, using tiny gold bullets or vertical dividers; make it look like a real restaurant menu card rather than a decorative quote page.
- Decorative graphics: include subtle gold corner ticks, a tiny ingredient line-art accent such as truffle slice, herb stem, or sauce spoon mark, and refined divider rules that support the fine-dining identity.
- The overall layout must remain a single featured dish page; supporting text should be restaurant details, service information, and menu metadata rather than a full multi-item menu.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use {한글 폰트} for Korean text, and {영문 폰트} for English labels; body copy should be light to regular, the dish name medium to semibold, and micro-information clean and crisp.
- Color palette: derive from {컬러 톤}; keep cream ivory paper, deep charcoal body text, muted mustard-gold dividers, and occasional warm-gray secondary labels.
- Print finish: emulate premium uncoated stock, slight debossed gold ink on rules, very soft page-edge shadow, and subtle ink density differences visible on close inspection.
- Layout details: use consistent baseline alignment, clear visual hierarchy, refined dividers, small menu-code metadata, and carefully placed footer information so the card feels professionally typeset.
- Border/shadow: allow a thin inset gold rule or corner ticks and a very soft paper shadow around the sheet edge, with no heavy boxed frame effect.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: flat printed editorial layout, as if photographed with a Hasselblad X2D 100C and 80mm lens at f/5.6 for even paper clarity, or rendered as a perfectly sharp print mockup.
- Lighting: soft diffused studio top light with gentle falloff, mild paper texture visibility, controlled highlights on muted gold ink, and no harsh reflections.
- Color grade: cream ivory, muted gold, charcoal black, warm gray, low saturation, warm neutral balance, and refined restaurant-stationery realism.

[6. MOOD]
Michelin Guide presentation page meets luxury Seoul fine-dining stationery — quiet confidence, polished service details, tactile paper, restrained gold accents, and a signature-dish focus.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 들어가야 하는 문자열: {레스토랑 이름}, {지점명}, {시그니처 메뉴}, {메뉴 부제}, {메뉴 설명}, {셰프 노트}, {가격}, {와인 페어링}, {원산지 안내}, {알레르기 안내}, {운영 정보}, {주소}, {연락처}, {예약 안내}, {메뉴 코드}, {소셜 핸들}
- 고정 라벨은 선명하게 렌더링: 시그니처 단품, 셰프 노트, 원산지, 알레르기, 페어링, 예약, 주소, 문의, VAT 포함
- Keep Korean characters fully intact and readable; no broken jamo, no incorrect spacing, no garbled bilingual title treatment.
- Maintain one clear focal menu item, with restaurant footer details and menu metadata supporting the featured dish.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications / fabricated Michelin stars or award badges
- Broken Korean characters, split jamo, or garbled bilingual text
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized celebrity likeness

studio:prompts3:ours-257.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Create a dark-gold luxury course menu card for fine dining hospitality, designed as a premium printed menu, Instagram portrait card, menu booklet insert, and table welcome card.
The design should feel like a Michelin-guide-inspired tasting menu without using fake awards or official seals: deep charcoal paper, antique-gold dividers, cream typography, realistic restaurant information, and refined editorial pacing.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Portrait composition with {레스토랑 이름} as the main masthead in the top 16%–18%, {지점명} and {메뉴 날짜} placed as small supporting information near the header, and {메뉴 컨셉} positioned below as the seasonal descriptor.
- Use a dark charcoal matte-paper background with subtle pressed paper grain, very faint ink absorption at the edges, and a warm premium print finish.
- The central 55% should contain {코스 메뉴 리스트} as a structured tasting-course sequence, divided by thin mustard-gold rules and small course labels.
- The lower 22% should include {가격}, {와인 페어링}, {운영시간}, {예약 안내}, {주소}, {연락처}, and {알레르기 안내} in a realistic menu-footer layout.
- Add restrained fine-dining details such as tiny gold corner ticks, small tableware line icons, a reservation QR placeholder box, menu code {메뉴 코드}, and certificate-like hairline ornaments that support the restaurant-card feeling without implying official certification.
- Keep the composition centered, elegant, and print-realistic, with a balanced restaurant menu hierarchy rather than a loud promotional poster.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header area: set {레스토랑 이름} as the dominant title in a classic serif masthead treatment, centered, with {지점명} beneath in smaller cream text and a tiny gold uppercase-style dining label such as “DINING ROOM · SEOUL” as part of the typographic texture.
- Date and menu code: place {메뉴 날짜} on the upper left or right and {메뉴 코드} on the opposite side in very small cream text, aligned to the same invisible top baseline.
- Primary divider: add one thin mustard-gold rule spanning about 28%–36% of the width, with a tiny centered dot or fork-and-knife line icon in gold.
- Seasonal concept area: place {메뉴 컨셉} in small tracked typography or restrained italic serif, with a refined editorial rhythm and clear separation from the courses.
- Main course block: list {코스 메뉴 리스트} as stacked course entries; show course names first, followed by dish details on the next line, and use short gold separators or delicate dotted leaders between sections.
- Pricing and pairing: place {가격} and {와인 페어링} below the course list as two calm centered lines, readable and premium, using gold emphasis only for labels or tiny divider marks.
- Restaurant footer: include {운영시간}, {예약 안내}, {주소}, and {연락처} in two compact columns or a centered stacked footer, separated by hairline dividers.
- Practical details: add {알레르기 안내} as a small footnote, and include a small square “예약 QR” placeholder or monogram box near the bottom without overpowering the text.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Trajan Pro, Bodoni, or Playfair Display for English-style headings; use 본명조, Spoqa Han Sans Neo Light, or Noto Serif KR for Korean text; keep weights light to regular, with masthead sizing around 6%–7% of canvas width and body around 1.6%–2.5%.
- Korean text must look professionally typeset, with correct spacing around slashes, middle dots, won prices, course dashes, and parentheses.
- Color palette: deep charcoal #1a1a1a, blackened graphite #111111, mustard gold #c9a55c, antique gold #b8944f, and cream white #F4EEDD.
- Texture and print finish: use a subtle matte card-stock grain, faint gold-foil impression on divider lines, and slight ink softness around cream text to make the card feel physically printed.
- Border/shadow: allow delicate hairline corner ornaments, thin double rules, small monogram marks, and very soft printed depth; avoid heavy drop shadows or glossy plastic effects.
- Letter spacing: apply generous tracking to the title and small labels; keep course descriptions tighter and highly legible.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: studio flat-art composition, equivalent to a Hasselblad X2D 100C top-down editorial layout with a 50mm normal-view look, no perspective distortion.
- Lighting: even diffuse studio lighting from above with zero harsh hotspots, as if photographed under large softboxes and then converted into a clean typographic poster.
- Color grade: restrained charcoal, antique gold, and cream-white print palette with a slight warm paper tint and no saturation spikes.

[6. MOOD]
Michelin-star tasting menu card atmosphere — luxury hotel dining editorial, quiet Seoul fine-dining confidence, dark gold evening service, with the calm restraint of a modern Kinfolk x The New Yorker layout.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 렌더링되어야 하는 문자열은 {레스토랑 이름}, {지점명}, {메뉴 날짜}, {메뉴 컨셉}, {코스 메뉴 리스트}, {가격}, {와인 페어링}, {운영시간}, {예약 안내}, {주소}, {연락처}, {알레르기 안내}, {메뉴 코드}.
- Recommended visible Korean footer examples: “예약 QR”, “디너 18:00–22:30”, “라스트 오더 20:30”, “알레르기 또는 식이 제한은 직원에게 알려주세요”.
- Typography hierarchy must remain intact: title, location/date, concept line, course list, pricing, pairing, and restaurant footer must be clearly separated and readable.
- All course entries must remain readable as distinct menu items with no broken Korean characters, no merged lines, and no random punctuation changes.
- Decorative ornaments, tableware icons, dividers, and QR placeholder should look like premium menu-card production details, not fake awards or official certification marks.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites
- Fake Michelin stars, fake guide badges, or official-looking award emblems

studio:prompts3:ours-256.content:
[INPUT]
- reference_image: {참고 이미지}
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean dessert SNS campaign card, square 1:1 Instagram-style advertising layout, photoreal food composite with bold promotional copy.
Retail cinema / convenience-store PB ad aesthetic, centered product hero with explanatory arrow labels, account handle, campaign badge, price/CTA, hashtag line, and subtle save/share micro icons for a realistic social feed impression.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Subject placement: {원본 보존} food hero centered and enlarged to occupy about 60–65% of the frame, with the cut face clearly visible and slightly angled for depth.
- Text placement: {메인 카피} as the dominant headline near the upper third or strong side block, {서브 카피} placed as a smaller supporting line below or opposite the headline.
- Social ad header: add a compact top-left account label with {브랜드명} and {인스타 핸들}, plus a small {프로모션 배지} tag near the headline.
- Annotation system: {화살표 라벨 가이드} should use thin clean arrows and compact Korean labels that precisely match the pointed surface.
- Purchase information: include {가격 문구} and {CTA 문구} as a readable lower information strip or rounded sticker-style callout.
- Social micro UI: add small save/share/like-style micro icons, carousel dot indicator, and {해시태그 문구} near the lower edge as if this is a polished Instagram ad card.
- Background treatment: {배경 톤} with subtle campaign-grade texture, soft gradient, cocoa dust speckles, faint geometric patterning, or gentle paper-like grain that supports the dessert mood.
- Framing direction: {구도} with copy zones arranged around the product while keeping the cut section readable, sharp, and visually dominant.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Hero food layer — {원본 보존} as a photoreal cutout, preserving the matte cocoa powder surface, rough kataifi interior, pistachio green, and white chocolate granularity exactly as seen in the reference.
2) Brand/social header layer — {브랜드명}, {인스타 핸들}, and a small “Sponsored” or “광고” style marker, rendered like a real Korean SNS campaign post header without overpowering the product.
3) Main headline layer — {메인 카피} set in large bold Korean sans-serif, positioned so it does not cover the cut face or arrow endpoints.
4) Subcopy layer — {서브 카피} in a smaller supporting weight, aligned with the campaign composition and kept visually subordinate to the headline.
5) Campaign badge layer — {프로모션 배지} in a rounded capsule, sticker, or small ribbon graphic using pistachio green, cream, or cocoa brown accents.
6) Arrow labeling layer — {화살표 라벨 가이드} rendered with thin, precise lines and small Korean labels, each label pointing to the correct material region only.
7) Commerce and CTA layer — {가격 문구}, {CTA 문구}, and {캠페인 날짜} arranged as realistic ad information, such as a bottom band, small coupon tag, or caption-like line.
8) Instagram detail layer — {해시태그 문구}, small save/share/like micro icons, and a 3-dot carousel indicator to make the card feel like an actual SNS ad creative.
9) Background finish — {배경 톤} with a polished Korean dessert ad look, including refined grain, cocoa-powder speckles, soft radial lighting, and gentle accent graphics that frame the product.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard Black, Sandoll Gothic Bold, or Cafe24 Ssurround style for the main copy at about 72–110 px equivalent; subcopy in Pretendard Medium or Noto Sans KR at about 28–40 px equivalent.
- Color palette: use {배경 톤} as the base, with charcoal black, cream white, cocoa brown, and accent greens matching the pistachio tones in the reference.
- Social UI text: {인스타 핸들}, {해시태그 문구}, {캠페인 날짜}, and micro-labels should be smaller but legible, using Noto Sans KR or Pretendard Regular/Medium.
- Badge and CTA styling: {프로모션 배지} and {CTA 문구} may use rounded rectangles, ticket-stub edges, small arrow icons, cocoa bean motifs, pistachio-green highlights, or cream sticker shapes.
- Border/shadow: subtle soft drop shadow under the food only, around 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity; arrows should stay fine and precise.
- Layout realism: make the design feel like a finished Korean Instagram ad card with headline hierarchy, product callouts, commerce information, hashtags, and social micro-icons all balanced in a 1024x1024 frame.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: photoreal product-shot look, 85mm lens at f/4 equivalent for a clean commercial food portrait, crisp focus on the cut surface and surface texture.
- Lighting: studio softbox from upper-left at about 45°, with a gentle fill from the right and controlled specular glare so the cocoa powder remains matte and realistic.
- Color grade: cinematic Korean dessert campaign grade with cocoa brown, deep olive, cream ivory, and pistachio green balanced in a clean retail-ad palette.
- Material detail: preserve powdery cocoa bloom, crumb fragments, uneven kataifi strands, pistachio paste color variation, and white chocolate pieces with realistic micro-shadowing.
- Graphic finish: crisp vector-like Korean typography and arrows composited over photoreal food, with subtle texture in the background rather than flat empty color.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean dessert campaign card — cinema chain concession ad meets convenience-store PB launch poster and Instagram sponsored post, polished and commercial like a seasonal dessert drop with appetizing product close-up, playful labels, and shareable social-feed energy.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 렌더링할 문구: "두바이 쫀득쿠키", "겉은 쫀득, 속은 바삭", "@dozzon.cookie", "NEW 시즌 한정", "1개 ₩3,900", "지금 가까운 매장에서 만나보세요".
- Required visible SNS details: 브랜드명 "두쫀쿠", 캠페인 날짜 "2026.05 출시", 해시태그 "#두쫀쿠 #두바이쫀득쿠키 #피스타치오디저트"를 작은 보조 요소로 포함.
- Arrow-label integrity: the arrow pointing to the cocoa-coated outer surface must be labeled as the outer cocoa coating only, and the arrow pointing to the interior cut face must be labeled as the kataifi / pistachio / white chocolate interior only.
- Preserve the original dessert identity, shape, cocoa powder tone, and rough cut-face texture; do not smooth out the interior.
- Food cutout must remain photoreal and anatomically plausible to the original dessert shape.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Misaligned arrow-label targets
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized portrait likeness
