studio:prompts3:ours-255.content:
[INPUT]
- reference_image: {참고 이미지}
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean convenience-store dessert campaign SNS card, photoreal food composite, 1:1 square ad for Instagram feed, blog thumbnail, and mobile commerce promotion.
Create a realistic retail dessert advertisement with a delicious buttertteok hero, bold Korean headline, supportive campaign details, small social-media UI cues, and warm butter-themed graphics that feel like an actual Korean convenience-store launch card.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center the {원본 보존} food subject as the hero at 55–65% of frame width, angled slightly toward the viewer so the golden-brown baked surface, cracks, and chewy rice texture are clearly visible.
- Use a warm cream / ivory / butter-yellow background based on {배경 톤}, enriched with soft milk-and-butter swirl graphics, faint grainy paper texture, caramel-colored accent strokes, and gentle studio shadow separation from the subject.
- Follow {구도}: place the main copy in the upper-left or upper-center 20–25% of the canvas, with the food hero occupying the center/lower-center and small campaign details arranged around it like a real SNS retail ad.
- Place {메인 카피 (큰 글씨)} as the dominant headline, {서브 카피 (작은 글씨)} beneath it in smaller scale, and {태그·말풍선 (선택)} as small sticker-like accents near the food or card edge.
- Add realistic Instagram-card details: a tiny handle line “@buttertteok.daily”, hashtags “#상하이버터떡 #겉바속쫀 #편의점디저트”, small save/share/heart micro icons, a compact “NEW” tag, and a price or CTA area such as “출시기념 ₩2,900” and “오늘 간식으로 저장”.
- Add tasteful food-ad surroundings that naturally support the product: a small parchment sheet or cream ceramic plate under the buttertteok, a tiny butter curl, a few toasted crumb specks, and subtle golden highlights, without changing the original food count or shape.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Hero food area: Extract the buttertteok from {참고 이미지} and render it photorealistically with the exact golden-brown baked surface, surface cracks, chewy glutinous rice interior texture, and original count/shape preserved from {원본 보존}. Place it on a warm parchment sheet or low cream plate with soft contact shadows.
2. Background field: Fill the canvas with {배경 톤}, using a cream-to-ivory or butter-yellow base, layered with faint dairy-wave graphics, tiny caramel dots, subtle paper texture, and soft studio shadows for depth.
3. Headline zone: Set {메인 카피 (큰 글씨)} large and bold in the upper area, using strong Korean sans-serif typography with clear spacing, high legibility, and the selected {텍스트 톤}.
4. Subcopy zone: Place {서브 카피 (작은 글씨)} directly under the headline or along one side, sized to feel like a real retail campaign message; include a small supporting line such as “프랑스 고메버터로 완성한 겉바속쫀 식감”.
5. Tag/accent zone: Add {태그·말풍선 (선택)} in sticker-like, pill-like, or speech-bubble accents, plus short Korean promo labels such as “NEW”, “한정”, “GLUTEN FREE”, “상하이에서 보고온 디저트”, and “겉바속쫀”.
6. Social commerce details: Include a bottom or side micro-info strip with “@buttertteok.daily”, “출시기념 ₩2,900”, “저장하고 오늘 간식 픽”, tiny heart/comment/share/save icons, and 2–3 hashtag-style words in Korean.
7. Finishing pass: Ensure all ad elements feel integrated into a polished square SNS campaign card, with realistic food texture, readable typography, warm retail color grading, and layered visual details that make the image feel produced for an actual dessert launch.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard Black, Sandoll Gothic Bold, or Cafe24-style Korean sans-serif; headline very heavy, subcopy medium to regular weight, micro-info small but readable, with crisp anti-aliased edges and large mobile-friendly sizing.
- Color palette: butter cream, ivory, warm beige, soft milk white, golden brown, caramel, and dark charcoal text; emphasize the background range from {배경 톤} while keeping all accents appetizing and warm.
- Border/shadow: use a soft drop shadow with about 4px y-offset, 12px blur, and 15% opacity; add subtle rounded sticker edges, thin cream outlines, small sparkle dots, and semi-transparent label panels where useful.
- Graphic details: include a small Instagram-style top handle or bottom action row, subtle decorative arcs, butter-swipe shapes, dotted dividers, and short Korean promo badges that reinforce a convenience-store dessert campaign.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 50mm product-photography look or 85mm f/1.8 close product framing, optimized for a square commercial food ad with shallow but natural separation.
- Lighting: soft studio softbox from upper-left at 45° with gentle fill from the right, enough to reveal the baked cracks and rice texture without glossy glare.
- Color grade: warm cream + butter yellow + caramel brown with controlled contrast, clean highlights, realistic shadows, and a polished convenience-store dessert campaign finish.

[6. MOOD]
Commercial Korean dessert campaign card — warm, appetizing, launch-day SNS promo energy with a photoreal buttertteok hero, bold Korean typography, playful micro stickers, social-commerce cues, and a modern convenience-store dessert advertisement feel.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: “상하이 버터떡”, “프랑스 고메버터로 완성한 겉바속쫀 식감”, “GLUTEN FREE”, “상하이에서 보고온 디저트”, “한정”, “NEW”, “출시기념 ₩2,900”, “@buttertteok.daily”, “#상하이버터떡 #겉바속쫀 #편의점디저트”.
- Preserve the buttertteok identity exactly: golden-brown baked surface, surface cracks, chewy glutinous rice interior texture, and original number/shape from the reference image.
- Food must remain photoreal and recognizable as buttertteok; do not alter it into another pastry shape.
- Layout must remain square SNS-card ready with clear Korean headline hierarchy, readable micro details, and a realistic retail-ad finish.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized likeness

[INPUT]
- reference_image: {참고 이미지}
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Create a photorealistic editorial food descriptor card with the attached food photo as the hero subject. The result should feel like a real café menu feature, Instagram feed card, blog header, storefront sign insert, or menu-book page: calm, refined, appetizing, and filled with believable printed details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Square 1:1 editorial menu-card layout for {출력 비율}, using a balanced magazine grid with visible hierarchy and practical printed-card information.
- Hero food subject from {참고 이미지} placed prominently at the center or slightly above center on a warm ivory-beige paper surface from {배경 톤}, with realistic paper grain, faint print texture, and natural surface shadows.
- Use a left-led editorial layout with supporting microcopy arranged in neat columns, small labels, dividers, price lines, and menu-card metadata.
- Add realistic café/menu details around the main content: store name “오늘의 식탁”, date label “2026.05.01”, card number “MENU CARD 254”, price “₩7,500”, serving note “1인 추천”, address line “서울 성동구 작은길 12”, contact “02-000-2540”, and small hours text “11:30–20:30”.
- Use {음식 이름}, {한 줄 정의}, {핵심 키워드 3개}, {위트 한 줄}, {한글 폰트}, {영문 폰트}, {배경 톤}, {출력 비율} as customizable values.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Top header band: place a small English category label in all caps with wide tracking, such as “TODAY’S PLATE”, alongside “MENU CARD 254” and the date label “2026.05.01”. Add tiny credit text such as “photo / house kitchen” and “recipe note / seasonal table”.
2) Store identity area: add the Korean store name “오늘의 식탁” in small refined type, with a short subline “계절 재료로 준비한 오늘의 한 접시”. Keep it printed-card realistic rather than logo-like.
3) Title area: place {음식 이름} as the main headline, large and calm, with regular weight and slightly tightened tracking. Add a small price and serving row nearby: “₩7,500 · 1인 추천 · 매장/포장 가능”.
4) Hero image area: extract the food from {참고 이미지} as a photorealistic cutout or naturally plated subject, placed prominently in the center, occupying roughly 58–68% of the frame width. Preserve the food’s original texture, sauce sheen, crumbs, steam cues, garnish, plate edge, and material feel. Add a soft natural contact shadow beneath and allow a subtle ceramic plate rim, parchment sheet, linen napkin corner, or wooden tray edge if it supports realism.
5) Description block: beneath or beside the hero food, place {한 줄 정의} in a light gray tone, smaller than the title, with a short caption label “TASTING NOTE”.
6) Keyword line: place {핵심 키워드 3개} as small caps or compact Korean caption text separated by slashes, using a restrained magazine/menu caption style.
7) Companion menu strip: add a small “함께하면 좋은 메뉴” section with 2–3 believable items and prices, such as “아이스 아메리카노 ₩4,500”, “제철 샐러드 ₩6,800”, “오늘의 수프 ₩3,900”. Use thin dividers, dotted leaders, or small alignment marks like a real printed menu.
8) Footer information: place {위트 한 줄} near the bottom as an italic or lighter caption. Add realistic footer details: “서울 성동구 작은길 12 · 02-000-2540 · 11:30–20:30”, a tiny order note “take-out available”, and a small barcode/receipt-like block or QR-placeholder pattern that looks printed but not official.
9) Overall finish: keep the food visually dominant and appetizing while the surrounding information feels like a thoughtfully designed café menu card printed on warm textured paper.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: {한글 폰트} for Korean text, {영문 폰트} for English text; use regular to light weights for captions and a confident larger scale for {음식 이름}. Combine main headline, small metadata, price row, tasting note, companion menu, and footer information with clear hierarchy.
- Color palette: warm ivory and beige from {배경 톤}, plus charcoal and soft gray for text. Use very subtle warm brown or muted olive only for tiny section marks, dividers, or price emphasis if needed.
- Printed details: use hairline dividers, dotted leaders, tiny registration-like marks, small barcode/receipt area, and natural paper fibers to make the card feel tangible and professionally printed.
- Shadows and surface: use a realistic contact shadow under the food and slight paper depth; keep edges natural, tactile, and photographic.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: high-end editorial food photography, 85mm macro at f/4 or 100mm macro at f/4, clean product-style framing.
- Lighting: soft diffused window light from upper-left with a gentle fill from the right, creating realistic surface volume, appetizing highlights, and a light shadow under the food.
- Color grade: muted cream, beige, charcoal, and soft paper-white; low saturation, controlled contrast, natural food color, no HDR look.
- Material realism: visible paper grain, slight ink impression, real food texture, believable plate/napkin/tray surfaces, and subtle imperfections that make the card feel photographed rather than digitally sterile.

[6. MOOD]
Kinfolk × MUJI × Cereal Magazine first-page editorial with a real neighborhood café menu feeling — calm, refined, tactile, appetizing, and lightly witty.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following Korean strings must appear correctly if rendered from the provided values: {음식 이름}, {한 줄 정의}, {핵심 키워드 3개}, {위트 한 줄}.
- All visible Korean text must remain clean Korean without broken characters or jamo separation, including added labels such as “오늘의 식탁”, “계절 재료로 준비한 오늘의 한 접시”, “함께하면 좋은 메뉴”, “매장/포장 가능”, and “서울 성동구 작은길 12”.
- Set believable menu text in Korean where appropriate: “₩7,500”, “1인 추천”, “아이스 아메리카노 ₩4,500”, “제철 샐러드 ₩6,800”, “오늘의 수프 ₩3,900”.
- Keep the food large enough to feel like the main subject; it should remain appetizing, sharply rendered, and naturally integrated with the printed card environment.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Jamo-separated Korean text

[INPUT]

- language: Korean

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean object-usage hand-drawn infographic, practical quick-start card style for social feed, package insert, and product-care guide.
Photoreal studio object placed on a warm white manual-sheet surface with black ink overlay instructions, small production details, and readable Korean hand-lettering.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Feature one primary {사물 카테고리} as the hero subject, occupying the central 58–66% of the square frame, with surrounding annotation space integrated like a real folded instruction leaflet.
- If the input angle is weak, switch to the most useful readable {사물 뷰} and {사물 상태} while preserving the object identity exactly.
- Use a warm off-white paper surface or seamless studio sheet with subtle paper fiber, faint fold crease, tiny registration ticks, and natural contact shadow so the card feels printed and handled.
- Place the title box in one corner with a hand-drawn outline, and balance arrows, step chips, caution notes, and checklist marks around the object.
- Add a small footer strip containing {제작처}, {발행일}, {페이지표기}, and a short storage/save cue such as “저장해두고 보기”.
- Use {언어} only for every title, subtitle, label, step, arrow note, footer, and mini-box text.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Hero object area: the {사물 카테고리} rendered photoreally with its real material, surface texture, edges, seams, buttons, caps, hinges, openings, or grip points visible; add a natural soft shadow directly beneath or slightly to one side for depth.
- Title box: one hand-drawn corner box containing {타이틀} and {서브타이틀}, with subtitle smaller and matched to {인포그래픽 목적}.
- Metadata strip: small handwritten details such as “{문서번호}”, “{발행일}”, “{난이도}”, and “{소요시간}” arranged like a real quick manual, without implying official certification.
- Callout layer: 6–10 black handwritten notes, placed around the object with thin arrows pointing to true functional parts, openings, buttons, handles, caps, seams, surface contact points, cleaning points, or storage points.
- Step layer: if {인포그래픽 목적} is 사용법 안내, show 3–5 short numbered actions in order, each paired with a clear arrow and a brief imperative phrase in {언어}.
- Support layer: if {인포그래픽 목적} is 세척 관리, 안전 주의, 빠른 팁, 해야 할 것과 피할 것, or 문제 해결, replace extra steps with concise mini boxes, ✓/✗ pairs, short if-then notes, or a tiny troubleshooting checklist.
- Social card layer: add a small page indicator “{페이지표기}”, a save/share micro icon row drawn in black ink, and an end-card cue such as “다음 장: 보관법” when it fits naturally.
- Integrity rule: annotations should orbit the object and remain attached to actual parts; do not cover brand labels, moving parts, important contours, warning labels, or recognisable identity features.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: hand-drawn marker lettering for headers and callouts, with bold handwritten emphasis for the title; use legible Korean hand-lettering that stays stable at small size.
- Linework: consistent black ink strokes with slight natural wobble, thicker stroke for title box and section labels, thinner stroke for arrows, checkboxes, dividers, and small notes.
- Color palette: warm white paper, black ink, realistic product colors from the reference, soft gray shadow, and optional very pale graphite smudges from hand-drawn marks.
- Printed-card details: include tiny divider lines, circled numbers, check marks, hand-drawn brackets, page dot indicator, and small tape-like annotation tabs when they support readability.
- Layout rhythm: keep all notes compact, practical, and scan-friendly, with clear hierarchy from title → steps → callouts → footer.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Canon EOS R5 with RF 100mm f/2.8L Macro at f/8, high-resolution studio product shot, front-facing or top-down according to the most useful reading angle.
- Lighting: soft diffused studio light from upper-left with gentle fill from right, evenly exposed warm white paper background, crisp micro-contrast on the object surface.
- Color grade: neutral product-documentary grade with clean black ink overlay, accurate reference colors, soft paper texture, no hue shift, no tinted shadows, no retro wash.

[6. MOOD]
Practical package-insert infographic meets friendly workshop note card, like a real product quick guide photographed before being slipped into a box.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: every rendered string must be in {언어} only, with no broken Korean characters.
- Must preserve the exact identity, shape, material, logo/label placement if present, and key functional parts of the input {사물 카테고리}.
- Use one primary object as the visual subject; all instructions must appear as separate ink overlay, not as a cartoonized replacement of the product.
- Keep arrows precise to actual touch points, opening points, closing points, cleaning points, safety points, or storage points.
- If step numbering is used, keep it short and stable, with 3–5 steps maximum for 사용법 안내.
- Include realistic Korean microcopy such as “1단계”, “뚜껑을 끝까지 닫기”, “사용 후 물기 제거”, “손잡이 부분 잡기”, “그늘에 보관”, “저장해두고 보기”, and “{페이지표기}”.
- Footer details must read like helpful editorial metadata, for example “{문서번호} · {발행일} · {제작처}”, not like an official government approval mark.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized likenesses
- False safety approval marks or fabricated legal compliance badges

[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean pet natural-light portrait, editorial-style single-subject photo for memorial, SNS, calendar, and merchandise use.
Create a warm, real-world animal portrait with tactile environmental details, lifelike fur, gentle atmosphere, and enough contextual richness to feel like an authentic photographed moment rather than a sterile studio mockup.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Single animal hero subject occupies about 60–70% of the frame, with the face and eyes placed near the upper third for immediate emotional focus.
- Background is a believable natural setting or window-side interior based on {장면}: include realistic details such as sunlit floor texture, linen fabric, wooden bench grain, soft grass, fallen leaves, flower stems, window frame shadows, ceramic bowl, collar tag, or a favorite blanket when appropriate to the scene.
- Eye-level composition at {구도}, with natural breathing room around the head and ears; paws, tail, and chest should feel intentionally framed rather than accidentally cut.
- The scene should feel intimate and calm, with {감정} guiding the pose, ear angle, body posture, and gaze direction.
- Add small documentary cues that support {용도}, such as a subtle corner date/location label, a tiny handwritten-style caption strip, or calendar/postcard-like micro text, while keeping the animal as the emotional center.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Subject block: {동물 종류} rendered as the clear focal point, with crisp fur strands, visible whiskers or muzzle texture, moist nose detail, natural paw or feather texture if visible, and believable catchlights in the eyes.
- Environment block: build the setting from {장면} into a lived-in natural-light portrait space, using layered depth such as foreground grass blades, soft curtain folds, worn wood, fabric weave, dust motes in sunlight, or blurred garden/window shapes.
- Camera framing: follow {구도} precisely, with a stable portrait layout that emphasizes the animal’s face, chest, and upper body while preserving realistic scale and perspective.
- Lighting block: shape the subject with {라이팅}, preserving natural falloff on fur, warm edge highlights, soft shadows under the chin and body, and gentle reflected light from the floor or surrounding surfaces.
- Detail treatment: use {카메라·렌즈} to imply sharp subject separation and shallow depth of field, then apply {필름·톤} for a restrained, filmic color response with fine grain and natural highlight roll-off.
- Expression block: direct the pose toward {감정}, making the gaze feel candid and emotionally honest, as if captured during a quiet walk, a sunlit nap, or a familiar moment at home.
- Usage-aware finish: keep the image polished enough for {용도}, with realistic micro-contrast, organic texture, and a premium editorial finish; avoid over-smoothing, waxy fur, plastic texture, or synthetic HDR-like effects.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: optional small editorial caption only, set in Korean using Pretendard SemiBold or a neat handwritten postcard style; place as a tiny lower-corner label, film-note tag, or calendar caption without covering the face. Example text may include “오늘의 햇살”, “2026.05”, “함께 걷는 오후”, or “서울 · 창가”.
- Color palette: warm cream, amber, muted sage, soft taupe, deep charcoal, and natural fur browns from {필름·톤}.
- Surface details: allow real photographic textures such as linen weave, grass, wood grain, window condensation, paper label texture, faint film grain, and gentle bokeh highlights when they naturally support {장면}.
- Finishing: use a soft realistic contact shadow with about 4px vertical offset, 12px blur, and 15% opacity where a printed card, calendar page, or tabletop presentation is implied; subtle paper edge, postcard note area, or small date stamp may be included if suitable for {용도}.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Fujifilm X-T5 style capture with XF 56mm f/1.2 R WR look, 1/640, ISO 200, f/1.8, shallow depth of field and clean subject separation.
- Lighting: golden-hour side light from frame left or soft window light from upper-left at 45°, with a subtle rim light along the fur edge, visible natural reflections in the eyes, and soft shadow roll-off across the body and nearby surfaces.
- Color grade: Classic Chrome or Portra 400-inspired grading with warm cream, amber highlights, slightly muted midtones, fine analog grain, and a natural editorial finish.

[6. MOOD]
Premium pet editorial portrait — feels like a quietly composed feature from Kinfolk or a refined animal portrait page in National Geographic style, blending gentle documentary realism with affectionate everyday storytelling.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: if text appears, render it cleanly and legibly in Korean, using short phrases only, such as “오늘의 햇살”, “2026.05”, “함께 걷는 오후”, or “서울 · 창가”.
- Anatomy/layout invariants: exactly one animal subject; eyes, nose, ears, limbs, paws, whiskers, feathering, and fur texture must look anatomically natural; no extra limbs, duplicated ears, warped muzzle, mismatched eye size, or distorted face proportions.
- The subject must remain the main focus, with believable optical separation from the background and no artificial sticker-like cutout look.
- Environmental details must support {장면}, {감정}, and {용도} without changing the animal species, camera direction, or core portrait concept.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[1. PURPOSE]
Create a natural-light wedding photograph with an editorial wedding-magazine feel, suitable for wedding albums, invitations, and gallery display. Emphasize a candid emotional moment in a realistic ceremonial setting filled with believable wedding details, atmosphere, and human warmth.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- {장면} as the primary scene setting, with the couple occupying the visual center while the surrounding ceremony environment adds depth and realism.
- {구도} with the couple filling the mid-frame hero area; include softly layered background guests, floral décor, ceremony chairs, aisle petals, fabric ribbons, candles, greenery, or chapel/garden architecture as appropriate to the scene.
- Compose vertically for a premium wedding album spread, allowing the veil, bouquet, dress texture, boutonniere, hands, rings, and emotional facial expressions to be clearly readable.
- Keep facial details gentle and natural, avoiding waxy retouching while preserving real skin texture, soft makeup, stray hair, fabric folds, and authentic contact between the couple.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Main couple area: The couple should be the clear focal point, captured in a candid pre-kiss, forehead touch, vow-reading pause, or intimate embrace moment, with natural body language and balanced posture.
- Wardrobe and detail layer: Show tactile wedding details such as lace veil edges, satin or crepe dress folds, groom suit texture, boutonniere, bouquet stems tied with ribbon, wedding rings, subtle manicure, cuff buttons, and a few wind-touched strands of hair.
- Background layer: Wedding venue elements such as garden greenery, chapel arches, floral arrangements, string lights, linen-draped chairs, petal-scattered aisle, softly blurred guests, ceremony programs, or champagne glasses should sit behind and around the couple in a cinematic depth-of-field layer.
- Incidental text layer: If small venue signage, a paper ceremony program, or a welcome board appears, use natural Korean wedding text such as “오늘의 결혼식”, “축복합니다”, “2026.05.24”, or “신랑 · 신부” as tiny background details, never as a graphic overlay.
- Motion and expression: {감정} should read clearly through relaxed shoulders, soft eye contact, hand placement, breath-before-a-kiss timing, and authentic micro-expressions rather than stiff posed smiles.
- Camera treatment: {카메라·렌즈} should produce a shallow depth of field and flattering portrait compression, with crisp subject separation, soft bokeh, and realistic lens falloff.
- Color and tone layer: {필름·톤} should shape the overall palette into refined pastel wedding tones with airy highlights, warm skin, natural greens, gentle shadow roll-off, and subtle grain.
- Lighting layer: {라이팅} should create a flattering natural rim on hair, veil, shoulders, bouquet edges, and suit lapels while keeping skin tones luminous but not overexposed.
- Usage finish: Frame the image so it works beautifully for {용도}, with a timeless print-ready wedding editorial look and rich real-world ceremony atmosphere.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: no designed overlay typography; only incidental real-world wedding text may appear on background programs, signs, menus, or place cards, and it must be small, natural, and in Korean when legible.
- Color palette: soft cream, ivory, blush coral, warm beige, muted sage, pale gold, pale eucalyptus green, champagne highlights, with Kodak Portra 400-inspired faded pastel balance.
- Texture and materials: include believable fabric texture, bouquet petals, greenery, wood grain, stone or chapel wall detail, paper stationery, candle glass, and soft bokeh highlights to make the scene feel lived-in and photographed on location.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Canon R5 with RF 85mm f/1.2L look, ISO 400, f/1.8, 1/500 sec, portrait telephoto compression.
- Lighting: golden-hour natural light, slightly backlit from behind the couple, subtle hair rim light, glowing veil edge, soft shadow edges, gentle exposure on skin.
- Color grade: Kodak Portra 400 faded tone, soft cream–coral–ivory grading, low saturation, smooth highlight roll-off, delicate film grain, realistic pastel greens and warm beige midtones.

[6. MOOD]
Editorial wedding portrait — a refined Kinfolk-style ceremony photograph with the tenderness of a documentary wedding moment, the tactile richness of a premium lifestyle magazine spread, and the warmth of real guests and venue details softly present around the couple.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: any incidental visible Korean text must be legible and natural, for example “오늘의 결혼식”, “축복합니다”, “2026.05.24”, or “신랑 · 신부”; do not create broken or random Korean characters.
- Preserve natural wedding anatomy and realism: exactly two human subjects as the central couple, anatomically correct hands, natural facial proportions, believable contact, realistic posture, and authentic emotion during the candid moment.
- Keep the scene candid and documentary-like, with real ceremony details, natural venue atmosphere, and a premium editorial wedding-photo finish.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[1. PURPOSE]
35mm black-and-white street snapshot for photo-book, blog, and magazine use.
Documentary urban scene with candid human presence, emphasizing lived-in city texture, natural street density, and analog authenticity.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Frame the scene in a 3:2 landscape composition, with the main figure placed on the left or right third and the rest of the frame filled by real street life, signage, reflections, architecture, and small everyday details.
- Set the location and moment using {장면}, keeping the subject unposed and partially turned away, with {모티프 변주} as the visual variation.
- Build strong depth from foreground street texture to midground subject and background shopfronts, bus-stop elements, posters, utility poles, umbrellas, bicycles, delivery scooters, or passing pedestrians.
- Keep the figure non-identifiable from the front; prefer back view, side profile, partial silhouette, umbrella-obscured face, motion blur, or reflection-based framing to maintain privacy.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Background layer: Build a real urban street environment matching {장면}, with wet pavement reflections, worn curb paint, stacked crates, shop awnings, handwritten notices, menu boards, window stickers, cables, traffic mirrors, crosswalk markings, and weathered building surfaces that feel observed rather than staged.
- Street text layer: Include natural Korean signage only where it belongs in the environment, such as “분식”, “커피”, “세탁”, “24시”, “오늘의 메뉴”, “우산 판매”, “버스정류장”, or a small posted notice like “임시휴무”; these must look printed, painted, or handwritten in the scene, not added as graphic overlays.
- Subject layer: Place one anonymous person as the visual anchor, positioned according to {구도}, with candid body language such as waiting, walking through rain, checking a bag, crossing the street, looking into a shop window, or pausing under an awning.
- Human environment layer: Add secondary passersby as blurred silhouettes or cropped partial figures, plus traces of daily life such as steam from a food stall, rain droplets on glass, a folded newspaper, plastic stools, a delivery helmet, or a bus arriving in the distance.
- Camera look: Render as {카메라·렌즈}, with visible 35mm documentary framing, slight grain, modest edge falloff, handheld imperfection, and natural motion character.
- Tonal layer: Apply {필름·톤} so blacks stay rich, midtones remain textured, skin and fabric tones translate naturally into grayscale, and bright signs or reflections retain detail.
- Light layer: Use {라이팅} with realistic shadow density, ambient bounce from storefronts and pavement, and documentary naturalism.
- Editorial layer: Keep the image suitable for photo essays and magazine spreads, aligned with {무드}, with enough authentic detail to reward close viewing.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: no designed caption blocks or editorial text overlays; allow real-world Korean street typography embedded in signs, stickers, posters, menus, license plates, or shop windows.
- Color palette: pure black, charcoal gray, silver gray, wet asphalt gray, fog white; if any color bleed appears, keep it muted and subordinate to monochrome realism.
- Film edge: if a print-like edge appears, use subtle darkroom scan falloff, slight gate shadow, or contact-sheet irregularity that feels photographic rather than graphic.
- Texture realism: emphasize damp concrete, scratched glass, corrugated shutters, peeling paper, fabric folds, rain speckles, scuffed shoes, and reflected streetlights in grayscale.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Leica M6, Summicron 35mm f/2, Kodak Tri-X 400 look, 1/125s, f/4, handheld street photography perspective.
- Lighting: natural light only; overcast diffused daylight or side light, with soft contrast, ambient storefront glow if appropriate, and no artificial fill or flash.
- Color grade: monochrome Tri-X classic grade, deep blacks, clean midtones, detailed shadows, fine silver grain, restrained highlight roll-off.
- Optics: realistic 35mm perspective with mild barrel character, imperfect focus falloff, slight motion softness on moving pedestrians, and crisp tactile detail where the focal plane lands.

[6. MOOD]
Magnum contact-sheet realism — Henri Cartier-Bresson street photography sensibility with a classic documentary press-photo feel, but grounded in a dense contemporary Korean street moment shaped by {무드}.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: any visible Korean signage or notices must be legible and natural, using short real-world phrases such as “분식”, “커피”, “세탁”, “오늘의 메뉴”, “임시휴무”, or “버스정류장”; avoid random or broken characters.
- Keep the subject anonymous and non-identifiable from the front; do not create a recognizable portrait or front-facing close-up.
- Maintain a believable 35mm street-photo candid look with no polished advertising composition and no obvious digital retouching.
- Preserve the requested {장면}, {구도}, {카메라·렌즈}, {필름·톤}, {라이팅}, {무드}, and {모티프 변주} as the dominant creative instructions.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized recognizable likeness

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean outdoor natural-light fashion lookbook, editorial vertical format for seasonal campaign pages, printed lookbook sheets, and social media previews.
Create a realistic premium fashion page with a photographed model, tactile street atmosphere, readable outfit details, small editorial text elements, issue/date labeling, barcode area, and campaign-style credits.
Commercial lookbook image with full-body and half-body outfit presentation, emphasizing fabric texture, silhouette, styling layers, and the lived-in quality of an outdoor Korean city setting.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- {모델} should be the clear focal subject, occupying about 55–65% of the frame, with one dominant full-body fashion photograph and one tighter inset or secondary crop emphasizing upper-body styling, fabric texture, collar, sleeves, bag, shoes, or accessories.
- Place the scene in {장면} with real outdoor depth: pavement texture, weathered wall surfaces, soft foliage, storefront reflection, curb line, steps, railing, shadow patterns, or passing-city details that support the lookbook mood without hiding the outfit.
- Use {구도} to create a balanced editorial page feel, arranging the hero image, inset image, garment captions, small page markers, and barcode/credit area like a premium printed campaign spread.
- Wardrobe styling should reflect {컬렉션·시즌} with relaxed but polished posture, hands relaxed, shoulders natural, believable walking or leaning motion, and editorial confidence rather than stiff commercial posing.
- Include small realistic production details: LOOK number, collection/date label, model credit, page number, barcode block, and 2–3 short Korean editorial blurbs placed around the images.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Hero subject area: {모델} standing or walking in a natural pose, with the main outfit fully readable from head to toe, shoes visible, hemline clearly visible, and fabric folds responding naturally to posture and breeze.
- Secondary fashion crop: include a smaller inset frame or overlapping contact-sheet style crop showing face, upper body, sleeve detail, textile surface, jewelry, bag strap, or layered styling, consistent with the same outfit and {컬렉션·시즌}.
- Environment layer: {장면} rendered as a real outdoor location with architectural lines, ground texture, foliage, signage fragments, reflected daylight, and believable urban depth that frames the model.
- Editorial information layer: add a refined masthead area, VOL.249 issue marker, date label, barcode area, small spine/credit text, model-name credit, page indicator, and short Korean fashion blurbs such as seasonal styling notes.
- Composition layer: {구도} arranged like a fashion editorial spread, with one image emphasizing full silhouette and one image emphasizing upper-body detail and outfit texture; allow layered paper edges, tiny crop marks, alignment guides, or caption rules for a printed-lookbook feel.
- Technical realism layer: {카메라·렌즈} look should produce medium-format compression, clean skin texture, natural fabric micro-texture, true-to-life seams, and gentle separation between subject and background.
- Atmosphere layer: {라이팅} should shape soft shadows on clothing folds, show natural daylight direction, preserve realistic skin tones, and reveal details in pavement, walls, hair, and accessories.
- Finish layer: apply {포스트} so blacks stay rich, highlights remain controlled, color stays premium and restrained, and the overall image feels like a photographed Korean outdoor campaign page printed on matte stock.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: visible editorial typography is required. Use Pretendard SemiBold or Noto Sans KR Medium, 28–42px for main Korean headings and 12–18px for captions, date, credit, page numbers, and garment notes. Keep the type aligned to the editorial grid and integrated with the photographs.
- Suggested rendered text elements: masthead, issue/date label, LOOK 01 and LOOK 02 markers, model credit, 2–3 short Korean blurbs, barcode label, page number, and small vertical spine text.
- Color palette: cream #F5F0E8, stone beige #D8CBB8, charcoal #2B2B2B, muted olive #8A9276, denim blue #4D6475.
- Border/shadow: subtle editorial print softness, very light paper-edge shadow, soft drop shadow for layered collage treatment, faint film grain, realistic paper tooth, and restrained crop marks or registration dots if they enhance the lookbook layout.
- Decorative details: include tasteful graphic rules, tiny page indicators, garment caption dividers, swatch-like color chips, or small seasonal tags that support the fashion presentation.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: shot on Pentax 67 with 105mm f/2.4, Kodak Portra 800, f/4, 1/250, medium-format look with gentle compression and clean tonal rolloff.
- Lighting: overcast diffused daylight for even skin and fabric rendering, or golden-hour side light from camera-left for warm edge definition and soft shadow falloff.
- Color grade: muted warm neutrals with restrained contrast, Portra-style beige, olive, and soft brown tones, with slightly lifted shadows and natural highlights.
- Surface realism: matte printed lookbook page, subtle paper texture, natural film grain, accurate fabric weave, realistic shoe soles, hair strands, skin pores, and outdoor texture detail.

[6. MOOD]
Korean fashion editorial — feels like a Celine or The Row lookbook photographed in a quiet Kinfolk-style city street setting, but enriched with real campaign-page details, tactile outdoor atmosphere, and premium printed magazine realism.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: render all visible Korean cleanly and legibly. Include these text elements where appropriate: 자연광 룩북, {컬렉션·시즌}, 도시 산책의 결, 가벼운 레이어링, 오래 입는 실루엣, LOOK 01, LOOK 02, MODEL {모델}, 2026년 5월호, VOL.249, PAGE 08.
- Add a small barcode area with numeric microtext and a tiny credit line such as photographed in seoul / outdoor editorial / natural light, keeping it secondary to the model and outfit.
- The model must look naturally posed, with realistic body proportions, anatomically correct hands, and no duplicated limbs or distorted clothing edges.
- Outfit details must remain consistent with {컬렉션·시즌} across the entire image, including the hero full-body view and the secondary crop.
- Preserve realistic clothing construction: seams, buttons, lapels, cuffs, hems, shoe shape, bag straps, fabric weight, and wrinkles should align with posture and daylight.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized likeness

[1. PURPOSE]
Professional food photography layout for a restaurant menu, in-store pricelist, and delivery-app promo, with a magazine-quality editorial finish.
Vertical full-bleed food image that combines premium plated food photography with realistic Korean menu information, ready for print menu use, Instagram, and premium delivery listings.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main food area occupies about 60–65% of the frame, with {메뉴 모티프} presented as the hero subject and a designed menu-information zone integrated along the upper or side area.
- Background uses {배경·소품} as a tactile restaurant surface, including real tabletop texture, fabric folds, utensil reflections, crumbs, sauce sheen, garnish fragments, and small service details that naturally fit the dish.
- Composition follows {구도}, with framing that emphasizes the dish silhouette, ingredient texture, plated balance, and printed menu usability.
- The dish should read as the primary hero, while supporting props such as folded linen, cutlery, small sauce dish, water glass rim, receipt corner, or menu card reinforce restaurant mood and scale.
- Use {메뉴 모티프} as the exact food subject, arranged with natural asymmetry, appetizing garnish placement, and premium plating discipline.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Hero plating zone: {메뉴 모티프} rendered as the central subject, with crisp edges, visible surface texture, realistic moisture, browned edges, cream layers, glaze, garnish, or ingredient detail appropriate to the dish.
- Menu/pricelist zone: add a refined Korean menu block for {매장명}, including category title, 4–6 menu items, prices, short descriptions, address, contact, and business hours, laid out like a premium restaurant menu overlay or printed menu card placed on the table.
- Information hierarchy: include {대표메뉴명} as the highlighted dish name, {대표가격} as the main price, and a smaller “오늘의 추천” or “시그니처” label near the hero dish.
- Surface and base: place the dish on {배경·소품}, allowing wood grain, slate texture, linen weave, ceramic glaze, metal cutlery, and soft contact shadows to enrich the restaurant atmosphere.
- Light-and-shadow structure: shape highlights so the food surface looks dimensional, with controlled shadow falloff, believable reflections on glaze or sauce, and no plastic-looking shine.
- Atmosphere detail: keep 음식 텍스처·증기·스팀 자연스럽게, with realistic heat cues only where appropriate, such as subtle warmth above noodles, soup, steak, or fresh pastry.
- Final polish: maintain a premium magazine-food aesthetic for {용도}, with natural color fidelity, elegant typography placement, and commercial menu readability.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: include Korean menu typography in a tasteful editorial layout, mixing a refined serif-style headline with small sans-serif details; text should look printed or professionally overlaid, aligned with dividers and price columns.
- Menu details: show {매장명}, {메뉴카테고리}, {대표메뉴명}, {대표가격}, {주소}, {연락처}, {영업시간}, and 4–6 additional item lines with realistic won prices.
- Graphic accents: use thin divider lines, small dot leaders, tiny allergen-style icons, a small QR-style reservation mark, and subtle section labels, all integrated with the food photo rather than floating randomly.
- Color palette: natural food colors balanced with deep neutrals from {컬러·톤}; include dark walnut brown, slate gray, warm cream, muted beige, ink black, and subdued accent tones.
- Print finish: menu panel or card may have soft paper texture, slight shadow, rounded corners, foil-like dark ink accents, or a small stamped date label to feel like an actual restaurant menu.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: {카메라·렌즈}, with premium medium-format clarity and controlled depth separation.
- Lighting: {라이팅}, mimicking soft studio daylight from one side and creating natural, controlled shadows across plate, paper, utensils, and tabletop.
- Color grade: {컬러·톤}, natural food color fidelity with a slightly dark matte magazine grade, restrained contrast, and elegant tonal separation.
- Rendering quality: high-resolution commercial food photo realism, tactile paper and tabletop detail, readable Korean typography, realistic ceramic, glass, metal, sauce, crumb, and garnish materials.

[6. MOOD]
Premium editorial food still life — akin to a high-end restaurant menu spread and boutique bistro print menu, with refined commercial polish, appetizing realism, and a warm dining-table atmosphere.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: render legible Korean menu text, including “{매장명}”, “{메뉴카테고리}”, “대표 메뉴”, “{대표메뉴명}”, “{대표가격}”, “오늘의 추천”, “주소 {주소}”, “문의 {연락처}”, “영업시간 {영업시간}”.
- Add realistic sample item lines in Korean, such as “트러플 크림 파스타 ₩18,000”, “한우 채끝 스테이크 ₩42,000”, “계절 샐러드 ₩13,000”, “바닐라 에클레어 ₩7,500”, with aligned prices and small descriptions.
- Maintain realistic food anatomy and plating structure: the dish must look physically possible, with believable ingredients, portions, temperature cues, utensils, and surface texture.
- Keep the layout consistent with restaurant-menu usage: readable, appetizing, commercially usable, and suitable for {용도}.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized likeness mashups

[INPUT]

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean café interior editorial photo, film-toned lifestyle space image for magazine header and blog cover.
Designed to feel like a premium interior spread with a human-scaled, shareable café atmosphere: warm surfaces, real furniture wear, layered table objects, small menu signage, and believable neighborhood café details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- The main scene centers on a café interior with the counter or window-side table taking about 55–65% of the frame, while the remaining space shows walls, shelving, plants, chairs, framed art, and café service details for depth.
- Background should be a real interior surface with wood grain, soft off-white walls, plaster texture, faint scuffs near chair legs, fabric upholstery, ceramic objects, and naturally imperfect lived-in details.
- Keep the framing wide and editorial, using {구도} as the base composition, with architectural lines, furniture placement, and daylight guiding the eye through the café.
- Place {소품 디테일} naturally on the table or counter, supported by realistic café items such as a ceramic latte cup, small pastry plate, folded receipt, paper napkin, water glass, menu card, coffee beans jar, order buzzer, magazine, linen pouch, or a casually placed tote bag.
- Add subtle environmental text only as real café signage: a small chalkboard or printed menu near the counter, shelf labels, or a tiny receipt, integrated into the scene rather than overlaid on top.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Hero zone: build the main visual around {공간 컨셉}, with the counter edge, window table, or row of chairs acting as a leading line into the space.
2. Light behavior: use {시간대} as the key daylight mood, with sunlight entering from one side and creating soft shadow bands across the floor, tabletop, chair backs, ceramic cups, and plant leaves.
3. Material detail: emphasize walnut or oak counter texture, chair fabric weave, ceramic glaze, paper fiber, glass reflections, brushed metal espresso tools, and plant leaves with gentle contrast and visible film grain.
4. Styling layer: place {소품 디테일} in a relaxed arrangement with believable café clutter: spoon marks, a half-torn sugar packet, pastry crumbs, stacked saucers, folded napkins, a small vase with seasonal stems, and a handwritten order slip.
5. Environmental realism: include background shelves with cups and coffee bags, a grinder silhouette, menu board, framed print, outlet plate, coat hook, small floor plant, textured curtain, and slight variations in furniture alignment.
6. Camera look: render the scene as {카메라·렌즈}, with natural perspective, realistic depth, and no wide-angle distortion.
7. Tone finish: apply {필름·톤} across highlights, midtones, and shadows so the image feels like a scanned film editorial frame rather than a digital interior render.
8. Layout use: ensure the final composition can support {비율·용도} while keeping the main table/counter, key props, and architectural rhythm intact.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: no graphic overlay text; any visible text must exist physically in the café, such as a small printed menu, handwritten chalkboard, receipt, bean bag label, or wall card. Use clean Korean lettering similar to Pretendard SemiBold, Noto Sans KR Medium, or casual handwritten chalk script.
- Suggested environmental Korean text: menu board lines like '오늘의 원두', '아메리카노 4.8', '카페라떼 5.5', '바닐라빈 라떼 6.2', '소금빵 3.8', or a tiny receipt reading '주문번호 27'. Keep it small and naturally photographed.
- Color palette: warm cream, amber, walnut brown, muted olive, soft beige, matte black accents, milky ceramic white, pale brass, and gentle shadow gray; keep saturation controlled and avoid neon or overly vivid greens.
- Surfaces and shadows: natural shadow under cups, saucers, chair legs, plants, and props, with soft falloff, realistic contact shadows, slight dust in light beams, fingerprints on glass, and delicate film halation around bright window edges.
- Composition density: create a rich editorial café scene with layered foreground, middle ground, and background objects; avoid sterile showroom staging or perfectly aligned catalog furniture.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Fujifilm X-T5 look, XF 23mm f/1.4 equivalent 35mm, ISO 400, f/2.8, documentary interior photography perspective.
- Lighting: natural window light only, coming from the side at roughly 45°, with soft bounce fill from the opposite wall and no obvious studio setup.
- Color grade: Kodak Portra 160 style grading, warm cream + amber highlights, slightly muted greens, soft highlight roll-off, gentle film grain, mild vignette, and a scanned-photo softness in the deepest shadows.

[6. MOOD]
Premium café interior editorial — a Kinfolk magazine spread meets a quiet boutique coffee-house atmosphere, with the realism of a Seoul neighborhood café just before the afternoon rush.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: if visible café text appears, keep it short and legible, for example '오늘의 원두', '카페라떼 5.5', '소금빵 3.8', '주문번호 27', '테이크아웃 가능'. Do not garble Korean characters.
- The scene must read as a real café interior with plausible architecture, furniture scale, natural object placement, functional counter equipment, and believable wear on surfaces.
- Do not introduce people unless they are part of the intended composition; if people appear, they should be incidental café customers or staff with correct anatomy, natural posture, and no distracting emphasis.
- Preserve {공간 컨셉}, {시간대}, {구도}, {카메라·렌즈}, {필름·톤}, {소품 디테일}, and {비율·용도} exactly as the controlling inputs.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

studio:prompts3:ours-246.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1536x1024
- title: 서울·홍콩·도쿄 네온 야경 사진

[1. PURPOSE]
Cinematic urban night photography for reels, blog headers, music artwork, and premium editorial-style city visuals.
Create a wide horizontal night street scene with rain-slick asphalt, layered neon signage, realistic storefront life, and a noir-cinematic atmosphere inspired by Seoul, Hong Kong, and Tokyo night districts.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- {도시장면} should define the main street or alley environment, with wet pavement occupying the lower 30–40% and dense signage layers filling the upper two-thirds.
- {시간대·계절} should be felt through air density, clothing, puddle texture, condensation on glass, and late-night street activity.
- {인물모티프} should remain secondary and small in frame, placed near the lower third or mid-depth so the neon environment stays dominant.
- {구도} should anchor the vanishing point near the center, with left-right signage, awnings, shop windows, wires, and parked scooters forming a corridor-like frame.
- Include {거리디테일} as believable street-life evidence: delivery bikes, taxi tail lights, menu boards, plastic crates, rain gutters, vending machines, small puddles, and reflections stretching toward the camera.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Background layer: build a dense city-night setting based on {도시장면}, with stacked signs, narrow storefronts, utility wires, dark building facades, apartment windows, and a few lit upper-floor rooms.
- Signage layer: mix large vertical neon signs, smaller LED boards, handwritten paper notices, wet acrylic menu boards, and window decals using {주요간판문구} and {보조간판문구} where text is readable.
- Mid-ground: place {인물모티프} as a silhouette or distant figure near the lower third, partially softened by rain haze, passing headlights, or slight handheld motion blur.
- Foreground: render wet asphalt, puddles, crosswalk paint, curb edges, manhole covers, cigarette butts, folded umbrellas, and rippling neon reflections with realistic surface breakup.
- Light sources: layer neon tubes, shop signs, taxi brake lights, vending-machine glow, convenience-store spill, and warm restaurant windows so reflections ripple across wet asphalt without turning into flat graphic glow.
- Perspective: follow {구도} so the street corridor pulls the eye inward, with signage framing both sides and the brightest highlight near the center depth.
- Camera treatment: render with {카메라렌즈} for a low-light full-frame look, preserving crisp sign edges, natural handheld micro-motion, controlled grain, and believable depth falloff.
- Color atmosphere: apply {필름톤} as the base palette, keeping halation realistic around bright tubes and preserving shadow detail in storefront recesses.
- Mood variation: adapt the final feel to {모드변주} while keeping documentary street-photo realism intact.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: embedded street signage may use Hangul, numbers, small English fragments, or East Asian sign styling; Korean signs should be legible, correctly spaced, and naturally integrated into shop boards, window decals, price menus, and vertical neon panels.
- Street text density: include 5–10 readable or semi-readable signs at different depths, with a few crisp foreground/mid-ground Korean signs and softer background signage affected by rain and lens focus.
- Color palette: use deep navy #0B1020, cyan neon #00D4FF, hot pink #FF4FA3, tungsten amber #FFB15A, rain-slick black #050608, and occasional green pharmacy or taxi highlights.
- Natural separation: use real shadow pockets under awnings, wet curb reflections, window-frame silhouettes, mist diffusion, and subtle lens halation around bright signage.
- Realism details: keep pavement reflections directionally tied to actual light sources, vary sign brightness by distance, and let rain haze soften distant contrast while foreground textures remain tactile.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Sony A7S III look, 35mm f/1.4 GM, ISO 3200, f/1.8, 1/60, handheld night street photography.
- Lighting: neon sign illumination mixed with wet-road bounce, soft mist diffusion, taxi tail-light streaks, convenience-store spill, and faint ambient glow from second-floor windows; directional highlights should come from signage at mid-height and above.
- Color grade: Cinestill 800T-inspired tungsten-blue palette with coral and hot-pink accents, restrained contrast, realistic halation, fine low-light grain, and a clean cinematic roll-off.
- Texture rendering: emphasize water beads on umbrellas, glossy vinyl awnings, cracked asphalt, rain-streaked glass, brushed metal shutters, plastic menu boards, and slightly fogged shop windows.

[6. MOOD]
Wong Kar-wai-inspired city night still — neon-soaked, rain-reflected, intimate, cinematic, and frame-friendly like a premium travel magazine spread captured after midnight.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Render Korean signage cleanly when visible; recommended readable text includes “심야식당”, “24시 편의점”, “포장마차”, “비 오는 밤”, “택시 승강장”, “라멘·우동”, and “오늘의 메뉴”.
- If price/menu details appear, use believable Korean filler such as “김치우동 8,500원”, “생맥주 5,000원”, “야식 세트 12,000원”, and keep numbers aligned on menu boards.
- Preserve a realistic night-photo feel: reflections must come from wet surfaces, puddles, glass, headlights, and neon tubes, with rain haze and lens halation behaving naturally.
- Keep figure(s) anatomically correct if visible, with natural silhouette proportions, believable umbrella handling, grounded feet, and reflections matching their position.
- Maintain the 1536x1024 horizontal composition; prioritize cinematic depth, layered signage, and tactile rainy-street realism over flat poster-like effects.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters or unreadable Hangul on intended signage
- Celebrity composites or recognizable public figures
- Impossible anatomy, duplicated umbrellas, warped hands/faces

studio:prompts3:ours-245.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1536x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Magazine-quality nature landscape photograph for editorial travel content, suitable for framed wall art, travel posts, premium scenic storytelling, and a realistic destination feature spread that feels photographed on location.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Wide horizontal landscape with a 3:2 feel, where the ridge line or horizon sits around the upper or lower third depending on {구도}.
- Main landform mass occupies roughly 40–55% of the frame, supported by layered sky, mist, water, forest canopy, shoreline, or valley detail so the frame feels expansive and lived-in.
- Background surface should feel real and tactile: layered mountain silhouettes, dense conifer outlines, calm lake surface with ripples, waterfall spray, wet rock faces, reed field texture, cloud shadows, and distant tree-line variation depending on {모티프 변주}.
- Keep {자연 모티프} as the focal narrative element, with realistic secondary details such as a narrow hiking path, small wooden dock, scattered boulders, dew on grasses, floating leaves, distant birds, or a tiny hiker/boat only when it naturally fits the setting.
- Compose the scene with strong foreground-to-background depth: textured earth or shoreline in front, the primary natural subject in the midground, and atmospheric mountain/forest layers fading into the distance.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Foreground layer: anchor the scene with dark, detailed terrain edges, shoreline texture, tree trunks, reeds, moss, fallen branches, wildflowers, wet stones, pine needles, or rocky slope contours to create depth.
- Midground layer: place {자연 모티프} as the primary subject, with mist breaking the silhouette separation and guiding the eye through the frame; include believable natural irregularities such as uneven tree heights, exposed roots, sediment lines, and subtle water movement.
- Atmospheric layer: use {시간대·날씨} to build soft depth compression, with visible mist bands, drifting low clouds, faint rain traces, frost sparkle, or light haze and subtle light scattering rather than heavy fog opacity.
- Light behavior: apply {라이팅} so the scene has dimensionality, with rays or edge glow appearing naturally between trees, ridges, grasses, rock faces, or across water; reflections should respond to the real direction of light.
- Environmental realism: add small location-specific cues such as rippled reflections, bird silhouettes, broken reeds, lichen on rocks, snow patches on distant ridges, fallen leaves, or moisture on foliage without distracting from the main landscape.
- Camera rendering: {카메라·렌즈} for crisp landscape detail, realistic perspective, and controlled depth from foreground to distant ridge.
- Tonal finish: preserve {필름·톤} with natural greens, cool blues, and restrained contrast; keep highlights gentle and avoid clipped whites.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: no text overlays; the image should read as a pure photographic landscape, not a graphic poster.
- Color palette: deep forest green, pine blue, mist gray, slate teal, and soft dawn gold, aligned with {필름·톤}; allow earthy browns, moss yellow, rock charcoal, and water reflections where naturally present.
- Composition finish: prioritize authentic travel-photography framing with natural edges, environmental depth, and realistic detail; if the scene includes water, reflections should be slightly imperfect with ripples, reeds, or floating debris.
- Surface realism: foliage, bark, rock, snow, mist, and water must show varied texture, scale, and natural imperfections rather than smooth synthetic surfaces.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Fujifilm GFX100 II look, 32-64mm f/4 at 50mm, ISO 100, f/11, high-resolution landscape capture with clean micro-contrast.
- Lighting: {라이팅} with low-angle directional light, diffused through mist; if sunrise, keep the sun just outside frame or partially obscured by terrain.
- Color grade: Fuji Velvia 50-inspired landscape grading with rich but believable greens and blues, slight cyan bias, controlled saturation, and natural atmospheric perspective.
- Photographic detail: retain fine branch structure, believable leaf clusters, nuanced cloud texture, realistic water specular highlights, and subtle tonal separation across distant ridges.

[6. MOOD]
National Geographic-style wilderness editorial — calm, expansive, documentary-real, and immersive, with the feeling of standing at a quiet scenic overlook during {시간대·날씨}.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: no visible Korean text should appear in the image.
- Maintain a believable photographic landscape: no surreal terrain, no artificial glow, no painterly brush texture, and no overprocessed HDR look.
- If a tiny hiker appears in {자연 모티프}, keep the person anatomically correct and proportionally small within the environment.
- All natural elements must follow real scale relationships: trees, rocks, mist, lake reflections, ridges, wildlife, and human traces should look physically plausible.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness

[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1536x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean seascape photo for travel content, editorial wall art, and Reels cover. Wide coastal landscape with sunrise or dusk atmosphere, realistic waves, tactile shoreline details, and cinematic scale.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Primary framing: {구도} with a calm horizon line placed precisely on the upper or lower third, keeping the sea surface broad, layered, and naturally detailed.
- Scene layout: {장면구성} with the cliff/rocks acting as a visual anchor on the left, ocean bands leading the eye across the frame, and wet sand on the right reflecting the sky.
- Atmosphere treatment: {시간대날씨} with thin mist hugging the waterline, soft atmospheric depth, and gentle contrast shaped by low-angle coastal light.
- Foreground realism: add {전경디테일} in the lower foreground so the beach feels lived-in and photographed on location, not like an empty stock backdrop.
- Scale cue: keep the small figure from {장면구성} tiny but readable near the shoreline, turned toward the sea, emphasizing the vastness of the coast.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Background plane: build a layered ocean scene from foreground foam to mid-distance waves to a pale horizon, with subtle tonal separation between each band.
- Left anchor zone: place cliffs and wet rocks in the left third, textured with dark volcanic stone, mossy edges, tide marks, and small glints of reflected sunrise.
- Center flow zone: let the wave direction and foam trails guide the viewer’s eye horizontally toward the horizon, using smooth long-exposure motion while retaining a few crisp foam edges.
- Right shoreline zone: show wet reflective sand with footprints, shallow ripples, small shells, and a faint trail where the tide recently receded.
- Natural life/details: include {자연요소} such as distant seabirds, a tiny fishing boat near the horizon, and subtle sea spray caught in the light.
- Human scale element: place one tiny silhouette from {장면구성} near the shoreline edge, standing naturally and not posing for the camera.
- Motion rendering: show {셔터기법} so the water becomes soft and mist-like while the rocks, horizon, and main shoreline textures remain crisp.
- Editorial overlay: add a small lower-left travel caption block with {여행캡션}, {위치라벨}, and {날짜라벨}, placed like a tasteful magazine/Reels cover metadata tag without covering the horizon.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard Medium or Noto Sans KR Bold for the small Korean caption block; clean editorial alignment, white or warm off-white text with a faint translucent shadow for readability.
- Color palette: {컬러톤} with pale pink, lavender, warm gold, muted sea blue, wet charcoal rock, and soft gray highlights; keep the palette natural and restrained.
- Shoreline texture: preserve tactile detail in rocks, shells, foam lace, wet sand reflection, light haze, and cloud gradation so the scene feels like a real coastal morning.
- Print/Reels readiness: composition should work as a 3:2 landscape photograph and still crop gracefully for a horizontal Reels cover, with the caption block remaining readable.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: {카메라렌즈} with a natural wide-angle coastal perspective and controlled edge distortion.
- Lighting: low-angle sunrise or sunset light from the side, softened by thin cloud cover and sea haze, with gentle rim highlights on water texture, rocks, and the distant figure.
- Color grade: {포스트} with faded cinematic coastal grade, pastel dawn/sunset tones, restrained contrast, lightly lifted shadows, and realistic highlight roll-off.
- Exposure feel: tripod-stable landscape photography, clean detail in the cliff and sand, smooth water motion, no artificial HDR halos.

[6. MOOD]
Quiet premium travel editorial — like a refined Korean coastal travel feature mixed with a restrained European seaside landscape photograph, calm but richly observed.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: render the caption exactly as “{여행캡션}”, “{위치라벨}”, and “{날짜라벨}”; all Korean characters must be clean, correctly spaced, and legible.
- Anatomy/layout invariants: the horizon must be perfectly level, the perspective must feel wide but not warped, and the small figure must remain proportionally tiny for scale.
- Realism invariants: water motion should look like true long exposure, rocks and horizon must stay sharp, and the beach details must follow the tide direction naturally.
- Composition invariants: keep the cliff/rock mass on the left third, the reflective shoreline on the right, and the caption block low and unobtrusive.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

[1. PURPOSE]
Studio mood portrait image for editorial and professional profile use, designed as a refined single-subject vertical portrait with magazine-cover-level polish and realistic studio presence.
Use for {용도} with a controlled studio look, clean facial detail, understated premium atmosphere, and subtle editorial profile-card information layered into the frame.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Subject placement: {구도} with the face occupying about 45–55% of the frame, composed as a premium vertical portrait with natural headroom and a confident editorial crop.
- Background treatment: {배경} with a subtle tonal falloff, visible studio depth, soft fabric or paper backdrop texture, faint shadow gradients, and realistic separation around hair and shoulders.
- Framing direction: vertical portrait crop, centered or slightly off-center for an editorial feel, with crisp edge separation from background and enough room for small profile-card typography.
- Subject styling: {인물 묘사} with a composed, polished presence; clothing should read clearly against the dark background, including realistic fabric texture, collar lines, seams, jewelry or styling details if naturally appropriate.
- Editorial overlay elements: add small refined profile-card details such as a date/location label, model credit, subtle caption, and two small tag/sticker accents placed around the portrait without covering the face.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Main portrait area: {인물 묘사} presented as the clear focal point, with natural skin texture preserved, believable pores, fine hair detail, and no plastic smoothing.
2) Face and shoulders: {구도} rendered with balanced headroom, subtle eye catchlights, natural expression, and realistic shoulder posture.
3) Background plane: {배경} with premium studio texture, gentle tonal falloff, soft shadow contact behind the subject, and believable depth rather than a flat mockup.
4) Lighting build: {라이팅} shaping the face with soft contrast, gentle falloff, luminous catchlights, and a premium studio portrait separation.
5) Camera rendering: {카메라·렌즈} used to produce realistic depth, crisp detail, controlled perspective compression, and medium-format sharpness.
6) Color treatment: {컬러·톤} applied across skin, clothing, background, and overlay typography with restrained saturation and matte finish.
7) Profile-card details: include small Korean editorial text elements such as “PROFILE 2026.05”, “서울 스튜디오”, “나다운 온도”, “MODEL / {인물 묘사}”, and “@studio.mood” in a tasteful layout.
8) Final output use: {용도} with a polished, publication-ready portrait look suitable for profile, portfolio, and editorial cover contexts.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: include small premium editorial typography in Korean and simple Latin labels; use refined sans-serif or quiet serif styling, aligned like a professional portrait profile card.
- Text hierarchy: one small date/location label near the top or side, one short Korean caption near the lower third, one model-name credit line, and tiny tag-like accents; keep the face unobstructed.
- Color palette: use the restrained palette from {컬러·톤}, centered on charcoal, deep navy, muted flesh tones, and low-saturation neutrals; keep blacks rich but not crushed.
- Border/shadow: allow a subtle editorial card-edge shadow, delicate corner registration marks, or thin understated divider lines if they support a premium profile layout; keep all graphic elements elegant and integrated.
- Realism details: retain natural skin, individual hair strands, fabric weave, slight lens falloff, soft catchlights, and realistic studio shadows.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: shot on Phase One XF IQ4 150MP, 80mm f/2.8 LS, ISO 50, f/4.0, with clean medium-format detail and slight perspective compression.
- Lighting: Profoto large softbox key light at 45° from front-left, small rim light from rear-right, face shadows diffused smoothly with controlled contrast.
- Color grade: matte studio editorial grade, near-monochrome with charcoal, skin-tone beige, and deep navy balancing subtle warmth and coolness.
- Graphic finish: subtle magazine-profile-card layout with crisp micro typography, tasteful alignment, and realistic ink-on-print or digital editorial overlay feel.

[6. MOOD]
Premium studio editorial portrait — sophisticated magazine-profile energy with an understated Aesop / The Gentlewoman aesthetic, quiet confidence, tactile studio realism, and a polished professional identity-card atmosphere.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: render all visible Korean text cleanly and correctly, especially “서울 스튜디오”, “나다운 온도”, “프로필 기록”, and “오늘의 무드”.
- Required visible text examples: “PROFILE 2026.05”, “서울 스튜디오”, “나다운 온도”, “MODEL / {인물 묘사}”, “@studio.mood”.
- Anatomy/layout invariants: facial proportions must be natural; eyes, nose, mouth, ears, and hairline must be anatomically correct; hands should only appear if included naturally in the crop, and any visible hands must have exactly 5 fingers per hand.
- Keep the portrait realistic, sharp, and human; preserve skin texture, subtle facial asymmetry, fabric texture, and natural lighting transitions.
- All typography must be secondary to the portrait and must not cover the eyes, nose, mouth, or key facial contours.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness

[1. PURPOSE]
Create an outdoor natural-light portrait image for Korean social media profiles and magazine-style sharing. The result should feel like a classic 35mm film editorial portrait with a candid, polished finish, enriched with subtle profile-card details that make it look like a real lifestyle feature rather than a plain mockup.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Place {인물 묘사} as the clear subject, occupying about 55–65% of the frame, with the face and upper body emphasized for profile-friendly readability.
- Use {장면} as a softly blurred real-world backdrop, with recognizable street, park, riverside, café-front, foliage, railing, pavement, signage, or city-life details that support the story of the portrait.
- Keep {구도} framing with natural breathing room around the gaze direction and enough surrounding environment to feel like a spontaneous outdoor editorial capture.
- Use {포즈} as the main body language cue, avoiding stiff posing and preserving a candid walking-or-pausing snapshot feel.
- Add small editorial portrait-card details: a discreet date/location label, a tiny caption line, and 1–2 subtle sticker/tag elements placed near the edge of the composition without covering the face.
- Background treatment: outdoor daylight scene with gentle depth separation, natural color variation from trees, buildings, seasonal flowers, water reflections, parked bicycles, benches, shop windows, or passing pedestrians rendered softly in the distance.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Subject zone (center-left 60%): {인물 묘사} rendered with realistic skin texture, subtle facial detail, catchlights in the eyes, natural hair flyaways, fabric texture, and crisp focus on eyes and hair edges.
- Environmental zone (full background): {장면} kept softly out of focus with visible seasonal cues such as autumn leaves, spring blossoms, summer greenery, winter light, riverside railings, café awnings, sidewalk texture, or warm building reflections, depending on the setting.
- Pose/action layer: {포즈} captured mid-motion or in a brief pause, with relaxed shoulders, natural hand placement, believable clothing folds, and an authentic candid expression.
- Framing layer: {구도} maintained with a vertical magazine portrait crop, comfortable headroom, realistic shoulder and hand placement, and no awkward cutoffs at joints.
- Light behavior layer: {라이팅} shaping the hair, cheek contour, eyelashes, nose bridge, collarbone, sleeve edges, and shoulder line with soft separation from the background.
- Camera rendering layer: {카메라·렌즈} used to create shallow depth of field, gentle compression, organic bokeh, and natural perspective without an artificial studio look.
- Tone layer: {필름·톤} applied to keep skin tones clean, highlights soft, contrast modest, grain fine, and the overall image like a warm editorial film scan.
- Text/detail layer: add tiny Korean editorial markings such as “SEOUL · 2026.05”, “자연광 포트레이트”, “오늘의 무드”, “#산책기록”, and a small handwritten-style sticker reading “good light”.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard Medium, Noto Sans KR SemiBold, or a small handwritten sticker style for editorial labels; keep text compact, believable, and integrated like a Korean lifestyle magazine portrait card.
- Include subtle on-image profile-card text: a date/location label like “서울 성수동 · 2026.05.01”, a small caption like “햇살이 머문 오후”, and one tiny tag like “#오늘의빛”.
- Color palette: soft cream, coral blush, muted beige, warm brown, leaf green, and muted sky blue; preserve the look of {필름·톤} with natural saturation and creamy highlight roll-off.
- Decorative details: optional thin off-white film-print edge, small corner registration marks, tiny star/dot stickers, or a translucent caption strip, all treated as realistic printed or social-card design accents.
- Wardrobe and material detail should feel real: visible knit, cotton, denim, linen, leather strap, jewelry glint, scarf weave, button detail, or bag strap texture when appropriate to {인물 묘사}.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: {카메라·렌즈} with a realistic 35mm film portrait rendering, shallow depth of field, gentle subject-background separation, and soft optical falloff.
- Lighting: {라이팅} with directional natural light from the side or rear side, plus soft ambient fill from the open environment; allow realistic sun flare, rim light, leaf-filtered highlights, or window-reflected glow when suitable.
- Color grade: {필름·톤} with creamy highlights, muted coral skin warmth, restrained greens, warm beige shadows, and a matte film scan finish.
- Realism cues: natural skin pores, tiny blemishes, individual hair strands, fabric seams, small environmental reflections, film grain, subtle lens halation, and imperfect candid timing.

[6. MOOD]
Classic 35mm film editorial portrait — like a subtle Kinfolk x Vogue Korea street portrait blend, with calm candid energy, real outdoor atmosphere, and polished magazine realism. The image should feel personal, lived-in, and shareable, like a Korean profile portrait taken during a beautiful walk in natural light.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: any on-image Korean must be short and clean, such as “자연광 포트레이트”, “햇살이 머문 오후”, “서울 성수동 · 2026.05.01”, “#오늘의빛”, or “산책 기록”.
- Maintain realistic human anatomy and proportions, with natural facial symmetry, believable hair detail, accurate fingers if hands are visible, and lifelike clothing interaction with the body.
- Preserve the requested candid outdoor portrait feel with real location context, natural daylight, editorial card details, and a polished 35mm film mood.
- Keep the subject’s face readable for social profile use while still including enough environment, labels, and small decorative details to make the image feel content-rich and realistic.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness
